projects.name: langchain-nextjs-template
projects.tagline: Next.js routes for LangChain.js chat, agents, structured output and RAG
projects.summary: Five Next.js API routes that each show one LangChain.js pattern: plain chat, Zod structured output, a prebuilt LangGraph.js agent with Tavily search, and RAG as a chain and as an agent over a Supabase pgvector table. Tokens stream to the client through the AI SDK, routes run on Edge functions, and there is no auth or persistence beyond the vector table. For developers learning LangChain.js who want runnable routes to copy.
strengths: Each pattern is one route file you can lift into your own app
Hosted demo on Vercel
Mock-backed integration tests run without API keys or a live database
Supabase adapter reuses the documents table and match_documents function; no migration
weaknesses: No auth and no chat history persistence
OpenAI only out of the box; other providers need code changes
Re-ingesting the same text duplicates vectors; no dedupe
Agent and search examples need a Tavily key

projects.name: chatbot
projects.tagline: Next.js chat template with Auth.js, Postgres history and AI Gateway models
projects.summary: Clone it and you get a Next.js App Router chat app on the AI SDK with Auth.js login, chat history in Neon Postgres through Drizzle migrations, file uploads to Vercel Blob and a streaming UI on shadcn/ui. Models route through Vercel AI Gateway; Mistral, Moonshot, DeepSeek, OpenAI and xAI are preconfigured in lib/ai/models.ts. For teams starting a chat product on Vercel who want auth and persistence wired on day one.
strengths: Auth.js, Postgres chat history and Drizzle migrations wired out of the box
Live demo plus a separate docs site
Per-model provider routing in lib/ai/models.ts; swapping vendors is a small edit
Tests included
weaknesses: Defaults to Vercel services: AI Gateway, Neon Postgres, Vercel Blob
Off Vercel you must set AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY and replace Blob storage
No Docker or compose files

projects.name: chat
projects.tagline: Nuxt UI chat template with GitHub login, SQLite history and AI Gateway
projects.summary: A Nuxt app on Nuxt UI and the AI SDK: streaming replies with reasoning, three models through Vercel AI Gateway (Claude Haiku 4.5, Gemini 3 Flash, GPT-5 Nano), provider web search, dictation over WebSocket, and chart and weather tool calls. GitHub OAuth, chat history in SQLite or Turso through Drizzle, and NuxtHub Blob uploads are included. For Vue and Nuxt teams who want a complete chat UI with persistence.
strengths: Auth, Drizzle migrations and uploads wired; local dev needs no external database
Blob storage swaps between local disk, Vercel Blob, Cloudflare R2 and S3
Live demo and a one-command scaffold (npm create nuxt -t ui/chat)
Committed within the last day
weaknesses: Models and dictation go through Vercel AI Gateway; direct keys need code changes
Auth is GitHub OAuth only
No tests listed
Production database path assumes Turso

projects.name: claude-quickstarts
projects.tagline: Independent Claude API starter projects, one folder per pattern
projects.summary: Independent Claude API starter projects in one repo, not one app: a customer support agent with a knowledge base, a financial data analyst with charts, computer-use and Playwright browser-use demos, a two-agent coding loop on the Agent SDK, and Managed Agents examples for Slack, Linear, Sentry, MCP and CopilotKit AG-UI. Mixed Next.js and Python, each folder with its own setup. For developers copying out one pattern.
strengths: Covers computer use, browser use, Agent SDK and Managed Agents in one checkout
Each quickstart is self-contained with its own README and setup
Tracks current toolset shapes (computer_toolset_20260801, browser_toolset_20260801)
Ships a CLAUDE.md for agent-driven edits
weaknesses: Not a single forkable app; you extract one subfolder
No auth, billing or database at the root; only what each sample needs
Anthropic-only; no provider abstraction
No root .env.example or Docker files

projects.name: gemini-chatbot
projects.tagline: Next.js chatbot template defaulting to Gemini with NextAuth and Postgres
projects.summary: An earlier cut of the Vercel chatbot template pinned to Google Gemini: Next.js App Router, AI SDK streaming with tool calls, NextAuth.js login, chat history in Vercel Postgres through Drizzle, and file storage on Vercel Blob. The default model is gemini-1.5-pro; the AI SDK lets you switch to OpenAI, Anthropic or Cohere. For teams on Google models who want the Vercel chat stack.

Two env vars to deploy: AUTH_SECRET and GOOGLE_GENERATIVE_AI_API_KEY
Deployed demo at gemini.vercel.ai

Tied to Vercel Postgres and Blob; self-hosting means swapping both
No tests, no Docker

projects.name: twitterbio
projects.tagline: Single-form Next.js text generator streaming from Together AI
projects.summary: A one-page Next.js app: a form builds a prompt, sends it to Together AI and streams the reply back, with two open models wired (Qwen 3.5 9B with thinking off, GPT OSS 20B with a reasoning indicator). Nothing else is included: no auth, no database, no tests. For developers who want the smallest prompt-to-text starter to grow from.
strengths: One env var (TOGETHER_API_KEY) and it runs
Shows streaming for both a direct model and a reasoning model
Deployed live example at twitterbio.io
weaknesses: No auth, database, rate limiting or tests
Tied to Together AI; no provider layer
Single feature; most of a product is still to build

projects.name: ai-chat

For Laravel teams who want a chat base in their own stack.

Auth, chat sharing and SSE streaming already wired
Adding a provider or model is one enum case
Tests included

No Docker files
PHP 8.3+ and Composer required

projects.name: zola

projects.summary: A Next.js chat interface on the AI SDK that talks to OpenAI, Mistral, Anthropic, Gemini and local Ollama models, with bring-your-own-key through OpenRouter. Supabase handles auth and file storage once you follow INSTALL.md, a docker-compose file pairs it with Ollama, and Zola is a running product (zola.chat) you fork rather than a scaffold. For builders who want a finished multi-model chat UI to brand.
strengths: Runs with one key or with local Ollama only; no database required for that path
docker-compose.ollama.yml included; auto-detects local Ollama models
Hosted instance at zola.chat shows the exact UI you get

No tests listed

For teams writing a custom ChatKit server who need a reference per feature.

Each demo starts with one command on its own port (5170 to 5173)
Attachment upload and dictation are implemented end to end

Python backend plus Node frontend; needs uv and npm

projects.name: openai-chatkit-starter-app

projects.summary: Two reference apps for embedding OpenAI ChatKit: one self-hosted integration where you run the ChatKit backend yourself, and one managed integration that connects the widget to a hosted Agent Builder workflow. The root README is a two-line index, setup lives in each subfolder, and seed data lists Next.js plus Python. For teams committed to ChatKit who want the smallest working wiring.

Shows self-hosted and managed hosting modes side by side
weaknesses: Root README has no setup, env or port details

projects.name: openai-responses-starter-app
projects.tagline: Next.js chat on the OpenAI Responses API with hosted tools
projects.summary: A Next.js chat UI wired to the OpenAI Responses API with streaming, multi-turn state, function calling and the hosted tools: web search, file search over a vector store you create from the UI, and code interpreter. For developers building an assistant on OpenAI hosted tooling.

Working OAuth example for OpenAI first-party connectors (Calendar, Gmail)
Custom functions live in config/functions.ts; clear extension point

projects.name: langgraph-fullstack-python

Opens directly in LangGraph Studio

No auth
Default model string claude-3-5-sonnet-20240620 is dated
Server-rendered FastHTML UI; limited for rich client-side features

projects.name: azure-search-openai-demo
projects.tagline: Azure RAG chat reference on AI Search and Azure OpenAI

For teams already on Azure.

Evaluation, safety evaluation, monitoring and productionizing guides in docs/
Multimodal, speech and agentic retrieval are switchable features
Commits within the last week; tests included

Provisions paid services by default (AI Search, Document Intelligence); run azd down
Azure OpenAI only; no other provider path
README itself says not production-ready without extra security work

projects.name: rag-postgres-openai-python
projects.tagline: RAG over Postgres table rows with hybrid search and SQL filters
projects.summary: A FastAPI backend and React frontend that answer chat questions about rows in a PostgreSQL table. Retrieval is hybrid (pgvector similarity plus full-text search fused with RRF), an OpenAI function call turns phrases like cheaper than 30 dollars into WHERE clauses, and it runs against Azure OpenAI, OpenAI.com or Ollama; azd deploys it to Container Apps with managed identity. For teams whose knowledge is structured rows, not documents.
strengths: Hybrid vector plus full-text search with RRF is implemented in SQL, not a vendor service
Provider switch by env var: Azure OpenAI, OpenAI.com or Ollama
Evaluation, safety evaluation and load-testing docs included
Tests included; dev container and Codespaces configs
weaknesses: Deploy path is Azure-only (azd, Container Apps, Flexible Server)
Local run expects Postgres 14+ with pgvector installed yourself
Sample schema is one products table; multi-table questions need new code
No auth in the app itself

projects.name: llm-app
projects.tagline: Pathway RAG pipeline templates that re-index live data sources
projects.summary: Eight Dockerized Python pipelines on the Pathway framework: question-answering RAG, a live document indexer, multimodal RAG with GPT-4o, unstructured-to-SQL, adaptive RAG, a private Mistral plus Ollama variant, slide search and video RAG. Each watches a source (file system, Google Drive, SharePoint, S3, Kafka, Postgres), keeps an in-memory vector and full-text index current and serves an HTTP API. For teams whose documents change constantly.
strengths: No separate vector DB, cache or API framework; indexing is in-process (usearch, Tantivy)
Connectors for file system, Google Drive, SharePoint, S3, Kafka and Postgres with live sync
Private variant runs fully local with Mistral and Ollama
Docker images and tests included
weaknesses: Pathway is the real dependency; its Rust engine is opaque to most Python teams
Pipelines are backends; the UI is an optional Streamlit demo
Root README has no setup; each template README is required reading
Index lives in memory; sizing for millions of pages is on you

projects.name: chat-langchain
projects.tagline: LangChain docs assistant as a Managed Deep Agent with Next.js UI

Supabase token plus guest identity handled in identity.py
Frontend proxies LangSmith feedback so the API key never reaches the browser
Tests included
weaknesses: Tied to Managed Deep Agents (mda CLI) for identity, ingress and state
Needs a Pylon account and knowledge base ID to run as written
Docs retrieval depends on a managed MCP connector, not your own index
Product-specific: you replace the LangChain docs with your own corpus

projects.name: chat-with-your-data-solution-accelerator

Admin UI for ingesting documents and editing prompts without code changes
Two selectable orchestrators: Agent Framework or LangGraph

projects.name: azure-search-openai-javascript

projects.summary: The Node.js counterpart of the Azure RAG sample: a search API, an indexer service and a web app that answer chat and Q&A questions over your documents with citations, using Azure AI Search and Azure OpenAI through LangChain.js. azd up provisions Container Apps for the backend and a Static Web App for the frontend, and the search API speaks the AI chat HTTP protocol so the Python backend can replace it. projects.name: SupabaseAuthWithSSR

projects.summary: A Next.js 16 app on AI SDK v7 and Claude with complete Supabase SSR auth (signup, magic links, password reset, RLS on every table) and eight tools: PDF RAG (Mistral OCR, Voyage embeddings, hybrid RRF search in pgvector), Exa web search, versioned artifacts, memory, conversation search, sandboxed visualizations, PDF export and image generation. Per-step token and cache usage stored on messages; user and admin cost dashboards
Two-tier Anthropic prompt caching with a hit-rate readout

projects.name: llm-answer-engine
projects.tagline: Perplexity-style Next.js answer engine over Brave search results
projects.summary: A Next.js app that takes a question, pulls results from Brave Search and Serper, scrapes the top pages with Cheerio, chunks and embeds them with OpenAI embeddings, and streams an answer from Groq (Mixtral by default) with sources, images and follow-ups. docker compose and a standalone Express API variant included
Optional rate limiting and semantic cache via Upstash
weaknesses: Four API keys to start (OpenAI, Groq, Brave, Serper)

projects.name: nextjs-openai-doc-search
projects.tagline: Build-time embeddings of your MDX docs into Supabase pgvector
projects.summary: A Next.js starter that chunks the .mdx files in pages/ at build time, embeds each section with OpenAI and stores vectors in Supabase pgvector, skipping files whose checksum has not changed. At runtime an Edge function embeds the question, runs a similarity search and streams a completion with the matched sections in the prompt; the schema ships as a Supabase migration. For teams adding chat search to a Next.js docs site.
strengths: Checksum table avoids re-embedding unchanged files on every build
pgvector schema is a checked-in Supabase migration
One secret (OPENAI_KEY) when deployed with the Vercel Supabase integration
weaknesses: Uses the legacy OpenAI text completion endpoint; expect to port it
Only .mdx in pages/ is indexed; other sources need code
No auth, no conversation history, no tests
Design dates from 2023; last commit 2026-05

projects.name: openai-support-agent-demo

Includes an event-emitting websocket client, an audio layer and a tool-call example rendering Vega charts. For developers starting a browser client on Gemini Live; the API key sits in the frontend .env, so add a proxy before shipping.
strengths: Websocket client, audio in/out and log view ready to reuse
Mic, webcam and screen capture wired as model input
Tool-call example with Google Search grounding and Vega rendering
weaknesses: Gemini API key is read from the frontend .env; no server proxy
Built on Create React App, which is no longer maintained
Labeled an experiment, not an official Google product
Gemini only; last commit 2025-10

projects.name: mcp-typescript-template
projects.tagline: TypeScript template for remote MCP servers using Express and Effect
projects.summary: A degit-able starter for a stateless remote MCP server built on the MCP TypeScript SDK, Express and Vite. It ships two example tools (echo and elicit_echo) with typed input and output schemas via Effect, plus an example Agent Skill published through the MCP Skills extension. Includes tests, ESLint, Prettier, a Dockerfile and a compose file with a health check.
strengths: Stateless HTTP transport per the MCP 2026-07-28 spec, with SDK fallback for older clients
Effect Schema adapted to MCP Standard Schema; tools declare outputSchema and structuredContent
Integration tests with in-memory client/server plus HTTP boundary tests
Example elicitation tool and a bundled skill served via skills/list and skills/get
weaknesses: Tool code is written in Effect style, bridged to the SDK with runMcpEffect
Only toy tools (echo, elicit_echo); no auth or persistence example
Needs TypeScript 7 plus a TypeScript 6 alias for typescript-eslint
Targets newer MCP spec revisions; Skills extension needs client support

projects.name: mcp-use
projects.tagline: TypeScript framework for building MCP servers with React Views and an Inspector
projects.summary: mcp-use is a TypeScript v2 framework, built on the official MCP TypeScript SDK, for writing MCP servers with Zod-typed tools. It binds React Views to tools so they render as interactive apps in hosts such as ChatGPT and Claude. It ships a dev Inspector, a headless client CLI, a View screenshot command, tunneling, and a deploy command targeting Manufact.
strengths: Zod schemas flow from tool input and output into React View props
Inspector served at /mcp/inspector in dev; headless CLI can call tools and screenshot Views
Built-in tunnel (mcp-use dev --tunnel) for testing in ChatGPT and Claude before deploy
MIT licensed, with a self-hosting guide alongside the hosted option
weaknesses: v2 is a breaking change from v1; a migration guide is needed
Benchmark and comparison figures are the project's own, not independent
One-command npm run deploy targets the vendor's Manufact platform
Example apps live in separate repos, not in the main package

projects.name: template-mcp-server
projects.tagline: Python FastMCP server template with OAuth, OpenShift manifests and CI
projects.summary: Python 3.12+ package on FastMCP and FastAPI with HTTP, SSE and streamable-HTTP transports on port 5001, a /health endpoint, Pydantic settings, structlog JSON logs, optional SSL and OAuth with PostgreSQL token storage. Ships three example tools, a UBI Containerfile, compose.yaml, OpenShift manifests, CI for tests, lint, security and releases. For teams standardizing MCP servers on Red Hat tooling.
strengths: HTTP, SSE and streamable-HTTP transports selectable by env var
OAuth with PostgreSQL token storage and a documented auth guide
Containerfile, compose.yaml and OpenShift manifests included
CI runs tests, linting, security scans and releases
weaknesses: ENABLE_AUTH defaults differ between .env.example and code
Rename checklist touches nine files after cloning
OAuth mode needs PostgreSQL
Red Hat UBI base image and OpenShift focus may not fit other platforms

projects.name: mcp-for-next.js
projects.tagline: Stateless MCP server route for a Next.js App Router app
projects.summary: Next.js App Router project where app/mcp/route.ts hosts a stateless MCP server through mcp-handler 2 and the MCP TypeScript SDK v2, serving the 2026-07-28 protocol natively with a compatibility layer for 2025-era Streamable HTTP clients. Includes a sample client script that lists tools and calls echo. For teams adding an MCP endpoint to an existing Next.js app on Vercel; no auth is wired.
strengths: Stateless Streamable HTTP; no Redis or session store required
Current 2026-07-28 protocol plus 2025 Streamable HTTP compatibility
Sample client script for smoke-testing the endpoint
weaknesses: No auth; remote MCP clients will need OAuth added
Deprecated HTTP+SSE transport is not supported
Only an echo tool; the README is a few lines
No tests or Docker

projects.name: openai-apps-sdk-examples
projects.tagline: Example MCP servers and widgets for ChatGPT apps on the Apps SDK
projects.summary: pnpm workspace with React widget sources, a Vite build that emits hashed HTML/JS/CSS bundles served on port 4444, and paired MCP servers in Node and Python (Pizzaz, kitchen-sink-lite, solar system, shopping cart, an OAuth-gated example). Widgets use the window.openai host API and _meta.ui.resourceUri to render inside ChatGPT. For developers building ChatGPT apps; test via developer mode and an ngrok tunnel.
strengths: Node and Python MCP servers for the same widgets
kitchen-sink-lite covers the full window.openai host API surface
Shopping-cart example shows widgetSessionId state across tool calls
Authenticated server demonstrates OAuth-gated tools
weaknesses: Examples only; no persistence or deploy config beyond BASE_URL
Requires ChatGPT developer mode and a public tunnel to test
Chrome 142+ needs a flag change to render widgets locally
Maintainers may not review all PRs

projects.name: mcp-forge
projects.tagline: Go MCP server template with OAuth discovery and JWT validation
projects.summary: Go 1.24+ template on mcp-go that runs as an HTTP or stdio MCP server from a YAML config, with RFC 8414 and 9728 OAuth discovery endpoints and JWT validation either delegated to a proxy like Istio or done locally via JWKS and CEL claim rules. Ships a Dockerfile, Helm chart, GitHub Actions and example configs for Claude Web, OpenAI and local clients through mcp-remote. You add tools under internal/tools.
strengths: OAuth discovery endpoints and JWT middleware for remote clients like Claude Web
Helm chart, Dockerfile and CI workflows included
Same binary serves HTTP or stdio by swapping the YAML config
Access logs can redact or drop fields
weaknesses: Needs an external OIDC provider with dynamic client registration (Keycloak suggested)
Author recommends a proxy for JWT validation and a hashring router for sessions
Last commit 2026-01; no tests mentioned in the README

projects.name: ant-design-pro
projects.tagline: React admin dashboard template built on Ant Design 6 and Umi Max
projects.summary: Ant Design Pro is a React 19 and TypeScript boilerplate for enterprise back-office apps, built on Umi Max 4 and antd 6. It ships ready-made pages for dashboards, forms, lists, profiles, account settings, login and error screens, plus i18n, mock data and unit and e2e tests. A built-in AI chatbot page uses Ant Design X, and an `npm run simple` script strips the template down to a minimal version.
strengths: Includes dashboard, form, list, profile, account and result page templates
Built-in i18n, mock development setup, and unit and e2e tests
Ships Claude Code skills for upgrading the template and querying antd APIs
TypeScript with Tailwind CSS v4 and antd-style theming
weaknesses: AI support is a single chatbot page; no model backend is described
`npm run simple` permanently deletes files and cannot be undone
Tied to the Umi Max and antd stack; no other frameworks
No Docker or compose setup mentioned in the README

projects.name: next-js-boilerplate
projects.tagline: Next.js 16 starter with Clerk auth, Drizzle ORM, Tailwind 4 and tooling
projects.summary: A clone-and-edit Next.js App Router starter in TypeScript with Tailwind CSS 4, Clerk authentication, and Drizzle ORM on PostgreSQL (PGlite locally, Neon suggested for production). It also wires in next-intl i18n, Vitest, Playwright, Storybook, Sentry, LogTape and Arcjet. It includes no AI features beyond agent instruction files and CodeRabbit review.
strengths: Runs locally with embedded PGlite database, no Docker or extra setup
Broad dev tooling preconfigured: Vitest, Playwright, Storybook, Commitlint, Knip, i18n-check
Drizzle ORM supports PostgreSQL, SQLite and MySQL, with migration scripts
Includes instruction files for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode and Copilot
weaknesses: Auth depends on a hosted Clerk account and API keys
No billing; Stripe, teams, RBAC and shadcn UI are in the paid Pro kit
No built-in AI features such as chat or model calls
Many sponsor-linked services (Sentry, Arcjet, Crowdin, Better Stack) to configure or strip out

projects.name: react-starter-kit
projects.tagline: Full-stack SaaS monorepo template on React 19, tRPC and Cloudflare Workers
projects.summary: A GitHub template for SaaS apps split into three Cloudflare Workers (Astro marketing site, React 19 SPA, Hono and tRPC API) joined by service bindings. Better Auth handles email OTP, passkeys, Google OAuth and organizations, with optional Stripe subscriptions. Drizzle ORM talks to Neon PostgreSQL through Hyperdrive, provisioned with Terraform.
strengths: Auth, organizations and Stripe billing are already wired in
One TypeScript type contract from Drizzle schema through tRPC to the React UI
Separate migrate and deploy scripts for staging and production, same script in CI
A merge-seed skill pulls upstream template changes into your project
weaknesses: Tied to Cloudflare Workers, Neon PostgreSQL and Hyperdrive; no alternative runtime documented
Requires Bun 1.4+ instead of Node.js and npm
README describes no built-in AI features; they must be added yourself
Email OTP sign-in needs a verified Resend domain for users other than you

projects.name: velobase-harness
projects.tagline: Next.js AI SaaS base with credits, usage billing, workers and anti-abuse
projects.summary: A Next.js 15 and tRPC application with Prisma on Postgres and BullMQ on Redis that already has accounts, subscriptions, a credit ledger, Stripe and NowPayments, entitlement checks, affiliate accounting, server-side attribution, anti-abuse controls (rate limits, Turnstile, disposable-email checks), lifecycle email, an admin area and a multi-provider AI chat module. One command starts Postgres and Redis in Docker. For builders turning an AI prototype into a paid product.
strengths: Credit ledger, usage metering and entitlements are built in, not left to you
Anti-abuse for free credits: rate limits, Turnstile, disposable-email checks, clawbacks
Runs as one process or split web, worker and API by SERVICE_MODE
Docker compose, English and Chinese docs, AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md
weaknesses: No unit-test script; only service-mode smoke tests
Large surface area; the framework guide asks for domain design before coding
Payments are Stripe and NowPayments; others need adapters
Seed shows 607 stars; young project

projects.name: hackathon-starter
projects.tagline: Node.js and Express boilerplate with auth, API examples and AI samples
projects.summary: Hackathon Starter is an Express and MongoDB web app template with local, passkey and OAuth 2.0 sign-in, account management, 2FA, a contact form and file upload. It ships examples for third-party APIs such as Stripe, Twilio and Google Maps, plus AI samples: a ReAct agent with tool calling and MongoDB session persistence, and RAG with embedding caching. Views are server-rendered Pug with Bootstrap 5.3 and Sass.
strengths: Local, passkey and eight OAuth 2.0 providers already wired up
Account flows included: email verification, password reset, 2FA, account deletion
Many API integration examples: Stripe, Twilio, Google Drive, Maps, Steam
Live demo and a production checklist (PROD_CHECKLIST.md)
weaknesses: Requires MongoDB; no other database option is documented
No Dockerfile or compose file detected
AI examples are a small part of a general web boilerplate
Most integrations need separate API keys and OAuth app setup

projects.name: gin-vue-admin
projects.tagline: Go and Vue 3 admin platform with RBAC and a CRUD code generator
projects.summary: Full-stack admin framework with a Gin and GORM backend and a Vue 3 and Element Plus frontend. The README also advertises an MCP integration for AI editors that drives code generation.
strengths: JWT plus Casbin role, menu and API permissions built in
Code generator produces backend and frontend CRUD from a template
Swagger docs via swag; Redis-backed multi-login limit
File upload to Qiniu, Aliyun and Tencent Cloud included

No billing or tenancy described; some features need a paid license
No free technical support; paid support only
README is mainly in Chinese; no Docker setup detected

projects.name: open-saas

For teams that accept Wasp for a complete SaaS base.
strengths: Three payment providers and three email providers are switchable
Playwright e2e tests, admin dashboard and docs site included
One-command deploy to Railway or Fly
Live demo at opensaas.sh and a dedicated docs site
weaknesses: Wasp is the framework; its config DSL and release cadence become your dependency
AI part is one OpenAI example app; no usage metering or credits
Pulling template updates after forking is a documented manual process
No Docker files

projects.name: AI-Fullstack-SaaS-Boilerplate
projects.tagline: Fastify, tRPC and React SaaS base with Better Auth and SSE chat
projects.summary: A pnpm monorepo: a Fastify server with tRPC routers on port 2022, Drizzle over Postgres, Better Auth with user impersonation, and a Vite React 19 client with React Router that ships as static files. Better Auth with admin impersonation already wired
Playwright e2e tests and a seed script included
Hosted demo on Render
weaknesses: No billing, no usage metering; AI is a single SSE chat
OpenAI only
Static SPA; README notes it is not SEO-friendly
Demo on a free Render tier spins down; expect 50 second cold starts

projects.name: next-ai-starter

agent-helpers workflow and Cursor commands are ready for AI-assisted development

No tests or Docker

projects.name: lastsaas
projects.tagline: Go multi-tenant SaaS kit with Stripe billing and an MCP admin server
projects.summary: A Go backend with a React frontend served from the same binary: multi-tenant accounts with owner, admin and user roles, JWT with refresh rotation, OAuth, magic links and TOTP, Stripe subscriptions, per-seat pricing, trials and credit bundles, white-label branding, scoped API keys, 19 signed outgoing webhooks, analytics and health monitoring on MongoDB. Outgoing webhooks with HMAC signing and delivery tracking; scoped API keys

CI with coverage reporting; 14 MB Alpine image; Fly.io deploy

MongoDB, not Postgres; migrations and queries are Mongo-specific
One author; seed shows 173 stars

projects.name: saas-starter
projects.tagline: Next.js SaaS template with Stripe billing, email/password auth and team dashboard

README recommends Claude Code with Opus 5.5; other agents are only listed as supported
Requires Node.js 24+
Output is Next.js only; no other target framework is mentioned

projects.name: jeecgboot

Row, column and form-field level data permissions plus multi-tenant SaaS support

Mac and Windows builds available

Separate Code Interpreter and Desktop SDKs cover code execution and computer use
Self-hosting supported on AWS, GCP, Azure and generic Linux via Terraform

Self-hosted runtime lives in a separate repo, e2b-dev/runtime

Provides sandboxes only; agent logic and LLM integration are left to you

Workflows export to TypeScript with the use workflow directive
Execution history and per-node logs stored in Postgres
Better Auth and Drizzle already wired

Relative cost indicators and reasoning output per model
ReactFlow, TipTap, shadcn/ui and Kibo UI already composed

No auth or multi-user support
Vercel Blob required for media; Vercel-centric

Component versions pinned in manifest.json for reproducible releases
Custom apps can replace the defaults through app-definition.json
MIT license; docs cover network-isolated deployment

Default UI, orchestrator and ingestion code live in three separate repositories

Prerequisites and configuration are only in external docs, not the README

projects.name: fullstack-solution-template-for-agentcore

Agent patterns for both Strands and LangGraph under patterns/
Frontend uses React, Vite, Tailwind and shadcn components
Extensive docs for memory, streaming, sessions, observability and swapping out Cognito

README calls it a proof-of-value, not production-ready
Baseline is only a simple chat agent with two tools
No tagged releases

projects.name: azurechat

Chat over files, personas and extensions documented in docs/
Private endpoints and ESLZ-compliant deployment supported
azd template plus GitHub Actions deploy path

Identity provider setup is mandatory before first use
Contributions require a Microsoft CLA
README defers most detail to docs/; no tests mentioned

projects.name: openai-chat-app-quickstart

Bicep provisions the full Container Apps stack
Codespaces and Dev Container configs included
IaC security scan GitHub Action included

No user auth; sibling repos add Entra ID
Frontend is minimal HTML/JS, not a component framework
Azure Container Registry has a fixed daily cost

projects.name: serverless-rag-demo

strengths: Hybrid BM25 + KNN search with per-user document isolation
Demo OCU mode scales to zero, so idle cost is listed as $0
Full infrastructure as Python CDK stacks, with Cognito auth and CloudFront hosting
MIT-0 license with no attribution requirement
weaknesses: AWS only: Bedrock, AgentCore, OpenSearch Serverless and Cognito are all required
Models fixed to Claude Sonnet/Opus 4.6 and Titan Embed V2; no other providers listed
Supported in six regions only; us-west-1 and ap-southeast-1 excluded
No release tags, and tests cover CDK unit checks only

projects.name: get-started-with-ai-agents

Tracing via Application Insights and Azure Monitor included
Pytest agent evaluation and AI Red Teaming scans included
Managed Identity used for deployment and local development
weaknesses: Requires an Azure subscription and Foundry model quota; no non-Azure path
README warns the code is a showcase, not production-ready without extra security
Costs are usage-based and the README gives no estimate
Deployment takes 7–15 minutes with `azd up`; teardown up to 20

projects.name: openai-chat-vision-quickstart

Managed identity by default, so no API key in app config
Can point at a local OpenAI-compatible endpoint (Ollama doc) for development
Speech input/output uses free built-in browser APIs
weaknesses: Deploying needs Azure subscription and role-assignment write permissions
Basic HTML/JS frontend with no auth or multi-user features
Container Registry has a fixed daily cost even when idle
Local dev server still needs Azure credentials or a compatible endpoint

projects.name: agent-service-toolkit

docker compose watch runs Postgres, API and Streamlit with live reload
Unit and integration tests plus smoke tests for Postgres, Mongo, AG-UI and Langfuse
Hosted demo on Streamlit Cloud

Streamlit client is a demo UI, not a product frontend
Content moderation needs a Groq API key
Tests only run outside Docker

projects.name: full-stack-ai-agent-template

strengths: Wizard and presets pick framework, vector store, auth and billing per project
Template upgrades merge into generated projects on a branch
Chat UI renders tool calls, plans, subagents, charts and Python execution
100% coverage badge and CI on the generator

Seeds admin@example.com with a fixed password; rotate before exposing
Optional services (Milvus, Redis, Celery) raise the local footprint
Windows needs GNU Make or WSL2

README leads with a sponsor pitch for Atlas Cloud
Needs the pgvector extension and an OpenAI key for memory
Not a GitHub template; clone and strip

strengths: LiteLLM naming lets you switch between Ollama and cloud models by env
Promptfoo and Ragas evaluation wired into the template
CPU and CUDA docker compose variants
CI tests the app against local Ollama models
weaknesses: NiceGUI frontend is unusual for product UIs
No auth, database or persistence described
Ubuntu 22.04 or macOS only per prerequisites
CUDA path installs PyTorch; heavier install

projects.name: nodejs-api-boilerplate
projects.tagline: Express TypeScript CRUD API template with an LLM module generator
projects.summary: Express and TypeScript REST API with vertical-slice modules, Zod validation, InversifyJS DI, Knex transactions, ioredis caching, winston trace IDs, node-cron, S3 uploads and Supertest e2e tests, run via docker compose on port 8080. strengths: Codegen loop compiles and runs e2e tests until they pass
Supports OpenAI, Anthropic, DeepSeek and OpenRouter keys for generation
JWT auth routes, Redis cache and cron already in the base API
Tests run in Docker or against local SQLite
weaknesses: AI is a dev-time generator; the API itself has no AI features
Node badge pins v14 to v20; check against current LTS
Generated code still needs manual review and integration

projects.name: genai-api

Requests route through Cloudflare AI Gateway for caching and logs
Multimodal input via data-URL images
Biome lint and Snyk badge

Plain-text responses, no streaming
No tests mentioned; last commit 2026-04
Needs a Cloudflare account and AI Gateway id

strengths: Server proxy keeps API keys off the device and leaves room for auth
Streaming responses from all five LLM providers
Gemini image generation wired on the server
Five themes with a documented pattern for adding more

No auth implemented; the proxy is where you add it
No persistence of chats described

Auth session and storage shared between popup, content and options pages
CI publishing to Chrome Web Store and Firefox Add-ons
Plasmo variant maintained on a separate branch

Firefox builds target MV2 and load only in temporary mode
Requires Bun

projects.name: claw-code
projects.tagline: Rust CLI coding agent harness using Anthropic and OpenAI-compatible APIs

It runs one-shot prompts or interactive sessions using an API key, and the docs cover local OpenAI-compatible servers such as Ollama, llama.cpp and vLLM. The README describes the repo as an agent-managed exhibit, not the production project, and points to LazyCodex and Gajae-Code for real work.
strengths: `claw doctor` checks API key, model access and tool configuration after build
Docs cover local OpenAI-compatible providers: Ollama, llama.cpp, vLLM
Build steps documented for macOS, Linux and Windows PowerShell
MIT license; workspace test suite and deterministic mock-service parity harness
weaknesses: README says it is not the serious production project and points elsewhere
Build-from-source only; `cargo install claw-code` installs a deprecated stub
Requires an API key; Claude subscription login is not supported
No ACP/Zed daemon yet; `claw acp serve` only returns status

projects.name: opencode
projects.tagline: Terminal coding agent with build and plan modes, plus a desktop app
projects.summary: OpenCode is an AI coding agent that runs in the terminal and as a beta desktop app for macOS, Windows and Linux. It ships a full-access build agent, a read-only plan agent that asks before running bash commands, and a general subagent invoked with @general. It installs through a curl script, npm, Homebrew, Scoop, Chocolatey, pacman, mise or nix.
strengths: Read-only plan agent denies file edits by default and asks before bash commands
Many install paths: curl script, npm, brew, scoop, choco, pacman, mise, nix
Switch between build and plan agents with the Tab key
MIT licensed, with desktop installers for macOS, Windows and Linux
weaknesses: README does not list supported model providers or formats
Desktop app is marked BETA
README gives no hardware requirements; configuration is only in external docs
Primary install command pipes a curl script into bash

projects.name: pi
projects.tagline: Terminal coding agent with extensions, skills, and an SDK
projects.summary: Pi is a TypeScript coding agent CLI that runs in your project directory and connects to LLM providers through a login or API key. It is customized with extensions, skills, prompt templates and themes, shared as npm or git packages, and can be driven interactively, in print/JSON mode, over RPC, or through a TypeScript SDK. The monorepo also ships a multi-provider LLM API, an agent runtime and a terminal UI library.
strengths: Multiple interfaces: interactive CLI, print/JSON mode, RPC and a TypeScript SDK
Extensions, skills, prompt templates and themes ship as npm or git packages
Core libraries (pi-ai, pi-agent-core, pi-tui) are published as separate packages
Installer pins dependencies; Nix flake builds on Linux and macOS, ARM64 and x86-64
weaknesses: No built-in permission system; runs with the launching user's full permissions
Sub-agents and plan mode are intentionally omitted and must be added via packages
Requires Node.js 22.19 or newer
New contributors' issues and PRs are auto-closed by default

projects.name: oh-my-openagent
projects.tagline: Terminal coding agent that fans work out across many models
projects.summary: OmO is an `omo` command-line agent, built on senpi (a fork of pi), that reads a codebase, plans, and verifies each step. Typing `ulw` or `mass ulw` turns a job into a graph of parallel agents, each on a different model. Memory is kept as markdown files in a git repository, and `/login` covers Claude, ChatGPT, Kimi and GLM subscriptions.
strengths: Splits jobs across many agents and models in parallel with the `mass ulw` keyword
Memory stored as markdown in a git repo, so it is inspectable and versionable
Native binary installer with checksum verification, plus bun and npm packages
`omo setup` imports keys, MCP servers and skills from the OpenCode edition
weaknesses: License is SUL-1.0, not a standard OSI license; check terms before commercial use
Primary install path pipes a curl script into bash
README gives no RAM, token cost or hardware figures
Computer use is marked experimental

projects.name: orca
projects.tagline: Desktop app that runs CLI coding agents in parallel git worktrees
projects.summary: Orca is a desktop app for macOS, Windows and Linux that runs terminal-based coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode side by side, each in its own git worktree. It adds split terminals, an embedded browser with element picking, diff annotation, GitHub and Linear task views, SSH worktrees and a scriptable CLI. An iOS and Android companion app monitors agents and sends follow-ups.
strengths: Works with any CLI agent that runs in a terminal, with 30+ listed
Each agent gets an isolated git worktree, so parallel results can be compared
Supports remote worktrees over SSH with auto-reconnect and port forwarding
Orca CLI lets agents script worktree creation and browser actions
weaknesses: Does not include a model or agent; agent CLIs are installed and authenticated separately
Mobile app needs pairing with a running desktop host
Ships daily, so the README feature list lags behind the changelog
Collects anonymous usage telemetry, with an opt-out documented separately

projects.name: openinterpreter
projects.tagline: Terminal coding agent, a Codex fork tuned for low-cost models
projects.summary: Open Interpreter is a Rust fork of OpenAI's Codex that runs as a terminal coding agent. It can emulate other agent harnesses (claude-code, kimi-code, qwen-code, swe-agent and others) via /harness, so cheaper models are driven the way their providers recommend. It also runs as an ACP agent for editors and accepts the Codex exec protocol.
strengths: Switchable harness emulation: native, claude-code, kimi-code, qwen-code, swe-agent, minimal and more
Runs under native sandboxing on macOS, Linux and Windows
Works as an ACP agent via `interpreter acp`; Codex SDK users can swap the binary
Reads shared AGENTS.md and .agents/skills; supports MCP, hooks and permissions
weaknesses: Rewrite of the original Python project, which is now only a community fork
Built-in computer use relies on external tools: agent-browser and trycua
README gives no RAM, GPU or supported-model minimums
Install is a curl or PowerShell pipe-to-shell script; no Docker image

projects.name: goose
projects.tagline: Rust AI agent with desktop app, CLI and API, extended through MCP
projects.summary: goose is a general-purpose agent written in Rust that runs locally as a desktop app (macOS, Linux, Windows), a CLI, or an embeddable API. It connects to 15+ model providers, including Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Ollama, OpenRouter, Azure and Bedrock, and to 70+ extensions over the Model Context Protocol. It is hosted by the Agentic AI Foundation at the Linux Foundation.
strengths: Desktop app, CLI and API from one Rust codebase
15+ providers, including Ollama for local models
Can use existing Claude, ChatGPT or Gemini subscriptions via ACP
70+ MCP extensions; custom distros with preset providers and branding
weaknesses: README gives no RAM, GPU or port requirements
CLI install is a curl-pipe-to-bash script
Scope is general-purpose, not focused solely on coding
README has no demo and little detail on the API

projects.name: herdr
projects.tagline: Terminal multiplexer that keeps coding agents running and shows which are blocked
projects.summary: herdr is a Rust terminal multiplexer for running several coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and opencode. A background server keeps panes alive when the client detaches or SSH drops, and each pane is marked working, blocked or idle. Agents can also drive it through a CLI and socket API, and saved SSH machines appear in the same window.
strengths: Panes keep running in a background server after detach or SSH disconnect
Per-pane working, blocked or idle status across local and saved SSH machines
Agents can spawn panes and prompt each other via CLI and socket API
Single Rust binary; installs via curl script, Homebrew, mise or PowerShell
weaknesses: After a server or machine restart, processes are lost; only layout and supported agent sessions resume
Resume works only for supported agents; the README does not list which
Windows support is described as beta in the docs link
Install is a curl-pipe-to-shell script by default

projects.name: codewhale
projects.tagline: Terminal coding agent in Rust that works with hosted or local models
projects.summary: Codewhale is a coding agent that reads a project, edits files, runs commands and checks its own work from a terminal UI. It supports over 40 built-in provider routes plus any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, Ollama, vLLM and SGLang. The same local engine also serves headless `exec` runs, a local browser client, PR review and an HTTP runtime API.
strengths: Over 40 built-in provider routes plus OpenAI-compatible endpoints, Ollama, vLLM and SGLang
Plan, Work and Operate modes with Ask, Auto-Review and Full Access postures
`/undo`, `/restore` and `/receipts` recover changes and list files, commands and approvals
Headless `exec --auto` and `review --pr N` for scripts and CI
weaknesses: Usage telemetry is on by default and must be disabled with a config command
OS sandbox only on macOS (Seatbelt) and Linux with bubblewrap installed
Native desktop app is still being built; VS Code extension is community-maintained
Computer Use plugin must be reviewed and enabled manually before use

projects.name: deepseek-reasonix
projects.tagline: Coding agent for terminal, desktop, browser and VS Code, with DeepSeek preset
projects.summary: Reasonix is a Go coding agent that reads a project folder, edits files and runs commands and tests, showing each step. Models are set in reasonix.toml: a DeepSeek preset is built in and any OpenAI-compatible endpoint is a config entry. It ships as the Studio desktop app, a CLI/TUI, a local web UI (`reasonix web`), and a VS Code extension or ACP connection for other editors.
strengths: Any OpenAI-compatible provider is a config entry; DeepSeek ships as a preset
Permission levels and plan mode; forbid rules always apply
Rewind by conversation turn without touching git history
Static single binary (CGO_ENABLED=0), cross-compiled to six targets
weaknesses: Rewind covers only files its edit tools changed, not shell command effects
2.x line is still moving quickly; 1.x is the stable branch
VS Code extension requires installing the 1.x CLI separately
Model provider receives what the agent reads; no local model setup documented

projects.name: Archon
projects.tagline: YAML workflow engine that runs coding agents in isolated worktrees
projects.summary: Defines development processes (plan, implement, validate, review, PR) as YAML workflows and runs them through Claude Code, Codex or Pi, each run in its own git worktree. For teams standardizing how agents ship code.
strengths: Every run isolated in a git worktree; parallel fixes without conflicts
Bundled sdlc pack: ship, triage, investigate, plan, deliver, review, validate, upkeep
Adapters for web, CLI, Slack, Telegram, Discord and GitHub webhooks
Telemetry documented field by field; DO_NOT_TRACK=1 or CI=true disables it
weaknesses: Requires Claude Code (or Codex, Pi) installed separately; binaries need CLAUDE_BIN_PATH
Anonymous telemetry is on by default
x64 quick-install binaries require AVX2; older CPUs must build from source
Workflows from v0.11.1 and earlier no longer ship and must be copied manually

projects.name: gemini-cli

strengths: Free tier with Google login: 60 requests/min, 1,000 requests/day
1M token context window with Gemini 3 models
Headless mode emits plain text, JSON or newline-delimited stream-JSON
Auth via Google login, Gemini API key or Vertex AI
weaknesses: Only talks to Gemini models; no other providers listed in the README
Needs a Google account, API key or Vertex AI credentials; no local models
Preview and nightly channels may contain regressions
Free-tier quotas and terms are governed by Google, not the project

projects.name: OpenHands
projects.tagline: Web control center for running coding agents and scheduled automations
projects.summary: Agent Canvas is a web frontend that starts conversations with coding agents and switches between multiple Agent Server backends: local, Docker, VM or OpenHands Cloud. A paired Automation Server runs agents on a schedule or on webhook events, with Slack, GitHub and Linear integrations.
strengths: Works with OpenHands, Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Pi, OpenCode or any ACP agent
One UI switches between local, remote and cloud Agent Server backends
Scheduled and webhook-triggered automations with Slack, GitHub and Linear
Option to run each conversation in its own Docker container
weaknesses: Marked beta in the README
Non-Docker install gives the agent full filesystem access on the host
Needs Node.js 24+ and uv for npm or source installs
Automation backend is a separate repo; internet-facing setups need manual hardening

projects.name: cline
projects.tagline: Coding agent for VS Code, JetBrains, terminal and desktop

Works with Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, Bedrock, Vertex, OpenRouter, Ollama and LM Studio
Headless CLI accepts piped input and emits JSON for CI/CD scripts
Supports MCP servers, SDK plugins, cron-scheduled agents and multi-agent teams
weaknesses: JetBrains plugin source is not open-sourced

projects.summary: SWE-agent lets a language model such as GPT-4o or Claude Sonnet 4 autonomously use tools to fix issues in real GitHub repositories, find cybersecurity vulnerabilities, or run custom tasks.
