The README says the maintainers now focus on mini-swe-agent, which supersedes it, and recommend using that instead.
strengths: Single yaml file configures agent behavior; documentation site covers install, usage and batch mode
Batch mode for benchmarking on SWE-bench
Works with the model of your choice, e.g. GPT-4o or Claude Sonnet 4
MIT license, built by Princeton and Stanford researchers with an accompanying paper
weaknesses: README says mini-swe-agent supersedes it and recommends using that instead
Last release was 2025-05-22, well behind recent commits
EnIGMA cybersecurity mode requires SWE-agent 0.7 until it is updated for 1.0
Built for research and benchmarks rather than daily IDE-style assistance

projects.name: trae-agent
projects.tagline: Research-oriented CLI agent that runs software engineering tasks with LLM tools
projects.summary: Trae Agent is a Python CLI that takes a natural-language task and runs an LLM loop with bash, file-edit, sequential-thinking and task-done tools. It works with OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, Azure, OpenRouter, Doubao and Ollama, and can run tasks inside Docker containers. It records full trajectories to JSON and is built to be modified for agent research.
strengths: Many providers, including Ollama for local models, plus custom base_url support
Trajectory files log LLM calls, steps and tool use for debugging and analysis
Can run tasks in a new or existing Docker container, or one built from a Dockerfile
Optional MCP servers configured in YAML; modular code aimed at ablation studies
weaknesses: Terminal only; no IDE extension or web UI described
Installed from source with uv and Python 3.12+; no release published
Config is YAML with a legacy JSON format; tabs are not allowed
README says the project is still under active development

projects.name: copilot.vim
projects.tagline: Inline GitHub Copilot code suggestions for Vim and Neovim
projects.summary: Vim and Neovim plugin that shows GitHub Copilot completions inline as you type, built from comments and method names. Suggestions are accepted with Tab. It needs Node.js and an active Copilot subscription, including the Free tier, and is set up with `:Copilot setup`.
strengths: Works in both Vim (9.0.0185 or newer) and Neovim
Installs with any plugin manager or a plain git clone into the pack directory
Inline suggestions accepted with Tab; built-in help via `:help copilot`
Copilot Free tier is available for sign-up
weaknesses: Requires a GitHub Copilot subscription and a connection to the hosted service
Needs Node.js (and NPM) installed separately
Inline completion only; the README mentions no repo-wide agent features
License not identified (NOASSERTION); README lists no supported models

projects.name: avante.nvim
projects.tagline: Neovim plugin that adds Cursor-style AI chat and code edits inside the editor
projects.summary: avante.nvim is a Lua Neovim plugin with a Rust-built component. It opens a chat sidebar that answers questions about the current file and applies suggested changes to source files. It supports an agentic mode with tools, ACP agents such as codex and gemini, and many model providers. A per-project avante.md file supplies instructions.
strengths: Runs inside Neovim; suggested changes can be applied to files with one command
Supports many providers: openai, anthropic, mistral, deepseek, ollama, llama-cpp, copilot
ACP support lets external agents like codex and gemini drive edits
Project-level avante.md instructions file; optional local RAG service
weaknesses: Requires Neovim 0.11+ (badge says 0.12+); README is inconsistent on version
Install needs a build step: make with curl and tar, or cargo to build from source
Auto-suggestions are marked experimental and costly because of high request frequency
Tool permissions are auto-approved by default (auto_approve_tool_permissions = true)

projects.name: skills
projects.tagline: Agent skills for planning, TDD, debugging and code review
projects.summary: A collection of Markdown skill files for coding agents, split into engineering and productivity groups. It covers grilling sessions that build a project glossary and ADRs, spec and ticket generation, red-green-refactor TDD, a bug diagnosis loop, and diff review. Installs as a plugin for Claude Code, Codex and GitHub Copilot, via gemini skills install for Gemini CLI, or as editable files through npx skills.
strengths: Small, composable skills that can be edited; README says they work with any model
Plugin install for Claude Code, Codex and Copilot, with automatic updates
Setup skill configures issue tracker (GitHub, GitLab, local files), triage labels and doc locations
Separates user-invoked orchestration skills from model-invoked discipline skills
weaknesses: Manual updates for Gemini CLI and npx installs
Installing both plugin and npx copies gives every skill twice
Must run /setup-matt-pocock-skills once per repo before the engineering skills
Architecture skill is a survey only and will not untangle an old codebase

projects.name: ecc
projects.tagline: Agents, skills, hooks and rules bundle for Claude Code, Codex and other harnesses
projects.summary: ECC installs a plan, test, implement, review, verify workflow into coding agents. It ships 71 agents, 311 skills, 97 legacy command shims, hooks, selectable rules, session memory and the AgentShield scanner for prompts, hooks, MCP config and permissions. Native plugin paths exist for Claude Code and Codex; Cursor, OpenCode, Gemini, Zed and others get capability-limited adapters.
strengths: Large bundle: 71 agents, 311 skills, hooks and rules in one install
Guided setup wizard for Claude Code, Codex and Kimi Code with dry-run mode
Includes AgentShield scanning of MCP config, permissions, hooks and secrets
MIT licensed; npm releases pinned per version tag
weaknesses: Feature parity varies; non-Claude harnesses are capability-limited adapters
Claude plugins cannot ship rules, so rule packs need a manual copy
Stacking install methods duplicates skills and hooks; README warns against it
Private-repo GitHub App is paid (from $19/seat/month)

projects.name: caveman
projects.tagline: Cuts token use in coding agents with terse replies and compressed inputs
projects.summary: Caveman is a CLI and skill set that reduces token use in coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI and OpenCode. It shortens agent replies, compresses logs, JSON, CSV and test output before the model reads them, and can route each request to a model and effort level through a free account. Reported results include 33.2% fewer input tokens over 54 Claude Code runs and an interim 54% cost cut for Auto on 85 tasks.
strengths: One npx command sets up 30+ agents; runs locally with your own keys
README lists losing cases: HTML input 9.9% worse, grep-defs loses to bare grep
Each part can be switched off separately; the skill installs alone
Cited by Adobe Research paper, JetBrains A/B on 86 tasks, Elastic blog
weaknesses: Auto routing needs a Caveman account; its benchmark is interim and half complete
Terse output saves nothing on per-request billing such as GitHub Copilot
Rules cost about 1,160 input tokens; output benchmarks used older 3.1.0 rules
No HTML compressor yet; Blocks is pre-release (v0.1.0-rc.5), Python only

projects.name: ponytail
projects.tagline: Skill prompt that makes coding agents write less code and add tests
projects.summary: Ponytail is a single prompt (SKILL.md, with a compact AGENTS.md) that loads into coding agents such as Claude Code and Codex. It tells the agent to check existing code, the standard library and native platform features before writing anything, and adds /ponytail-review, /ponytail-audit and /ponytail-debt commands. The README reports 53% less code and 45% fewer tokens in its own 39-task benchmark.
strengths: Works with 20 agents; plugin install for Claude Code and Codex, AGENTS.md for others
Benchmark method and per-task tables are published in the repo
Keeps validation, security and accessibility; leaves a small test for risky logic
No config file required; default level can be set by env var or JSON file
weaknesses: Benchmark figures are self-reported, run in Claude Code with Opus 5.5 only
Slash commands need a skill-capable host; rule-file adapters get only the always-on prompt
Cursor with hooks supports only /ponytail level switching, not review or audit
README is heavy on banners and a waitlist, with a jokey tone

projects.name: ui-ux-pro-max-skill
projects.tagline: Design-system skill that gives coding agents searchable UI styles, palettes and fonts
projects.summary: An agent skill that runs a local Python search script (BM25 ranking, standard library only) over CSV datasets of UI styles, color palettes, font pairings, landing patterns and UX guidelines. Given a product description, it applies 192 industry reasoning rules and outputs a design system with pattern, style, colors, typography, anti-patterns and a checklist. An npm CLI installs it for Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI and about 20 other assistants.
strengths: Scripts use only the Python standard library and make no network calls
One CLI (uipro init --ai) installs to over 20 assistants, per project or globally
Data is plain CSV: 79 styles, 192 palettes, 74 font pairings, 119 UX guidelines
Covers 22 stacks including React, Next.js, Vue, SwiftUI, Flutter and Jetpack Compose
weaknesses: Requires Python 3 on the machine; the agent will not install it for you
Brand identity, logo, CIP and image-generation features are in the paid premium version
Recommendations are rule and keyword matches; output quality depends on the agent using it
Only 50 of 79 styles are active in normal recommendations

projects.name: impeccable
projects.tagline: Design skill with 24 commands and a detector for AI-generated frontends
projects.summary: Impeccable installs a single /impeccable skill into AI coding tools, with 24 commands such as audit, critique, polish, typeset and live browser variant iteration. It writes PRODUCT.md and DESIGN.md for project context, and ships 59 deterministic detector rules that run in a CLI and browser extension without an LLM or API key. Hooks flag common AI design tells on UI file edits in supported harnesses.
strengths: Supports many harnesses: Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Gemini CLI, Copilot, Grok Build, Hermes
59 deterministic detector rules run without an LLM or API key
Edit hooks surface design findings; Cursor blocks bad writes before they land
Several install paths: npx installer, Git submodule, plugin marketplace, manual copy
weaknesses: Native edit hooks are not available on every harness; Hermes and Veto get none
Roll API at impeccable.style is called when a new design starts; telemetry is opt-out
Downloads an engine binary into ~/.impeccable/bin/ on first run if not bundled
Codex and Grok Build need manual hook or folder trust approval after install

projects.name: spec-kit
projects.tagline: CLI and agent skills for spec-driven development, bug fixing and idea assessment
projects.summary: Spec Kit is a Python CLI (`specify`) that scaffolds a project with slash-command skills for AI coding agents such as GitHub Copilot. Its core flow is constitution, specify, plan, tasks, implement, converge. Bug-fix (assess, fix, test) and idea-assessment (intake through decide) processes are opt-in extensions that write Markdown reports under `.specify/`.
strengths: Three independent processes; bug fixing and assessment install separately via `specify extension add`
Artifacts are plain Markdown in `.specify/`, reviewable and editable by hand
Integration keys let the same workflow target different coding agents
Extensions, presets, workflows and bundles allow customizing or replacing the processes
weaknesses: Needs a separate supported AI coding agent; it does not run models itself
Skills are invoked in agent chat, with invocation syntax varying by agent
Requires Python 3.11+ and uv
Process is manual and stepwise: each skill is run and reviewed one at a time

projects.name: agent-skills
projects.tagline: Markdown skill pack and slash commands for the software lifecycle in coding agents
projects.summary: A set of 25 SKILL.md workflows covering spec, plan, build, test, review and ship, plus 9 slash commands, 4 agent personas and reference checklists. Skills are plain Markdown with steps, verification gates and anti-rationalization tables. They install into Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Copilot and others via the skills CLI or native plugin commands.
strengths: Installs into 70+ agents with one `npx skills add` command
Each skill has explicit steps, verification gates and exit criteria
Native plugin installs for Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity and Gemini CLI
Skills are plain Markdown, usable with any agent that reads instruction files
weaknesses: Slash commands like /spec and /build are Claude Code only; Copilot needs skills invoked by name
Per-skill npx install omits the shared references/ checklists (issue #361)
Cursor and Windsurf need manual copying into rules or skills directories
Testing reference examples target JavaScript/TypeScript

projects.name: claude-mem
projects.tagline: Persistent cross-session memory plugin for Claude Code and other coding agents
projects.summary: Claude-Mem hooks into Claude Code session lifecycle events (SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PostToolUse, Stop, SessionEnd), records tool-usage observations and summaries in SQLite, and injects relevant context into later sessions. A local Bun-managed worker serves an HTTP API and web viewer, with hybrid FTS5 and Chroma vector search exposed through three MCP tools: search, timeline and get_observations. Installers also cover OpenCode, T3 Code, Antigravity, OMP, Pi and OpenClaw.
strengths: Search, timeline, get_observations flow filters before fetching details; README claims ~10x token savings
Local SQLite storage with FTS5 plus Chroma hybrid search, and a web viewer for stored memory
One npx installer targets Claude Code, OpenCode, T3 Code, Antigravity, OMP, Pi and others
`<private>` tags exclude content from storage; settings live in ~/.claude-mem/settings.json
weaknesses: Default installer prompts for sign-in to a hosted observer with a 30-day trial, then paid
Needs Node 20+, Bun and uv; the last two are auto-installed
`npm install -g claude-mem` installs only the SDK, not the hooks or worker
Summaries are generated by an extra model (hosted, OpenRouter, Gemini or Anthropic plan), adding usage

projects.name: superpowers
projects.tagline: Skill set that enforces a plan-and-TDD workflow in coding agents
projects.summary: Superpowers is a library of composable skills plus a bootstrap skill (using-superpowers) that makes a coding agent brainstorm a spec, write a task plan, and implement it with subagents under red/green TDD and code review. It installs as a plugin or extension for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Copilot CLI, OpenCode, Pi and others. Skills trigger automatically.
strengths: Installs via plugin marketplaces or one command on 15+ listed agent harnesses
Covers the full loop: brainstorming, worktrees, plans, subagent execution, review, branch finish
diagnosing-superpowers skill reads session transcripts and can export a scrubbed bug bundle
MIT licensed, with eval harness and plugin tests in the repo
weaknesses: Workflows are mandatory, so small tasks go through the same process
Subagent-driven mode costs more tokens than inline execution
Install is per harness; each agent needs separate setup
Optional visual companion loads a vendor-hosted logo that reports version unless disabled by env var

projects.name: archify
projects.tagline: Agent skill that turns descriptions or repos into interactive HTML diagrams
projects.summary: Archify is a skill for Cursor, Claude Code, Codex CLI and OpenCode, installed with `npx skills add tt-a1i/archify -g`. Given a description or a repository, the agent generates a self-contained interactive HTML diagram of one of five types: architecture, workflow, sequence, data flow or lifecycle. Output supports theme switching, route and reach tracing, and PNG or share-card export.
strengths: Output is standalone HTML that opens in a browser without installing Archify
Five diagram types, plus Before/Delta/After architecture comparison with a machine receipt
Works from a plain description; no repository required
Update check can be disabled with ARCHIFY_UPDATE_CHECK_DISABLED=1 and never auto-installs
weaknesses: Needs an AI coding agent and its model; Archify does not generate diagrams alone
Optional update check makes a network GET to a fixed manifest by default
Deployment-ownership profile checks authored facts only, not live infrastructure
README is heavy on sponsors and promotion, which buries technical details

projects.name: ruflo
projects.tagline: Agent harness for Claude Code and Codex with swarms, memory and MCP tools
projects.summary: Ruflo wraps Claude Code and Codex with a CLI, an MCP server and Claude Code plugins that add agent definitions, swarm coordination, vector-backed memory, hooks and a console UI. It installs either as marketplace plugins (35 listed) or through `npx ruflo init`, which writes .claude/ config, hooks and a daemon into the project. The README cites 98 agents, 60+ commands, 30 skills and 314 MCP tools.
strengths: Two install paths: zero-file Claude Code plugins or full CLI init with hooks and MCP server
Works with any MCP client via `npx -y ruflo@latest mcp start`
Console permission levels (read/write/manage/full) with ask or auto approval
Optional standalone terminal UI via `npx ruflo tui`, with a plain mode for scripts
weaknesses: Large surface (314 MCP tools, 35 plugins) that the README itself says not to learn
Mods run with account permissions, are not sandboxed; README says read code first
Console, mods and hooks are Claude Code integrations; other clients get MCP tools only
Plugin path has different tool names and fewer features than the CLI path

projects.name: oh-my-claudecode
projects.tagline: Multi-agent orchestration plugin and CLI for Claude Code
projects.summary: Adds staged team pipelines (plan, PRD, exec, verify, fix), autopilot and persistent execution loops to Claude Code, as a plugin and as an `omc` npm CLI. `omc team` can launch tmux worker panes running claude, codex, gemini, antigravity, grok or cursor-agent CLIs. Configuration lives in `.claude/omc.jsonc`.
strengths: Installs as a Claude Code plugin or as an npm CLI (`omc`)
Team workers can be claude, codex, gemini, antigravity, grok or cursor CLIs in tmux
Workers spawn per task and exit when done, so nothing idles
Includes a deep-interview skill and a HUD statusline
weaknesses: Requires Claude Code; in-session team mode needs an experimental flag enabled
Slash-command skills such as /autopilot and /ralph cannot run in CI
Named autopilot workflow profiles need Linux with flock
npm package name (oh-my-claude-sisyphus) differs from repo name; install prints a deprecation warning

projects.name: graphify
projects.tagline: Skill that maps a codebase and docs into a queryable knowledge graph
projects.summary: Graphify installs as a skill for AI coding assistants such as Claude Code, Cursor, Codex and Gemini CLI. Running /graphify parses code with tree-sitter across about 40 languages, and handles docs, PDFs, images and video through the assistant's model. It writes graph.json, graph.html and GRAPH_REPORT.md, and the graph can then be queried with query, path and explain commands instead of grepping files.
strengths: Code parsing is local tree-sitter AST, with no LLM calls and no data leaving the machine
Each edge is tagged EXTRACTED or INFERRED, so direct reads are separable from resolved links
Installs into 20+ assistants with one command per platform, including project-scoped installs
Outputs plain files (graph.json, graph.html, GRAPH_REPORT.md) queryable without re-reading source
weaknesses: Docs, PDFs, images and video need an LLM backend or the assistant's model for the semantic pass
PDF, Office, video, MCP and Neo4j support are separate optional extras to install
Monorepo and cross-repo support, formal verification and Sentry/Jira connectors are in paid Graphify Cloud
Benchmarks are the project's own; LOCOMO QA accuracy is below supermemory (45.3% vs 49.7%)

projects.name: rtk
projects.tagline: CLI proxy that compresses shell command output before coding agents read it
projects.summary: rtk is a single Rust binary that wraps 100+ shell commands (git, cargo test, pytest, docker, kubectl, aws and others) and returns grouped, truncated or deduplicated output. `rtk init` installs a hook for Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Codex, Cursor, Windsurf and other agents that rewrites Bash calls such as `git status` to `rtk git status`. The README claims up to 90% less bash output and under 10ms overhead.
strengths: Single Rust binary; README states under 10ms overhead per command
Auto-rewrite hook covers many agents: Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Codex, Cursor, Windsurf, Cline
Per-command filters for tests, linters, git, docker, kubectl, AWS and Pulumi
`rtk gain` reports savings history; `rtk discover` finds missed rewrites
weaknesses: Hook only affects Bash calls; Claude's built-in Read, Grep and Glob bypass it
Token counts are estimated as bytes/4; no tokenizer, so absolute numbers are approximate
Up to 90% applies to bash output only, not to the total bill
Another 'rtk' crate exists on crates.io; install via git, not the crate name

projects.name: openspec
projects.tagline: Spec-driven workflow CLI that guides AI coding assistants through plan, apply and archive
projects.summary: OpenSpec is a Node.js CLI that adds an `openspec/` folder to a repo and installs slash commands (such as /opsx:propose, /opsx:apply, /opsx:archive) into 30+ AI coding tools. Each change gets a folder with proposal.md, specs, design.md and tasks.md in plain Markdown, which the human reviews before code is written. A beta Stores feature keeps specs and changes in a separate shared repo for cross-repo work.
strengths: Specs and changes are plain Markdown in the repo, versioned with git
Works with 30+ AI coding tools through generated slash commands
Install via npm or Homebrew; no server or database needed
Designed for existing codebases, with an adoption guide for brownfield projects
weaknesses: Needs Node.js 20.19.0 or higher
Stores (cross-repo shared planning) are still in beta
Collects anonymous usage telemetry by default; opt-out via config or env var
Command syntax differs per tool, e.g. /opsx-propose, @opsx-propose, $openspec-propose

projects.name: agentic-awesome-skills
projects.tagline: 2,689 installable SKILL.md playbooks for coding agents, with a local MCP
projects.summary: A library of SKILL.md playbooks for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Kiro, Copilot and others, installed with an npx installer. AAS Core is a local MCP plus an `aas` CLI that lets the agent search the catalog, save its chosen skills to `aas-stack.json`, validate them and write a plan preview. Core does not rank skills, and apply and recovery are experimental.
strengths: 2,689+ skills, each a plain SKILL.md, with a machine-readable skills_index.json
Installer has --dry-run and filters for category, risk and tags
Install targets for about a dozen agent hosts, plus Claude Code and Codex plugin bundles
Core records the exact selected skills in a manifest you can review before installing
weaknesses: Core apply and recovery are experimental and outside the supported preview
Validation checks structure only, not whether a skill fits or is safe
Loading too many skills can overload Antigravity, so a selected set or filter is required
Core MCP setup is supported only for Codex and Claude

projects.name: book-to-skill
projects.tagline: Converts books and document folders into on-demand agent skills with per-chapter files
projects.summary: A Python extractor turns PDF, EPUB, DOCX, Markdown, HTML, RTF or MOBI files into clean text. The agent then follows SKILL.md to generate a skill: a core SKILL.md, one file per chapter, a glossary, patterns and a cheatsheet. The skill installs under ~/.agents/skills/ and loads chapters on demand in Claude Code, Copilot CLI, Amp, Codex, Hermes Agent, OpenCode or OpenClaw. The README reports 24x–51x fewer tokens than dumping the book into context.
strengths: Reads PDF, EPUB, DOCX, MD, HTML, RTF and MOBI, with fallbacks to stdlib parsers
One SKILL.md output works across seven agent hosts that follow the Agent Skills format
Chapter files load only when asked, keeping the base skill near 4,000 tokens
Extraction runs locally; `extract.py --check` reports which extractors are missing
weaknesses: Scanned PDFs are rejected; OCR (for example ocrmypdf) must be run first
Generation quality depends on the host agent and its model, not the extractor
MOBI/AZW needs Calibre installed separately
Sharing skills built from copyrighted books can infringe; README advises keeping them private

projects.name: cc-switch
projects.tagline: Desktop app for switching API providers across AI coding CLIs
projects.summary: CC Switch is a Tauri 2 desktop app (Rust) for Windows, macOS and Linux. It swaps API providers for Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Codex, Gemini CLI, Grok Build, OpenCode, OpenClaw, Hermes Agent, Pi and MiniMax Code, and manages MCP, Skills and Prompts in one place, so JSON, TOML or YAML configs need not be edited by hand.
strengths: Covers ten coding agents and CLIs from one provider list
Manages MCP servers, Skills and Prompts alongside provider switching
Native desktop builds for Windows, macOS and Linux via Tauri 2
MIT licensed, with a user manual and multilingual READMEs
weaknesses: Desktop GUI only; no Docker image or server mode
Much of the README is sponsor relay advertising, not technical detail
Config backup and rollback behavior unknown; README is truncated
Does not run agents itself; the CLIs must be installed separately

projects.name: gstack
projects.tagline: Slash-command skill pack giving Claude Code review, QA and ship roles
projects.summary: gstack is a set of Markdown skills, invoked as slash commands such as /office-hours, /plan-eng-review, /review, /qa, /cso and /ship, that give Claude Code defined roles for planning, code review, browser QA, security audit and release. A Bun-based ./setup installs it into ~/.claude/skills and builds a bundled browser. Experimental installs exist for Codex, OpenCode, Cursor, Copilot CLI and others.
strengths: Covers planning, review, QA, security audit and release as separate slash commands
Team mode auto-updates for shared repos without vendoring files into them
Installs on Claude Code plus experimental hosts such as Codex, Cursor and OpenCode
Setup took 31 seconds on a 4-vCPU Linux machine, per the README
weaknesses: Safety hooks like /careful and /freeze are enforced only on Claude Code
Only Claude Code is certified; other agents are experimental or instruction-only
/cso needs a recent Bun with specific build flags and a native C toolchain
Outside reviews need a signed-in Codex CLI; design tools use an OpenAI key

projects.name: repomix
projects.tagline: CLI that packs a repository into one file for LLM context
projects.summary: Repomix reads a local or remote Git repository and writes a single file, XML by default or Markdown, JSON or plain text, with a directory tree and file contents. It reports token counts, respects .gitignore, .ignore and .repomixignore, and uses Secretlint to leave out files matching known credential formats. The --compress option uses Tree-sitter to keep code structure while cutting tokens.
strengths: One command (npx repomix@latest) produces the packed file with no install
Token counts per file and for the whole repo help fit context limits
--compress uses Tree-sitter to reduce tokens while keeping code structure
Packs remote repos by URL, branch or commit, and file lists piped via --stdin
weaknesses: Output is a static snapshot; you paste or upload it to the model yourself
Secret detection only covers known credential formats via Secretlint
VSCode extension is community-maintained, not part of the core project
Whole large repos can exceed model context unless filtered or compressed

projects.name: reverse-skill
projects.tagline: Routes AI coding agents to reverse-engineering and pentest playbooks
projects.summary: reverse-skill is a skill/routing package for AI coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode) that, when the agent hits an APK, binary, obfuscated JS, CTF challenge or pentest target, picks the right methodology and tool (jadx, apktool, Frida, IDA, radare2, Ghidra, BurpSuite) instead of guessing commands. Routing is driven by a single JSON config (43-44 rules) validated by a 173-case regression suite and CI on Windows and Ubuntu, covering mobile, firmware, malware, pwn, EDR bypass and API security.
strengths: Client-neutral routing core works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and OpenCode
Single routing.json source of truth with a 173-case regression benchmark run in CI
Covers a wide scenario matrix: APK, iOS, .NET, JS, firmware, pwn, EDR bypass, CTF
Includes case/evidence workflow (scope, timeline, findings) not just tool dispatch
weaknesses: Core scripts are PowerShell-based, with separate bash variants for Linux/macOS/Kali
Requires external install of Java/JDK, Node.js 22.12+, Python 3.x and the RE tools themselves
CTF-Sandbox-Orchestrator submodule is GPLv3, mixed licensing alongside the MIT core
A routing layer, not an RE engine itself, so it depends on tools already being installed

projects.name: taste-skill
projects.tagline: Agent Skills that steer AI coding agents toward better frontend design
projects.summary: A set of SKILL.md files that give coding agents rules for layout, typography, motion and spacing, plus image-generation skills for web, mobile and brand-kit reference boards. The default skill exposes three 1-10 dials (DESIGN_VARIANCE, MOTION_INTENSITY, VISUAL_DENSITY). Installs with `npx skills add` or as a Claude Code plugin; also usable in Codex and Cursor.
strengths: Installs per skill via `npx skills add --skill <name>` or as a Claude Code plugin
Three adjustable dials in the default skill: variance, motion intensity, visual density
Separate skills for redesign, minimalist, brutalist, soft UI and image-to-code workflows
Framework agnostic; rules target design intent rather than one framework API
weaknesses: Default taste-skill v2 is marked experimental and not yet at a stable 2.0.0
Image-generation skills need a separate generator such as ChatGPT Images
No published releases; output quality depends on the agent and model used
README gives no benchmarks or measured results, only one example screenshot

projects.name: claude-hud
projects.tagline: Status line plugin for Claude Code showing context, usage limits and todos
projects.summary: Claude HUD is a Claude Code plugin that registers a status line command, which prints context-window usage, subscriber rate limits, model, project path and git branch below the input. Optional lines show active tools, subagents, skills, MCP servers and todo progress, read from the session transcript. Settings live in a JSON config file or the /claude-hud:configure flow, and it needs no tmux or separate window.
strengths: Installs from the Claude Code plugin marketplace with a few slash commands
Reads session data Claude Code passes on stdin; no separate window or tmux
Extensive config: layout, element order, thresholds, colors, git and jj status
Labels available in English, Simplified and Traditional Chinese
weaknesses: Works only with Claude Code
Subscriber usage limits are hidden on API-key, Bedrock and Vertex sessions
Tools, agents and todos lines are off by default and parse the transcript
Needs a JavaScript runtime; Windows users must install Node.js separately

projects.name: compound-engineering-plugin
projects.tagline: Plugin of 36 agent skills for a plan, build, review and document loop
projects.summary: Compound Engineering is a plugin of 36 skills for AI coding agents, organized around a loop of brainstorm, plan, work, simplify, review and compound. The compound step writes learnings into docs/solutions/, which later brainstorm and plan runs read as context. It installs on 14 agent hosts, including Claude Code, Cursor and Codex, and includes an autonomous /lfg pipeline that can open a PR and watch CI.
strengths: Runs on 14 agent hosts, including Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Copilot and OpenCode
Captures learnings as repo files (docs/solutions/) that later planning reads
Covers the full cycle: brainstorm, plan, work, review, plus debug, commit and PR skills
Artifact folder location is configurable via the docs_root setting
weaknesses: 36 skills and a multi-step workflow add process overhead for small changes
Install steps differ per host; Cline and Pi need extra setup or companion packages
Compound Packs for org-wide rules are marked experimental
Some Devin skills use Claude-style tool names and prompt for permission

projects.name: oh-my-codex
projects.tagline: Workflow layer for Codex CLI with skills, roles and durable project state
projects.summary: OMX wraps OpenAI Codex CLI with an `omx` launcher, skills such as `$deep-interview`, `$ralplan`, `$ultragoal`, `$team` and `$code-review`, and specialist roles. Plans, logs, memory and mode state are kept under `.omx/`, and team workers run in separate git worktrees, with tmux for the team runtime. Codex remains the execution engine; OMX adds scoped AGENTS.md guidance and an optional Codex plugin layout.
strengths: Staged workflow: interview, plan, then durable execution with checkpoints in .omx/ultragoal
Team workers get dedicated git worktrees automatically; named worktrees isolate sessions
Installs with npm; omx doctor and omx exec smoke test check install and auth
Also ships a Codex plugin layout with marketplace metadata
weaknesses: Tuned mainly for macOS/Linux; native Windows and Codex App get less support
Requires Codex CLI installed and authenticated; does not run standalone
--madmax disables Codex approvals and sandbox, so only use in trusted repos
Large skill and command surface; loading many skills bloats context

projects.name: planning-with-files
projects.tagline: Agent skill that keeps task plans in markdown files that survive /clear
projects.summary: Keeps task_plan.md, findings.md and progress.md in the project and uses lifecycle hooks to re-inject the active plan each turn, so a coding agent resumes after /clear, compaction or a crash. A Stop-time completion gate can hold the agent until the plan reports complete. Installs via `npx skills add` for 60+ agents, with native plugins for Claude Code, Codex CLI, Qoder CLI, Pi, Hermes, OpenCode and DeepSeek Harness.
strengths: Plain markdown plan files on disk, no runtime state or database elsewhere
Native plugins for several hosts plus the generic Agent Skills install route
Completion gate holds the agent's stop until the plan reports complete
Translated variants in 5 languages ship the full script surface
weaknesses: Hook behavior and available commands differ per host; Qoder CLI needs Bash and Python 3.10+
Plan files are gitignored and overwritten by the next task unless you keep them
Benchmark claims rest on small samples (3 blind A/B comparisons, 30 assertions)
Completion gate depends on literal English status tokens matched with grep -F

projects.name: skills
projects.tagline: CLI that installs SKILL.md agent skills into dozens of coding agents
projects.summary: An npm CLI (`npx skills`) that fetches skills defined as SKILL.md files from GitHub, GitLab, Azure Repos, any git URL, a local path or an archive URL, and installs them into each coding agent's skills directory. It supports project or global scope and symlinked or copied installs, and it adds list, find, update, remove and init commands. The README lists about 80 supported agents, including Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and OpenCode.
strengths: One command installs a skill into many agents' directories, using symlinks to a canonical copy
Accepts GitHub shorthand, GitLab, Azure Repos, any git URL, local paths and archive URLs
Private repos use existing Git credentials, GitHub CLI or SSH; a token is optional
Non-interactive flags (-y, --all, -g, -a) make it usable in CI
weaknesses: Needs Node.js and npx; the README does not state a minimum version
Only manages skills; it does not supply the agents themselves
Agent support depends on a hand-maintained table of paths for each agent
Symlinks may not work on every platform; copy mode is the fallback

projects.name: notebooklm-py
projects.tagline: Unofficial Python API, CLI and MCP server for Google NotebookLM
projects.summary: Drives NotebookLM (now Gemini Notebook) through its undocumented web endpoints, with an opt-in Android gRPC backend. It exposes notebooks, sources, cited chat, research agents and artifact generation (audio, video, slides, quizzes, mind maps) via an async Python client, a CLI, an MCP server, a REST server and an installable agent skill. Artifacts download in bulk as MP3, MP4, PDF, PPTX, CSV, JSON or Markdown.
strengths: Covers notebooks, sources, chat, notes, research, sharing and all Studio artifact types
Bulk artifact download in MP3, MP4, PDF, PPTX, CSV, JSON and Markdown
Ships CLI, MCP server (stdio or remote), REST server and Claude Code/Codex skill
Master-token auth refreshes sessions unattended for servers and CI
weaknesses: Relies on undocumented Google APIs that can break without notice
Not affiliated with Google; heavy use may be rate limited
Needs a Google account; source counts per notebook depend on account tier
Default login downloads Chromium (~170 MB) via Playwright

projects.name: agents
projects.tagline: Plugin, agent and skill collection for Claude Code, Codex CLI, Cursor and others
projects.summary: A catalog of 94 plugins (92 local, 2 external) holding 202 agents, 184 skills and 105 commands, written once as Markdown in the Claude Code plugin format. Native marketplaces serve Claude Code, Codex CLI and Cursor, while adapters generate artifacts for OpenCode, Antigravity CLI, GitHub Copilot and Pi. Individual skills can be installed alone with `gh skill` or `npx skills`.
strengths: One Markdown source adapted to seven coding tools
Skills install individually via gh skill or npx skills
Broad coverage: Python, JavaScript, testing, security, infrastructure
MIT license; plugin-eval runs static skill checks without model calls
weaknesses: OpenCode, Antigravity, Copilot and Pi need a clone, uv and Python 3.12+
Features differ by harness; Codex agents and commands use a separate generated path
Pi agents need a subagent extension
plugin-eval LLM judge and Monte Carlo layers are experimental, not validated against human labels

projects.name: beads
projects.tagline: Dependency-aware issue tracker CLI that gives coding agents persistent task memory
projects.summary: bd (Beads) is a Go CLI that stores tasks as a dependency graph in a Dolt database, replacing markdown TODO lists for coding agents. Agents use commands such as bd ready, bd update --claim and bd close, with JSON output and hash-based IDs to avoid merge collisions. bd setup installs hooks and instructions for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and others; sync runs through Dolt remotes on a git remote.
strengths: Hash-based IDs (bd-a1b2) avoid merge collisions across agents and branches
Embedded Dolt mode needs no separate database server
bd setup installs integrations for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Factory and more
Works without git via BEADS_DIR and --stealth, including non-git VCS
weaknesses: Embedded mode is single-writer; concurrent writers need an external dolt sql-server
HTTP backend is marked experimental and diverges from local behavior in documented ways
Upgrades across schema migrations need a designated clone to migrate and push
issues.jsonl is only an export, not a backup; sync relies on Dolt remotes

projects.name: claude-code-router
projects.tagline: Local gateway that routes coding agents to the model providers you choose
projects.summary: Claude Code Router runs a local gateway on port 3456 that Claude Code, Codex, Grok CLI, Kimi CLI, Kilo Code, OpenCode and other clients point at. Providers, models, credentials and routing rules are managed in an Electron desktop app or an npm CLI with a browser UI. It adds retries, ordered fallbacks, credential pools, request logs with token and cost estimates, and tools such as web search, MCP and ToolHub.
strengths: One local endpoint for ten named agents, so provider config lives in one place
Retries, key rotation, credential pools and ordered fallback models are built in
Logs show resolved provider, model, latency, tokens and estimated cost per request
Ships as desktop app (macOS, Windows, Linux), npm CLI or Docker Compose
weaknesses: Docker script builds against a sibling ../../next-ai/gateway checkout when present
Windows desktop packaging must run on Windows x64 because of native better-sqlite3
Remote exposure needs care; README points to a separate Docker guide for it
Large surface (AgentClaw chat relays, browser automation, plugins) beyond plain routing

projects.name: claude-howto
projects.tagline: Tutorial modules and copy-paste templates for learning Claude Code features
projects.summary: A Markdown guide with 10 tutorial modules covering Claude Code slash commands, memory, skills, subagents, MCP, hooks, plugins, checkpoints, advanced features and the CLI. Each module has Mermaid diagrams and templates you copy into .claude/ or ~/.claude/. It also ships /self-assessment and /lesson-quiz commands and a learning path the README estimates at 11-13 hours.
strengths: Templates for each feature: commands, CLAUDE.md, hook scripts, MCP configs, subagents, plugins
Ordered learning path with time estimates per module
Built-in /self-assessment and /lesson-quiz commands for finding gaps
MIT licensed; README says it is synced with each Claude Code release
weaknesses: Tied to Claude Code only; templates are not for other coding agents
Documentation and examples, not an installable tool or library
Most templates are copied by hand; only the plugin examples use /plugin install
Can lag behind Claude Code changes between releases

projects.name: agency-agents
projects.tagline: Markdown agent persona files for Claude Code, Cursor, Codex and other coding tools
projects.summary: A repository of role-specific agent definitions written as Markdown files and grouped into divisions such as engineering and design. Each file describes the agent's identity, workflow, code examples and success metrics. Shell scripts (convert.sh, install.sh) generate and install the files for Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Aider, Windsurf, Codex and others. A separate desktop app for macOS, Linux and Windows does the same install with a GUI.
strengths: Installs into 14+ tools via one script, with --division and --agent filters
Roster spans dozens of engineering roles, from SRE and RAG pipelines to Solidity
Plain Markdown files, easy to read, copy and adapt without running anything
Separate desktop app handles install and updates without a clone
weaknesses: Prompt files only; no runtime, orchestration or agent execution included
OpenCode registers only about 119 agents, so full installs get silently truncated
No tagged release; versioning relies on commit history
Effectiveness claims like 'battle-tested' are not backed by benchmarks in the README

projects.name: understand-anything
projects.tagline: Plugin that builds an explorable knowledge graph of a codebase or wiki
projects.summary: Understand Anything is a plugin for Claude Code and about 15 other agent platforms. Its /understand command runs a multi-agent pipeline that combines Tree-sitter parsing with LLM summaries to write a knowledge graph to .ua/knowledge-graph.json. A local dashboard then offers graph navigation, search, guided tours, diff impact analysis and chat, and /understand-knowledge handles Karpathy-style LLM wikis.
strengths: Tree-sitter extracts imports and call sites deterministically, so structural edges are reproducible
Graph is plain JSON that can be committed; teammates view it with Node.js >= 18 and no LLM
Incremental re-analysis of changed files, plus an optional post-commit auto-update hook
Installs on Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Kiro and others
weaknesses: First /understand run on a large repo can use a significant number of tokens
Needs a host agent platform and an LLM; it is not a standalone tool
Output languages limited to en, zh, zh-TW, ja, ko, ru, vi
Graphs over 10 MB need git-lfs to commit comfortably

projects.name: claude-code-best-practice
projects.tagline: Reference repo of Claude Code configuration patterns and guides
projects.summary: A documentation-first repository that catalogs Claude Code features (subagents, commands, skills, hooks, MCP, settings, memory) with write-ups and example configs under .claude/. It includes a command-to-agent-to-skill orchestration demo (/weather-orchestrator) and a table comparing community workflows such as Superpowers, Spec Kit and OpenSpec.
strengths: Each concept links to a guide page and a matching implemented example in the repo
Working orchestration demo wires a command, an agent and a skill together
Workflow comparison table lists agent, command and skill counts per project
Covers recent Claude Code features such as auto mode, worktrees and agent teams
weaknesses: Reference material only; not an installable plugin or package
Specific to Claude Code; limited use with other coding agents
Many entries link out to external docs and tweets rather than local content
Several listed features are marked beta and may change between releases

projects.name: claude-code-templates
projects.tagline: Installable agents, commands, hooks and MCP configs for Claude Code
projects.summary: A catalog of Claude Code components (agents, slash commands, settings, hooks, MCP integrations and skills) installed per item with `npx claude-code-templates@latest` and browsable at aitmpl.com. It also ships npx-run tools: an analytics view for Claude Code sessions, a mobile-friendly conversation monitor with optional Cloudflare Tunnel access, a health check and a plugin dashboard.
strengths: One npx command installs a chosen agent, command, hook, setting, skill or MCP
Web catalog at aitmpl.com plus docs at docs.aitmpl.com
Includes analytics, health-check and conversation-monitor tools beyond the templates
MIT license; bundled third-party components keep their original licenses
weaknesses: Targets Claude Code only; no other coding assistant is mentioned
Many components come from third-party repos under mixed licenses (MIT, CC0, Apache 2.0)
README gives no per-component quality or review process; vetting is left to the user
Requires Node.js for npx; version requirements are unknown

projects.name: opencodex
projects.tagline: Local proxy that lets Codex, Claude Code and Grok Build use any LLM
projects.summary: opencodex is a local proxy that translates Codex's Responses API into the protocol a chosen provider speaks, covering streaming, tool calls, reasoning tokens and images. It also fronts Claude Code, Claude Desktop and Grok Build, with 40+ built-in providers or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint. A web dashboard on port 10100 configures providers, combos with failover, and a ChatGPT account pool with quota-aware routing.
strengths: 40+ built-in providers plus any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, including Ollama for local models
Combos give one virtual model id with failover or weighted round-robin across providers
Dashboard on localhost:10100 with live request log; `ocx stop` restores original Codex config
Installs via npm with bundled Bun runtime; also desktop apps for macOS, Windows and Linux
weaknesses: ChatGPT account pooling may conflict with provider terms; README warns of possible enforcement
Desktop app is beta and the Windows .msi is not code-signed
Cursor provider is marked experimental
JEV Auto routing is tested only against a mocked endpoint, not a live account

projects.name: openwiki
projects.tagline: Generates a linked Markdown wiki of your repo for coding agents
projects.summary: OpenWiki writes a Markdown wiki into `openwiki/` in a repository, tracks each fact back to source evidence, and updates only what changed. It installs as a skill plus MCP tools into coding agents such as Codex, Claude Code, Cursor and Copilot CLI, or runs as a standalone CLI with its own Deep Agents-based writer. Agents query it through local, model-free `openwiki_search` and `openwiki_read`.
strengths: Installs into ten coding agents, reusing the host's authenticated model session
Claims tracked to source evidence; clean updates skip model calls
Search and read tools are local and read-only; workspaces span linked repos
Resumable page queue; scheduled CI examples for GitHub, GitLab and Bitbucket
weaknesses: Agent-hosted runs cover repository wikis only; personal wikis need the standalone CLI
Connector-sourced context, including LangSmith, is not yet supported in host runs
Visualizer loads graph and Markdown libraries from a public CDN, so it needs internet
Native CLI needs a separately configured model provider and credentials

projects.name: i-have-adhd
projects.tagline: Skill that makes coding assistants answer action-first with numbered steps
projects.summary: A skill/plugin for coding assistants such as Claude Code that rewrites response style around 10 rules: lead with the next action, number multi-step tasks, cap lists at 5 items, give time estimates in minutes, and drop preambles, recaps and closers. Behavior is defined in skills/i-have-adhd/SKILL.md, and you can fork and edit that file, then reinstall your copy through the plugin marketplace commands.
strengths: Behavior lives in one editable SKILL.md with 10 explicit rules
Before/after example shows the exact output change
Install is a single prompt pasted into the assistant
MIT licensed; README translated into 10 languages
weaknesses: Only changes response style; adds no tools or capabilities
Tune-it steps shown only for Claude Code plugin commands
No tagged releases
No evidence offered that it improves outcomes beyond one example

projects.name: diagram-design
projects.tagline: Agent skill that draws brand-styled diagrams as single HTML and SVG files
projects.summary: An Agent Skill that has a coding agent write one self-contained HTML file with inline SVG for a requested diagram. It covers 45 diagram types, each in minimal light, minimal dark and full-editorial variants, and can pull a site's palette and fonts so later diagrams match. strengths: Output is one HTML file with inline SVG; no build step, JavaScript or external images
45 diagram types, each in light, dark and editorial variants
Installs on many hosts: Claude Code, Codex, Copilot, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Cline, Pi, Kiro
CI checks for overlaps and clipping; layout is on a 4px grid
weaknesses: Output quality depends on the model; the same prompt can lay out differently twice

One opinionated editorial style; other looks need style guide edits
Slash commands (/export-diagram, /profile) only in native packages, not the skills CLI install

projects.name: claude-skills
projects.tagline: Skills and plugins library for Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI and Cursor
projects.summary: A collection of SKILL.md instruction packages, stdlib-only Python CLI scripts and reference docs across 20 domains, including engineering, marketing, compliance, C-level advisory and research. It installs as Claude Code plugins from a marketplace, or converts with scripts/convert.sh into Cursor, Aider, Windsurf, Kilo Code, OpenCode and Augment formats. strengths: Python tools are stdlib-only, no pip installs required
Installs via Claude Code plugin marketplace, per domain or per skill
convert.sh and install.sh target Cursor, Aider, Windsurf, Kilo Code, OpenCode, Augment

weaknesses: Broad scope; many domains are non-coding (marketing, finance, compliance)
README counts are inconsistent (345 vs 388 skills, 5,200+ stars claim)
Hermes Agent and Mistral Vibe need a manual one-time sync script
Windows needs a symlink-enabled clone and PYTHONUTF8=1 for mirror trees

projects.name: browser-harness
projects.tagline: Lets an LLM drive your real Chrome session over a single CDP websocket
projects.summary: Browser Harness connects a coding agent such as Claude Code or Codex to your own logged-in browser through the Chrome DevTools Protocol. strengths: Uses your real browser, so existing logins and sessions are available to the agent

MCP server over stdio works with Claude Code, Cursor, Devin and other clients
MIT license; install and connection steps documented in install.md

Agent-written helpers are not reviewed, so behavior can vary between runs
README gives no model list, hardware needs or test coverage details

projects.name: cc-haha
projects.tagline: Electron desktop workbench for Claude Code with diff review and multi-session tabs
projects.summary: cc-haha is an Electron and React desktop app for macOS, Windows and Linux that wraps a Claude Code-style agent runtime built on Bun. It adds multi-session tabs, per-file diff review, an in-app browser preview, graphical permission approval, MCP and SubAgent management, and Computer Use. strengths: Installers for macOS, Windows and Linux; CLI also runs from source with Bun
Model choice includes Claude, ChatGPT, Grok, DeepSeek, Kimi, GLM, LM Studio and Ollama
Per-file syntax-highlighted diffs, with the whole turn revertible
Remote access via phone browser (H5) and IM bridges such as Telegram, Slack and Feishu
weaknesses: README does not state RAM or system requirements
Unsigned Windows and draft macOS builds can trigger SmartScreen or Gatekeeper prompts
README carries sponsor and affiliate promotions for third-party API resellers
Main README and most of its text are in Chinese; English is a separate file

projects.name: context-mode
projects.tagline: MCP server that keeps raw tool output out of the context window
projects.summary: Context Mode is an MCP server that runs analysis in a sandbox so raw tool output stays out of the agent's context. strengths: Sandbox tools cut raw output; README cites 315 KB reduced to 5.4 KB
Session events stored in SQLite with FTS5/BM25 retrieval after compaction
Hooks for Claude Code, Gemini CLI, VS Code and JetBrains Copilot, Copilot CLI, Cursor
Claude Code plugin install, plus MCP-only option via npx
weaknesses: Elastic License 2.0, not an OSI open-source license
Non-hook platforms need a manual routing file copy
Most platforms require Node.js >= 22.5 or Bun
Savings figures are README examples, not independent benchmarks

projects.name: claude-code-game-studios
projects.tagline: Claude Code template with 49 game-studio subagents, 74 slash-command skills and hooks
projects.summary: A project template that adds studio-style structure to Claude Code for game development: 49 subagents in three tiers, 74 skills such as /start, /brainstorm and /dev-story, 12 hooks and 13 path-scoped rules. A project.yaml `modes.rigor` setting (minimal, standard, full) controls how much documentation and review the workflow requires. It includes agent sets for Godot 4, Unity and Unreal Engine 5.
strengths: Engine-specific agent sets for Godot 4, Unity and Unreal Engine 5
Single modes.rigor setting scales process from jam-style minimal to full director review
Hooks validate commits, pushes and asset JSON; deny rules block force push and rm -rf
Stories that change visuals need a launched game and a retained screenshot to close
weaknesses: Requires Claude Code; no other coding agent is mentioned

README's own test ranked the standard rigor build last against minimal
No sample game is shipped, so output quality cannot be inspected in the repo

projects.name: awesome-claude-code-subagents
projects.tagline: Collection of 161+ Claude Code subagent definitions in 10 categories
projects.summary: Markdown subagent definitions for Claude Code, grouped into 10 categories such as core development, language specialists, infrastructure, quality and security, and data and AI. Interactive and standalone shell installers; standalone one needs only curl
MIT licensed; agents are plain Markdown files you can copy and edit

Written for Claude Code; other agent tools would need the files adapted
Meta-orchestration agents are meant to be used with other categories installed too

projects.name: claude-video

projects.name: claude-skills
projects.tagline: Claude Code plugin with 67 role-based skills and 9 Jira-linked workflow commands
projects.summary: A Claude Code plugin that installs 67 skills covering languages, frameworks, infrastructure, testing, DevOps and security. Covers 12 categories, from languages to security and data/ML
Documented multi-skill workflows, e.g. feature development through code review

Workflow commands require an Atlassian MCP server to be set up
Quality and overlap across 67 skills cannot be judged from the README
Skills are prompt text, so results depend on the model used

projects.name: img2threejs

projects.name: auto-claude-code-research-in-sleep

projects.name: video-shotcraft

projects.name: agentskills
projects.tagline: Open specification for SKILL.md folders that give AI agents reusable instructions
projects.summary: Defines the Agent Skills format: a folder with a SKILL.md file holding name and description metadata plus instructions, and optional scripts, references and assets. Agents load skills in three stages (discovery, activation, execution), so only names and descriptions sit in context until a task matches. Originally developed by Anthropic and released as an open standard; the repo holds the spec and docs, not a runtime.
strengths: Minimal format: one SKILL.md with name and description is enough
Progressive disclosure keeps context small with many skills installed
Skills can bundle scripts, references and templates in one version-controlled folder
Supported by multiple agent clients, listed in a client showcase
weaknesses: Specification and docs only; it is not an agent or runtime
Behavior depends on how each client implements skill loading
No tagged releases; versioning of the spec is not stated in the README
Skill quality and security of bundled scripts are left to authors

projects.name: loop-engineering
projects.tagline: Pattern library and CLI for running scheduled agent loops around a codebase
projects.summary: Loop Engineering is a library of documented patterns (daily triage, PR babysitter, CI sweeper, dependency sweeper, changelog drafter and others) for running coding agents on a schedule against a repo. An npm CLI (@cobusgreyling/loop) scaffolds a pattern for Claude, Grok, Codex or Opencode, then offers doctor, status, audit and cost commands. Rollout is staged from L1 report-only to L3 unattended.
strengths: CLI scaffolds a pattern with init, then checks it with doctor, audit and cost
Eight documented patterns, each with cadence, week-one level and relative cost
Staged L1 to L3 rollout; week one is report-only
Examples for Claude Code, Grok, Codex, Opencode, OpenClaw and GitHub Actions
weaknesses: Mostly docs and templates; the agent itself comes from a separate tool
PR Babysitter and CI Sweeper are rated high or very high cost
README warns unattended loops can ship mistakes and token costs can explode
Related features live in separate companion repos

projects.name: claude-plugins-official
projects.tagline: Anthropic's curated plugin marketplace for Claude Code
projects.summary: A Git repository that acts as the official plugin marketplace for Claude Code. Plugins install with `/plugin install {plugin-name}@claude-plugins-official` or through `/plugin > Discover`. The repo holds Anthropic-maintained plugins in `/plugins` and partner or community plugins in `/external_plugins`, each bundling any of MCP server config, slash commands, agents and skills.
strengths: Installs directly from inside Claude Code with one slash command
Documents a standard plugin layout with an example plugin as reference
Plugin names are immutable slugs, with a renames map for migrations
Supports skill-bundle entries for repos that ship SKILL.md files without a manifest
weaknesses: Only useful with Claude Code; not a standalone tool
Anthropic does not control or verify third-party plugin contents, which can change
No single license; each plugin carries its own LICENSE file
No tagged releases; plugins are pinned only by marketplace entry

projects.name: design.md
projects.tagline: Spec and CLI for describing a design system to coding agents
projects.summary: DESIGN.md defines a file format with YAML front matter for design tokens (colors, typography, rounded, spacing, components) and markdown prose for rationale. The TypeScript CLI, run with npx, lints files for broken token references and WCAG contrast, diffs two versions, and exports tokens to Tailwind v3/v4 and W3C DTCG. The format is at version alpha.
strengths: Lint output is structured JSON with a non-zero exit code on errors, usable in CI
Eleven lint rules cover broken refs, WCAG AA contrast, section order and typos
Exports to Tailwind v3 JSON, Tailwind v4 CSS @theme and W3C DTCG tokens
Also usable as a library via the @google/design.md/linter import
weaknesses: Format is marked alpha; the README warns the spec and schema will change
Only a fixed set of component properties is valid; others produce warnings
Sections must appear in a fixed order, otherwise the linter warns
Windows needs the designmd alias because of the .md bin name collision

projects.name: huashu-design
projects.tagline: Agent skill that turns prompts into HTML prototypes, decks, animations and infographics
projects.summary: A skill for Claude Code, Cursor, Codex and other skills-compatible agents, installed with `npx skills add alchaincyf/huashu-design`. It produces single-file HTML prototypes, HTML slide decks exportable to editable PPTX, timeline animations exported as MP4/GIF, infographics and 5-dimension design reviews. It adds a brand-asset protocol and a library of 60 HTML-native styles.
strengths: Works across skills-compatible agents: Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, OpenClaw, Hermes
Exports HTML decks to PPTX with real editable text boxes via html2pptx.js
Core render and export pipeline runs locally; cloud features are optional, in scripts/cloud/
Brand protocol extracts colors from official assets and writes brand-spec.md
weaknesses: Output is HTML; no layer-level export to Figma or Keynote
3D, physics and particle animation are out of scope
README says quality drops to 60-65 of 100 with no brand context
skills CLI 1.5.15 and older installs only SKILL.md, missing subdirectories

projects.name: superclaude_framework
projects.tagline: Slash commands, agents and modes that add structure to Claude Code
projects.summary: SuperClaude is a Python package that installs 30 `/sc:*` slash commands into Claude Code, along with 20 agent personas and 7 behavioral modes, all delivered as instruction files. It can also install 8 optional MCP servers (Tavily, Context7, Serena, Playwright and others) with `superclaude mcp`. Install is via pipx or an install script; a TypeScript plugin system is planned for v5.0 and is not available yet.
strengths: Installs with `pipx install superclaude` and `superclaude install`; `superclaude doctor` verifies it
30 slash commands cover brainstorming, implementation, testing, git, research and session save/load
MCP servers are optional; the framework works without them
MIT licensed, with docs for commands, agents, modes and flags
weaknesses: Targets Claude Code only; separate sibling projects exist for Gemini and Qwen
Claimed 2-3x speed and 30-50% token savings with MCPs come with no benchmark details
Plugin marketplace install is not available yet; v5.0 has no ETA
README mixes v4.1, v4.2 and v4.3 notes, and the research examples are unclear

projects.name: agency-agents-zh
projects.tagline: Chinese-language library of 277 role-based agent prompts for coding tools
projects.summary: Markdown agent definitions across 20 departments (executive, engineering, design, marketing, and others), each with a persona, workflow and deliverables. It is a Chinese community edition of msitarzewski/agency-agents: 213 translated roles plus China-market originals such as Xiaohongshu, Douyin, WeChat, Feishu and DingTalk. Shell scripts convert and install the files into 20 tools, including Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, Codex CLI and Gemini CLI.
strengths: Install script targets 20 tools, including Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, Codex CLI, Aider and Gemini CLI
Roles define persona, workflow and deliverables, not one-line prompts
Covers China-specific platforms and domains (Xiaohongshu, Douyin, WeChat, Feishu, DingTalk)
MIT license; files can be copied by hand into ~/.claude/agents/
weaknesses: Role content and docs are in Chinese; English is only linked to the upstream repo
Only Claude Code and Copilot install directly; other tools need convert.sh first
README counts disagree (277 total, 268 in gallery, 63 vs 64 originals)
README is dominated by sponsor and course promotion; quality of roles is unverified here

projects.name: trellis
projects.tagline: CLI that stores specs, tasks and session memory in your repo for coding agents
projects.summary: Trellis is an npm CLI that writes a `.trellis/` directory into your repo holding specs, task PRDs and per-developer journals, then injects the relevant context into coding agent sessions. It runs a four-phase loop (plan, implement, verify, finish) using skills and sub-agents, and generates platform-specific files for 22 AI coding platforms.
strengths: Specs, tasks and journals are plain files in the repo, reviewable like code
Same .trellis structure generated for 22 coding platforms, not just Claude Code
Verify step runs lint, type-check and tests against specs and self-fixes
Per-developer journals stay separate while shared specs live in git
weaknesses: AGPL-3.0 license may be a problem for some company use
Requires both Node.js >= 18 and Python >= 3.9
Needs upfront effort to write or draft specs to get value
No tagged release listed; versions only via npm

projects.name: brag
projects.tagline: Agent skill that renders a launch video for your project
projects.summary: /brag is an agent skill for Claude Code, Codex, opencode and other Agent Skills hosts. It reads the current project, plans a story and tone, then hands a brief to Hyperframes to render a short launch video with music, motion and share copy. Output goes to a brag-output/ folder with the plan, composition brief, share copy and brag.mp4.
strengths: Installs as a Claude Code or Codex plugin, or via npx skills for other agents
Writes plan, composition brief, share copy and brag.mp4 to one folder
Tone steerable with --tone; optional Kokoro voiceover with --voice
Bundled music and sound effects, plus a leaner /brag-slim variant
weaknesses: Full workflow depends on the Hyperframes CLI, Node.js 22+ and FFmpeg
/brag-slim is built for Claude Opus 5.5; README does not cover other models
Voiceover is off by default and needs an explicit flag
No tagged releases; README gives no render time or output spec

projects.name: fireworks-tech-graph
projects.tagline: Agent skill that generates validated SVG, PNG, GIF and HTML technical diagrams
projects.summary: A single Agent Skill for Codex and Claude Code that turns English or Chinese descriptions into SVG diagrams using a Python generator, then exports PNG, GIF motion and offline interactive HTML. It ships 12 visual styles and 14 diagram types (UML plus AI/agent patterns such as RAG and multi-agent), and checks geometry, routing and text fit before output.
strengths: Works in both Codex and Claude Code from one skill install
Deterministic validation of routing, crossings, spacing and labels before and after render
Exports SVG, PNG up to 4x, GIF and a single offline HTML file
12 styles and 14 diagram types including the full UML set
weaknesses: GIF animation only accepts SVGs carrying one of twelve approved motion contracts
PNG and GIF export need optional dependencies; Puppeteer path needs Node.js 22.12+
Style 8 (Dark Luxury) is AI-authored rather than generator-backed
README carries sponsor and paid-consulting sections

projects.name: skills
projects.tagline: Agent Skills for Google Cloud, GKE, BigQuery, Ads and Firebase
projects.summary: A repository of Agent Skills (Markdown skill folders) for Google products, mostly Google Cloud: GKE, BigQuery, AlloyDB, Cloud Run, IAM, SecOps, Genkit and the Gemini APIs. Install with `npx skills add google/skills`, choosing skills, target agents and project or global scope. It also bundles plugins (skills plus MCP servers) for Claude Code, Codex and Antigravity CLI.
strengths: Broad coverage: over 150 skills across GKE, data, security, ads and AI/ML
Installable per skill, per agent and per scope via npx skills
Plugin bundles for Claude Code, Codex and Antigravity CLI
Apache-2.0 licensed, with an issue tracker for skill content fixes
weaknesses: Focused on Google products; little use outside Google Cloud, Ads or Firebase
Documented install path requires Node.js and npx
No tagged releases; installs track the repository head
Some skills are marked Public Preview, such as the API Gateway MCP server

projects.name: agent-skills-for-context-engineering
projects.tagline: Collection of 18 Agent Skills on context and harness engineering for coding agents
projects.summary: A set of SKILL.md directories covering context fundamentals, compression, memory, tool design, multi-agent patterns, evaluation and harness design. It installs as a Claude Code plugin marketplace entry, an Open Plugins manifest for Cursor and Codex, or by copying single skill folders into .claude/skills, .cursor/skills or .codex/skills. Six worked examples and a router benchmark are included.
strengths: Installs via one /plugin command or by copying individual skill directories
Works across Claude Code, Cursor, Codex and other Open Plugins hosts
Skill router benchmarked: 600 calls per sweep across four models, with published results
Includes six worked examples, such as an LLM-as-judge TypeScript implementation with 19 tests
weaknesses: Skills are guidance text; scripts are Python pseudocode, not a runnable library
Router top-1 accuracy ranges 0.84 to 0.92 across tested models
Skill activation depends on the host agent's skill discovery
Some skills are labeled NEW and their maturity is unknown

projects.name: hallmark
projects.tagline: Design skill that steers coding agents away from generic AI-looking UI
projects.summary: Hallmark is a skill for Claude Code, Cursor and Codex that picks a page macrostructure for a brief, applies one of twenty-one themes, and runs fifty-seven slop-test gates plus a self-critique before returning output. It has four verbs: build (default), audit, redesign and study, which extracts design traits from a screenshot or URL. Output is self-contained HTML and CSS.
strengths: Works across Claude Code, Cursor and Codex from one SKILL.md plus references
Audit verb scores existing code and returns a punch list without editing
Twenty-one themes plus a Custom branch for briefs no theme fits
Live demo site and example pages are linked for each theme
weaknesses: Example output is static HTML and CSS; framework support is not documented
Cursor install needs manual copy into a .mdc rule without frontmatter
No benchmarks showing the slop-test gates improve output
No tagged releases

projects.name: security-audit-skill
projects.tagline: Coding-agent skill that runs a multi-phase security audit of a codebase
projects.summary: A skill for coding agents that audits a repository for vulnerabilities in six phases: reconnaissance, hunting, candidate validation, structured output, record verification and reporting. Isolated sub-agents hunt from a coverage ledger, and a fresh agent tries to disprove each candidate. Results go to findings.json, checked by Node validators, and to REPORT.md. It is the single-repo starting point for Cloudflare's vulnerability harness.
strengths: Separate agents find and validate each finding; verdicts are confirmed, needs_validation or rejected
Zero-dependency Node validators check findings.json and coverage-ledger.json against a schema
Attack-class prompts cover memory safety, web/auth, cloud, supply chain, client-side and LLM targets
Repeated runs reuse prior ledgers and findings to target coverage gaps
weaknesses: Needs a model with tool use and parallel sub-agents; token cost is unknown
Running target code requires an OS-enforced sandbox you must provide, else leads stay unvalidated
README says a single run found roughly half of what repeated runs found
No release published; install goes through the Skills CLI via npx

projects.name: autoharness
projects.tagline: Claude Code plugin that learns, merges and prunes its own skills from sessions
projects.summary: autoharness is a Claude Code plugin that distills skills from your real sessions into .claude/skills/, folds same-scenario skills together, and archives ones that stop being loaded. It only touches skills it wrote itself and injects a grouped index of them at session start. Reflection runs after a set number of tool calls (default 50), or on demand with /learn.
strengths: Touches only skills it generated; hand-written and installed skills are left alone
Each create/update logs reason and evidence slice to a per-skill ledger
Archives rather than deletes; moving a skill directory back revives it
Pure Python with zero third-party dependencies; tunable via AUTOHARNESS_* env variables
weaknesses: Requires python3 3.11+ on PATH; older interpreters turn the hooks off
Claude Code only; Linux and macOS only
README says default thresholds are placeholders pending empirical calibration
Background reflection spawns extra child sessions, adding token cost

projects.name: codex-plugin-cc
projects.tagline: Claude Code plugin that runs Codex reviews and delegates tasks
projects.summary: A Claude Code plugin that adds slash commands for running Codex code reviews and handing tasks to Codex without leaving Claude Code. It wraps the local Codex CLI and app server, so it reuses your existing Codex login, config.toml and base URL settings. Background jobs can be tracked and cancelled, and sessions can be resumed in Codex.
strengths: Reuses local Codex CLI auth and config.toml; no separate runtime
Read-only /codex:review and steerable /codex:adversarial-review with --base <ref>
Background jobs via /codex:status, /codex:result and /codex:cancel
Sessions can be continued in Codex with codex resume <session-id>
weaknesses: Requires Claude Code plus a ChatGPT subscription or OpenAI API key
Usage counts against Codex limits; optional review gate can drain them quickly
Multi-file reviews and rescue tasks can run long
/codex:transfer needs a Codex version that supports session import

projects.name: garden-skills
projects.tagline: Six Agent Skills for design, video, image and retrieval tasks
projects.summary: Garden Skills is a set of SKILL.md-format skills for Claude Code, Cursor, Codex and other coding agents. The six skills cover web video presentations (Vite, React, TypeScript, 23 themes, pluggable TTS), front-end design, GPT Image 2 prompting and generation, article formatting, code-rendered short video, and local knowledge retrieval. Install options include the skills CLI via npx, the Claude Code plugin marketplace, release zips, manual copy or a git submodule.
strengths: Follows the SKILL.md spec, so it works across Claude Code, Cursor and Codex
Five install paths, including pinned per-skill release zips
web-design-engineer ships 25 style recipes and a design direction advisor
gpt-image-2 includes 79 prompt templates and three runtime modes
weaknesses: Skills are narrow: design, video, images and articles, not general coding
gpt-image-2 local mode needs an image API; key setup not shown in the visible README
Built-in TTS providers are only MiniMax and OpenAI; others are paste-in snippets
README is truncated, so details of three skills (article, showreel, kb-retriever) are unknown

projects.name: frontend-slides
projects.tagline: Claude Code skill that generates HTML slide decks or converts PowerPoint files
projects.summary: A skill for Claude Code, packaged as a plugin, that builds single-file HTML presentations with inline CSS and JS. It shows three visual style previews to pick from, then writes the full deck, or extracts text, images and notes from a .pptx and rebuilds it for the web. Other coding agents can follow the same SKILL.md if they have filesystem and shell access.
strengths: Output is one HTML file with inline CSS/JS, no npm or build step
Converts .pptx files, extracting text, images and speaker notes
Ships 12 included styles plus 34 optional bold templates loaded on demand
Installs as a Claude Code plugin or by copying files into ~/.claude/skills
weaknesses: Plugin install flow and slash command are specific to Claude Code
Other agents must read SKILL.md manually; no install path is documented for them
Output is fixed 16:9 HTML, not editable .pptx
Style previews depend on the agent's generation, so results vary per run

projects.name: skills
projects.tagline: Agent Skills for Hugging Face Hub, training, evals and SageMaker deployment
projects.summary: A collection of about 24 Agent Skills folders (SKILL.md plus scripts) that teach coding agents Hugging Face workflows: Hub CLI operations, TRL and Unsloth fine-tuning, evals, Spaces, Gradio, Trackio and SageMaker deployment. Claude Code and Cursor marketplaces expose only hf-cli; other skills install with `hf skills add <name>`. A Gemini CLI extension and a generated AGENTS.md fallback are included.
strengths: Follows the Agent Skills format; works with Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI and Cursor
hf-cli skill is generated from the locally installed CLI, so commands stay current
Covers datasets, training, evals, Spaces, papers and SageMaker deployment
AGENTS.md fallback bundle for agents without skill support
weaknesses: Client marketplaces list only hf-cli; other skills need the hf CLI to install
Codex install is a manual copy or symlink into .agents/skills
Training skills target Hugging Face Jobs, a hosted service
Some skills overlap, such as huggingface-llm-trainer and trl-training

projects.name: ralph
projects.tagline: Bash loop that reruns Amp or Claude Code until every PRD story passes
projects.summary: Ralph is a bash script (ralph.sh) that repeatedly launches Amp or Claude Code with a fresh context, each time picking the highest-priority story in prd.json where passes is false. It implements one story, runs typecheck and tests, commits on success, and records learnings in progress.txt and AGENTS.md. It also ships prd and ralph skills for writing a PRD and converting it to prd.json.
strengths: Fresh context each iteration; state persists only in git, progress.txt and prd.json
Supports both Amp and Claude Code via a --tool flag
Small footprint: one shell script, prompt templates and two skills, plus jq
Installable as a Claude Code plugin marketplace entry
weaknesses: Needs working typecheck and tests; broken checks compound across iterations
Stories must fit one context window; large ones must be split by hand
Requires an authenticated Amp or Claude Code install, which are separate tools
No tagged releases; default cap is 10 iterations

projects.name: gsap-skills
projects.tagline: Official GSAP skills that teach coding agents correct animation API usage
projects.summary: Eight Agent Skills-format skill folders covering GSAP core tweens, timelines, ScrollTrigger, plugins, gsap.utils, React (useGSAP), performance, and Vue/Svelte lifecycle handling.
