Installs with `npx skills add` or the Claude Code plugin marketplace, and works with Cursor, Codex, Windsurf and others. Copilot gets a separate instructions file to copy by hand.
strengths: Maintained by the GSAP authors (greensock), so API guidance tracks the library
Eight skills split by topic: core, timeline, ScrollTrigger, plugins, utils, React, performance, frameworks
One install command via the skills CLI; Claude Code and Cursor plugin manifests included
Covers cleanup patterns such as useGSAP, gsap.context() and ScrollTrigger.refresh()
weaknesses: Only useful for GSAP; no effect on projects using other animation libraries
Copilot does not load skills; instructions must be copied manually
Instructs agents to recommend GSAP when no library is specified, which biases output
No tests or evals of skill effectiveness are described

projects.name: gitnexus
projects.tagline: Code knowledge graph exposed to coding agents through MCP tools
projects.summary: GitNexus indexes a repository with Tree-sitter into a LadybugDB graph of dependencies, call chains, clusters and execution flows. It serves that graph to agents such as Claude Code, Cursor and Codex through 19 MCP tools (impact, trace, query, rename, cypher and others), and installs skills and hooks. A browser Web UI offers graph exploration and chat.
strengths: Precomputes clusters and processes at index time, so impact returns callers and confidence in one call
One analyze command indexes, installs skills, registers Claude Code hooks and writes AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md
setup auto-detects editors; Claude Code and Codex get MCP, skills and pre/post tool hooks
CLI indexing runs locally with native Tree-sitter and persistent LadybugDB storage
weaknesses: PolyForm Noncommercial license restricts commercial use
Web UI in-browser mode is limited to about 5k files
npx install can crash on npm 11; some grammars need a C++ toolchain or are skipped
Render deploy costs about $35/month and the token is the only access control

projects.name: codegraph
projects.tagline: Local code knowledge graph served to coding agents over MCP
projects.summary: CodeGraph indexes a project into a local graph of symbols, call edges and dependencies under `.codegraph/`, then exposes it to coding agents through an MCP server. Agents can fetch relevant source, call paths and change impact in one call instead of grepping and reading files. `codegraph install` wires it into Claude Code, Cursor, Codex CLI, opencode, Gemini CLI, Kiro, GitHub Copilot and others, and auto-sync keeps the index current.
strengths: Runs locally; no Node.js needed, ships as a bundled installer or npm package
One `codegraph install` configures MCP for nine named agents and IDEs
Covers 30+ languages, including TypeScript, Python, Go, Rust, Java, C#, Swift
Watches files and updates the graph automatically; no manual re-index
weaknesses: README admits about 80% more retrieval context stays resident in long sessions
Published benchmarks are the author's, on 7 repos with one question each
No Docker or compose setup; install is via curl/PowerShell script or npm
Hosted CodeGraph platform is a waitlist product, separate from this repo

projects.name: chrome-devtools-mcp
projects.tagline: MCP server that lets coding agents drive and debug a live Chrome
projects.summary: chrome-devtools-mcp is an MCP server that gives coding agents such as Claude, Cursor and Copilot control of a live Chrome browser. It records performance traces through Chrome DevTools, inspects network requests and console messages with source-mapped stack traces, and automates page actions via puppeteer. A CLI is included for use without MCP, and a --slim mode exposes a smaller tool set.
strengths: Records DevTools performance traces and extracts insights from them
Puppeteer-based automation waits for action results automatically
Slim mode limits the exposed tools to basic browser tasks
Also ships a CLI for use without an MCP client
weaknesses: Usage statistics are sent to Google by default; opt out with --no-usage-statistics
Performance tools may send trace URLs to the Google CrUX API
Officially supports only Chrome and Chrome for Testing
Exposes all browser content to the connected MCP client

projects.name: codebase-memory-mcp
projects.tagline: Local MCP server that indexes code into a queryable knowledge graph
projects.summary: A native C MCP server that indexes functions, classes, imports and HTTP routes across 162 languages into a local graph, and exposes 17 tools (search, trace, impact analysis, Cypher queries, dead code detection) to coding agents such as Claude Code and Codex. Indexing and queries need no hosted service or API key. A browser UI, CBM Lens Beta, adds source reading, architecture maps and optional local chat, but it is only on main, not in v0.11.0.
strengths: Single native binary for macOS, Linux and Windows; no Docker, runtime or API key needed
162 tree-sitter grammars compiled in; hybrid LSP type resolution for 13 languages
Reports Linux kernel (28M LOC) indexed in about 3 minutes
Installer configures 45 detected agent client surfaces automatically
weaknesses: CBM Lens Beta is only on main; the current release ships the older graph UI
Token savings (120x, 10x) come from the project's own benchmarks
Preprint reports lower answer quality than file-by-file exploration (83% vs 92%)
Installer rewrites agent configs and a shared daemon requires identical builds across sessions

projects.name: github-mcp-server
projects.tagline: MCP server exposing GitHub repos, issues, PRs and Actions to AI tools
projects.summary: Official GitHub MCP server, written in Go, that lets MCP hosts read code, manage issues and pull requests, inspect Actions runs and review security alerts. It runs either as a GitHub-hosted remote endpoint (api.githubcopilot.com/mcp/) or locally over stdio via the ghcr.io Docker image or a binary built with go build. Authentication is OAuth or a personal access token.
strengths: Hosted remote endpoint needs no local install; local Docker image and Go build also available
Supports OAuth login or PAT; PAT takes precedence when set
Works with GitHub Enterprise Cloud (ghe.com) and Enterprise Server via GITHUB_HOST
Install guides for VS Code, Claude, Cursor, Windsurf, Zed, Codex and others
weaknesses: Enterprise Server is not supported by the remote server; local server only
Remote OAuth needs each host to configure a GitHub App or OAuth App
Local Docker OAuth needs a fixed callback port (8085) published to loopback
Only talks to GitHub; no other forges or providers

projects.name: serena
projects.tagline: MCP server giving coding agents symbol-level code search, editing and refactoring
projects.summary: Serena is an MCP server that gives a coding agent IDE-style tools: find symbol, find references, replace symbol body, rename, and a memory system. It uses language servers (over 40 languages) by default, or a paid JetBrains plugin that adds move, inline, type hierarchy and a debugger. It plugs into MCP clients such as Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and VSCode.
strengths: Symbol-level retrieval and editing instead of line numbers or text search
Language server backend is free and covers over 40 languages
Works with any MCP client, launched by command or run in HTTP mode
Layered YAML configuration: global, per-project, per-client contexts and modes
weaknesses: Move, inline, type hierarchy and debugging need the paid JetBrains plugin
Language server rename covers symbols only; some languages need extra installs
Application is GPL-3.0-or-later; only the SolidLSP component is MIT
Contributions require accepting a CLA

projects.name: code-review-graph
projects.tagline: Local Tree-sitter code graph served over MCP so agents read only affected files
projects.summary: Parses a repository with Tree-sitter into a SQLite graph of functions, classes, imports, calls, inheritance and tests, then serves blast-radius and review context to AI coding tools over MCP. A single install command detects and configures about 16 tools, including Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Windsurf and Zed. It also ships a GitHub Action that posts risk-scored PR comments, and updates the graph incrementally by SHA-256 hash.
strengths: One install command configures about 16 coding tools; uninstall leaves other config intact
Incremental re-parse by SHA-256; two-file edit on a ~3,000-file repo took about 2.5 s
Covers 30+ languages and notebooks, plus custom languages via languages.toml
Pinned-SHA benchmarks with a reproduction recipe; median 63x token reduction across 6 repos
weaknesses: Impact recall of 1.0 is circular, since ground truth comes from the same graph
Graph context can exceed a plain file read for small single-file edits
Search ranking needs work; Express queries can return no hits
Flow detection is strongest for Python and PHP/Laravel; JavaScript and Go are weaker

projects.name: context7
projects.tagline: MCP server and CLI that fetch current library docs into coding-agent prompts
projects.summary: Context7 looks up version-specific documentation and code examples for a library and places them in the agent's context. It runs as an MCP server (tools resolve-library-id and query-docs) or as a ctx7 CLI plus a skill, with no MCP needed. The repo holds the MCP server, CLI and SDKs; the API backend, parsing and crawling engines are private.
strengths: Two modes: MCP server tools, or ctx7 CLI with an installed skill
One command, npx ctx7 setup, configures Cursor, Claude Code or OpenCode
Version-aware lookups; prompts can pin a library ID such as /vercel/next.js
Also ships a TypeScript SDK and Vercel AI SDK tools
weaknesses: API backend, parser and crawler are private; only client code is open
Depends on the hosted service at mcp.context7.com; local run is a separate guide
API key recommended for higher rate limits; the limits are not stated
Indexed docs are community-contributed; README gives no accuracy guarantee

projects.name: unity-mcp
projects.tagline: MCP server that lets AI clients control the Unity Editor
projects.summary: A Unity package plus a Python MCP server that exposes 50 tool entrypoints for creating scenes and GameObjects, editing C# scripts, managing assets, running tests, profiling and building. It works with any MCP client, including Claude Desktop and Code, Cursor, VS Code, Windsurf, Cline and Gemini CLI. Installed through Unity Package Manager from a git URL or OpenUPM.
strengths: Covers scenes, scripts, assets, tests, profiling and builds in 50 tool entrypoints
Works with any MCP client; one menu action configures detected clients
Supports Unity 2021.3 LTS through 6.x
MIT licensed; docs cover multi-instance routing, tool groups and remote server auth
weaknesses: Requires Python 3.10+ via uv alongside the Unity install
Only targets the Unity Editor; no runtime or other engine support
Install tracks the main branch by default unless a version tag is pinned
Sponsored by a vendor that also sells a premium assistant, Aura for Unity

projects.name: cli-anything
projects.tagline: Generates command-line wrappers so AI agents can drive desktop and backend software
projects.summary: CLI-Anything runs a 7-phase generator inside a coding agent such as Claude Code, Cursor or Codex. It produces a Python (Click) CLI harness with JSON output and a SKILL.md for a target application or codebase. A companion package, cli-anything-hub, installs community-built CLIs from a registry, covering GIMP, Blender, LibreOffice, QGIS, n8n and others.
strengths: Ready-made registry of community CLIs installable with `cli-hub install <name>`
Generated CLIs emit structured JSON and ship a SKILL.md for agent discovery
Works with several agent hosts: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenClaw, Pi, OpenCode
Apache-2.0 license; README reports 2,461 passing tests
weaknesses: Many CLIs only wrap an upstream app, which must be installed separately
Generating a new CLI requires a supported AI coding agent, so output quality varies
Harness quality is per-CLI and community-contributed; test depth differs between harnesses
Windows use with Claude Code needs Git for Windows or WSL for bash and cygpath

projects.name: artemis
projects.tagline: Drives real Android phones from natural language via CLI, web console, SDK or MCP
projects.summary: ARTEMIS runs a multimodal agent that operates an Android device or emulator over ADB from plain-language instructions. It ships an MCP server for IDEs such as Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity and Windsurf, plus a CLI, a web console on port 8000 and a Python client. Two profiles exist: Flash, a reactive loop at about 3–5s per step, and Pro, a planner/operator/checker graph at about 15–40s per step.
strengths: Native MCP server with install commands for Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Windsurf and others
Flash and Pro profiles trade speed against planning and checkpoint verification
Falls back from accessibility tree to OCR and visual locating for Compose and Flutter UIs
Python client with no runtime dependencies for pytest or CI use
weaknesses: Android only; iOS support is a roadmap item
Installs an accessibility helper app on the phone at first task
Flash profile has no task plan, safety net, final report or ADB shell
Needs an external multimodal model; hardware and cost requirements are unknown

projects.name: claude-task-master
projects.tagline: Task manager that turns a PRD into tasks for AI coding agents
projects.summary: Task Master runs as an MCP server or CLI (task-master) and parses a PRD into structured tasks with dependencies, subtasks, tags and a research command. Editors such as Cursor, Windsurf, VS Code and Q CLI, plus Claude Code, call it to plan and pick the next task. It needs a provider API key (Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, Perplexity, xAI, OpenRouter and others) or the Claude Code or Codex CLI.
strengths: Works as an MCP server or CLI, installed with npx or npm
Separate main, research and fallback models across many providers
Claude Code and Codex CLI usable without an API key
TASK_MASTER_TOOLS limits loaded tools to 7, 15 or all 36
weaknesses: MIT with Commons Clause: no selling it or offering it as a hosted service
Default loads all 36 tools, about 21,000 tokens of context
Task quality depends on writing a detailed PRD first
AI commands need a provider API key or a Claude Code/Codex CLI login

projects.name: figma-context-mcp
projects.tagline: MCP server that feeds simplified Figma layout and style data to coding agents
projects.summary: Framelink MCP for Figma (npm package figma-developer-mcp) is an MCP server that fetches file, frame or group data from the Figma API. It trims the response to layout and styling information before passing it to the model, so the agent builds from structured data instead of screenshots. It runs via npx over stdio and needs a Figma personal access token.
strengths: Starts with one npx command; no install or build step needed
Trims Figma API responses to layout and styling to reduce model context
Works with MCP clients through a standard config entry, including Cursor
MIT licensed, written in TypeScript, with a docs site and demo video
weaknesses: Requires a Figma personal access token, passed as a CLI flag or env var
README says it is designed specifically for Cursor; other clients are not detailed
README does not list the exposed tools or parameters; docs are on an external site
One-shot accuracy claims are not backed by benchmarks in the README

projects.name: claude-context
projects.tagline: MCP server adding hybrid semantic code search to coding agents
projects.summary: Claude Context indexes a codebase into Milvus or Zilliz Cloud and exposes index_codebase, search_code, clear_index and get_indexing_status tools over stdio MCP. Search combines BM25 with dense vectors, chunks code with an AST splitter, and re-indexes only changed files using Merkle trees. It works with Claude Code, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, Cursor and other MCP clients.
strengths: Hybrid BM25 plus dense vector search over an indexed repo
Incremental re-indexing of changed files via Merkle trees
Embedding choice: OpenAI, VoyageAI, Ollama or Gemini
Also ships a core npm package and a VS Code extension
weaknesses: Needs a Milvus or Zilliz Cloud instance; no embedded vector store mentioned
Default setup sends code to OpenAI for embeddings unless Ollama is configured
README claims ~40% token reduction from its own evaluation only
No tagged releases listed on the repository

projects.name: pal-mcp-server
projects.tagline: MCP server that lets Claude Code, Codex CLI and Cursor call multiple LLMs
projects.summary: PAL is a Python MCP server that exposes tools such as chat, thinkdeep, planner, consensus, codereview, precommit and debug to a host CLI or IDE, and routes each call to a chosen model from Gemini, OpenAI, Azure, X.AI, OpenRouter, DIAL or Ollama. It keeps conversation threads across tools and models, and its clink tool launches other CLIs (Gemini CLI, Codex, Claude Code) as subagents with role prompts.
strengths: Works with many hosts: Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Codex CLI, Qwen CLI, Cursor
Supports Gemini, OpenAI, Azure, X.AI, OpenRouter, DIAL and local Ollama models
Conversation threading carries context across models and after host context resets
clink spawns other CLIs as isolated subagents with roles like planner and codereviewer
weaknesses: Needs at least one provider API key or a local Ollama setup
Each enabled tool adds to the context window; six tools are disabled by default
License is reported as NOASSERTION, so terms need manual checking
Last commit was 2025-12-15, so recent model releases may lack support

projects.name: open-code-review
projects.tagline: CLI that reviews Git diffs with an LLM agent and line-level comments
projects.summary: Open Code Review is a Go CLI (`ocr`) that reads a Git diff, groups related files into bundles, and runs each bundle through a tool-using LLM agent that produces structured review comments. File selection, rule matching, comment positioning and reflection are done by deterministic code rather than prompts. `ocr scan` reviews whole files when there is no diff, and delegation mode lets an existing coding agent do the review with its own model.
strengths: Deterministic file selection and bundling; each bundle runs as an isolated sub-agent
Reviews workspace changes, branch ranges, single commits, or full files via `ocr scan`
Sessions can be resumed and browsed in a viewer; JSON output for automation
Plugins for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Kimi Code, OpenCode; CI docs for GitHub, GitLab, Gerrit
weaknesses: Requires Git >= 2.41 and a configured LLM endpoint, unless delegation mode is used
Recall is lower than general-purpose agents by the README's own benchmark
Benchmark figures are published by the project itself, not independently verified
No Docker or Compose files detected

projects.name: front-end-checklist
projects.tagline: Front-end rules checklist with an MCP server for agent code review
projects.summary: A corpus of 386 English front-end rules across 11 categories (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, performance, accessibility, SEO, security, images, testing, privacy, i18n), each with a priority level, remediation guidance and verification steps. It is readable on the website or in the README, and a hosted MCP server and installable skills let agents review code or audit public URLs against the same rules.
strengths: 386 rules with Critical/High/Medium/Low priorities, grouped into 11 categories
Hosted MCP server exposes 11 tools, including review_code, search_rules and audit_url
Skills install with `npx skills add frontendchecklist/skills`, global or per rule
MIT licensed; rules also usable as a plain README checklist without any tooling
weaknesses: Content repo, not a linter: findings come from an agent applying the rules
audit_url only handles public https:// pages
Security, privacy and i18n categories are thin (22, 5 and 5 rules)
MCP tool discovery can be lazy in some clients; the prompt must name the server

projects.name: pr-agent
projects.tagline: LLM pull request reviewer that comments via /review, /describe and /improve
projects.summary: PR-Agent runs as a GitHub Action, CLI, Docker image or webhook service and posts AI-generated descriptions, reviews, code suggestions and Q&A on pull requests. Each tool makes a single LLM call, and a compression strategy handles large diffs. It supports GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Azure DevOps and Gitea, and any model reachable through LiteLLM.
strengths: Supports GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Azure DevOps and Gitea
Model-agnostic via LiteLLM: OpenAI, Claude, Gemini, Bedrock, Ollama and others
One LLM call per tool, about 30 seconds per command
Review behavior is configurable through a TOML settings file and JSON prompts
weaknesses: Described as a community-maintained legacy project of Qodo
/help_docs is disabled since v0.36.1 over a credential-exposure issue
Needs your own LLM API key and per-provider setup
Docker images moved to pragent/pr-agent from 0.34.2, so pinned references break

projects.name: screenshot-to-code
projects.tagline: Turns screenshots and mockups into Tailwind, React or Vue code
projects.summary: Takes a screenshot, mockup, Figma export or screen recording and generates HTML with Tailwind or CSS, React, Vue, Bootstrap or Ionic code using Gemini 3, GPT-5.5 or Claude Opus models, with Replicate for image generation and background removal. Runs as a React/Vite frontend on port 5173 and a FastAPI backend on 7001, or via docker-compose. For developers prototyping UIs from designs.
strengths: Six output stacks including React, Vue, Bootstrap and Ionic with Tailwind
Video mode turns a screen recording into a working prototype (needs Gemini)
Optional headless Chromium lets the agent render and check its own output
docker-compose brings up frontend and backend with one env file
weaknesses: Requires at least one OpenAI, Anthropic or Gemini API key; no bundled local model
Ollama models are possible but the README calls the results poor quality
Replicate key must be set in backend/.env, not in the UI
Docker setup has no hot reload; file changes need a rebuild

projects.name: Onlook
projects.tagline: Visual editor that edits Next.js and Tailwind apps with AI
projects.summary: Browser-based editor that loads a Next.js and Tailwind project into a web container, renders it in an iframe and maps DOM elements back to source so you can drag, restyle and edit visually or through an AI chat. Built on Next.js, tRPC, Supabase, Drizzle and the Vercel AI SDK with OpenRouter for models and CodeSandbox for sandboxes. For designers and front-end developers working on Next.js codebases.
strengths: Edits map directly to code; right-click any element to open its source location
Branching, checkpoints and a real-time code editor beside the visual canvas
Apache-2.0 with Dockerfile and compose file for local runs
Figma-like layers, pages, brand tokens and asset management
weaknesses: Next.js plus Tailwind only; other frameworks are roadmap items, not supported
Depends on hosted services: Supabase, OpenRouter, CodeSandbox SDK, Freestyle
Team comments, MCP support and image references are unchecked roadmap items
Maintainers are moving to a hosted early-access product; last commit July 2026

projects.name: agents.md
projects.tagline: Open Markdown format for giving coding agents project instructions
projects.summary: AGENTS.md is a specification for a plain Markdown file kept in a repo that holds dev environment, testing and PR instructions for AI coding agents. The repository also contains the Next.js site served at agents.md, which explains the format and lists examples. It has no runtime or agent code.
strengths: Plain Markdown, no tooling, schema or dependencies required
One predictable file location for agent instructions, separate from the human README
Website runs locally with pnpm install and pnpm run dev
weaknesses: No enforced schema; README shows only a minimal example
Repo holds the website and spec, not a tool or agent
README does not list which agents read the file
No releases published

projects.name: appwrite
projects.tagline: Self-hostable backend with auth, databases, storage, functions, messaging and hosting
projects.summary: Appwrite is a backend platform that bundles Auth, Databases, Storage, Functions, Sites, Messaging, Realtime and a Firewall behind REST, GraphQL and WebSocket APIs. It runs as a managed cloud or self-hosted via a Docker installer, and offers a hosted MCP server so coding agents can operate on a live project. Client and server SDKs cover Web, Flutter, Apple, Android, React Native, Unity, Node.js, Python, PHP, Go, Rust and others.
strengths: One Docker-based installer sets up the full stack, with Compose and env files also published
SDKs for 6 client and 10 server platforms, plus REST, GraphQL and Realtime APIs
Hosted MCP server uses OAuth, so no API keys are needed on Cloud
Same product runs on managed Cloud or on your own infrastructure
weaknesses: Installer needs access to the Docker socket on the host
Self-hosted instances must use a separate local MCP server, not the hosted one
Hybrid monolith-plus-workers architecture means many services to operate
RAM and CPU requirements are not stated in the README

projects.name: supabase
projects.tagline: Postgres backend with auth, storage, realtime and edge functions
projects.summary: Supabase bundles a Postgres database with generated REST and GraphQL APIs, JWT-based auth, S3-backed file storage, realtime change feeds over websockets, and edge functions. It also includes a vector and embeddings toolkit for AI workloads. It runs as a hosted platform, can be self-hosted, or run locally, and has official clients for JavaScript, Flutter, Swift and Python.
strengths: Built on Postgres, PostgREST, GoTrue and Realtime, so the data layer is plain SQL
Official clients for JavaScript/TypeScript, Flutter, Swift and Python
Hosted, self-hosted and local development options
Apache-2.0 license; vector and embeddings toolkit included
weaknesses: Many separate services to run when self-hosting; README gives no resource requirements
Go, Java, Rust, Ruby and C# clients are community-maintained, some partial
Repo has no Docker or compose files; self-hosting is documented elsewhere

projects.name: parse-server
projects.tagline: Node.js backend with REST and GraphQL APIs on MongoDB or PostgreSQL
projects.summary: Parse Server is a self-hosted backend that runs on Node.js, either standalone via the parse-server CLI or mounted on an Express app. It exposes REST and GraphQL APIs backed by MongoDB or PostgreSQL (with PostGIS), and adds Cloud Code, Live Query, push notifications, file adapters and per-key access scopes. Official Parse SDKs cover the major client platforms.
strengths: Runs standalone or embedded in an existing Express app
Supports both MongoDB (7, 8) and PostgreSQL (16-18) with PostGIS
Includes Cloud Code, Live Query, GraphQL, push and pluggable file storage adapters
Fine-grained access scopes: master, read-only master, session and maintenance keys
weaknesses: No built-in admin UI in this repo; a separate dashboard project is needed
Requires you to provision and operate your own MongoDB or PostgreSQL
Docker image must be built from the repo; README shows no prebuilt image or compose file
Node.js version support is tied to specific majors and shifts with each release

projects.name: graphql-engine
projects.tagline: GraphQL API layer over Postgres, MongoDB, ClickHouse and SQL Server
projects.summary: Hasura GraphQL Engine exposes data from PostgreSQL and its flavors, MongoDB, ClickHouse and MS SQL Server through a single GraphQL endpoint. Custom business logic can be added with TypeScript, Python and Go connector SDKs. The repo is a mono-repo holding the V3 engine (which powers Hasura DDN) and the stable V2 engine, with all data connectors open source.
strengths: Supports PostgreSQL, MongoDB, ClickHouse and MS SQL Server as data sources
Connector SDKs in TypeScript, Python and Go for custom logic
Core engines and data connectors are Apache-2.0 licensed
V2 remains available as the current stable version
weaknesses: Large mono-repo with long history; README recommends shallow or sparse clones
V2 and V3 are separate codebases with separate docs
V3 is documented around the hosted Hasura DDN workflow
README lists no RAM, port or AI model details

projects.name: spacetimedb
projects.tagline: Relational database that runs your app logic as modules and syncs clients live
projects.summary: SpacetimeDB is a relational database that doubles as the application server. You write tables and reducers as a module in Rust, C#, TypeScript or C++, upload it, and clients connect directly, subscribe to tables and receive committed changes automatically. State is held in memory with an on-disk commit log for durability, and reducers run as ACID transactions.
strengths: Replaces the API server and pub/sub layer: clients subscribe to tables and get pushed updates
Module languages: Rust, C#, TypeScript, C++; client SDKs include React hooks, Unity and Unreal
Reducers are ACID transactions; confirmed reads wait for commit log durability by default
Used for the full backend of the MMORPG BitCraft Online
weaknesses: BSL 1.1 license, converting to AGPL v3.0 with linking exception after a few years
Aimed at low-latency transactional workloads, not batch or analytical queries
Application logic lives inside the database, tying the app to its module model
RAM requirements are unknown, though all application state is held in memory

projects.name: insforge
projects.tagline: Postgres-based backend platform that coding agents operate through an MCP server
projects.summary: InsForge bundles Postgres, auth, S3-compatible storage, edge functions, an OpenAI-compatible model gateway and site deployment behind an MCP server. Coding agents read docs, schemas and logs, and run migrations, deploy functions and create buckets as tools. Self-hosting uses Docker Compose with generated secrets; a hosted cloud edition also exists.
strengths: Covers auth, Postgres, storage, edge functions and model gateway in one stack
MCP server exposes schemas, logs and config so agents can verify their own work
Setup script generates JWT, encryption and database secrets into a mode 600 .env
Storage can use local disk, bundled MinIO or RustFS, or any S3-compatible store
weaknesses: CLI + Skills interface is cloud only; self-hosted gets the MCP server only
Compute (long-running containers) is in private preview
Resource requirements such as RAM are not documented in the README
Running several instances needs manual per-project names and port overrides

projects.name: payload
projects.tagline: Next.js-native headless CMS and app framework with a React admin panel
projects.summary: Payload installs into an existing Next.js /app folder and provides a TypeScript headless CMS with auth, versions and drafts, localization, and a customizable React admin. Server components can query the database directly without REST or GraphQL. The README lists website and ecommerce templates plus one-click deploys to Vercel (Neon, Vercel Blob) and Cloudflare (Workers, R2, D1).
strengths: Installs inside an existing Next.js /app folder, so frontend and backend share one codebase
Auth, versions and drafts, localization, and field-level access control are built in
Generates TypeScript types for your data; hooks exist at document and field level
One-click deploy to Vercel (Neon, Blob) or Cloudflare (Workers, R2, D1)
weaknesses: README does not mention built-in AI features; it is a general CMS
Tied to Next.js and TypeScript for its native setup
Supported databases and minimum resources are not stated in the README
v2 to v3 required a migration guide, so older projects need upgrade work

projects.name: convex-backend
projects.tagline: Reactive database with TypeScript server functions and client libraries
projects.summary: Convex is a reactive database where queries and mutations are written as TypeScript server functions, with client libraries that keep app data live-updating. The backend is a Rust codebase with a JS runtime for user-defined functions. It can be used on Convex's cloud platform or self-hosted with Docker or a prebuilt binary, and the self-hosted version includes the dashboard and CLI.
strengths: Server logic and queries written in plain TypeScript with strong consistency
Self-hosted build includes the dashboard and CLI, with Docker or prebuilt binary options
Works with external databases such as Postgres, SQLite and RDS when self-hosting
Repository is synced with internal development within a handful of days
weaknesses: Test frameworks, including randomized tests, are not included in the open source repo
Self-hosted builds send an anonymous beacon unless started with --disable-beacon
Less tested on Windows than on Linux and Mac
License is not identified as a standard SPDX license (NOASSERTION)

projects.name: apijson
projects.tagline: Java ORM that exposes CRUD APIs over JSON requests without per-endpoint code
projects.summary: APIJSON is a Java library and JSON-based protocol. Clients send a JSON describing the tables and fields they want, and the server maps it to SQL and returns JSON in the same shape, so backend developers write no per-endpoint CRUD code. It covers reads, writes, fuzzy search and remote function calls, and ships with API docs and test tooling (APIAuto).
strengths: One JSON request can query several related tables, replacing multiple endpoint calls
Many data sources listed: MySQL, PostgreSQL, Oracle, SQL Server, ClickHouse, Redis, Kafka, Elasticsearch
Added via Maven or Gradle through JitPack; works with Spring, SpringBoot, JFinal, Nutz
Community ports listed for Go, C#, PHP, Node.js, Python and Rust
weaknesses: Java-centric; non-Java ports are separate third-party repositories with unknown maturity
License is reported as NOASSERTION, so terms need checking before use
README gives no setup steps for a standalone server; points to a separate demo repo
Not AI-specific; it is a general ORM and API protocol

projects.name: dokploy
projects.tagline: Self-hosted PaaS for deploying apps and databases on your own servers
projects.summary: Dokploy deploys applications (Node.js, PHP, Python, Go, Ruby and others) and Docker Compose stacks to a VPS, with Traefik handling routing and load balancing. It also creates MySQL, PostgreSQL, MongoDB, MariaDB, libsql and Redis databases, with scheduled backups to external storage. Multi-node scaling uses Docker Swarm, and remote servers can be managed from one instance. It has no AI-specific features; it is a general hosting layer.
strengths: Installs on a VPS with a single curl script
Built-in database provisioning and automated backups to external storage
Multi-node via Docker Swarm and remote server management
CLI and API, plus notifications via Slack, Discord, Telegram and Email
weaknesses: Not AI-specific; no model serving or LLM features
License is not identified by GitHub (NOASSERTION); check the license file
Requires Docker; Swarm clustering adds operational overhead
Minimum RAM and web port are not stated in the README

projects.name: dokku
projects.tagline: Self-hosted mini-Heroku PaaS that deploys apps with git push
projects.summary: Dokku is a small Platform-as-a-Service that runs on a single Ubuntu or Debian VM and builds and runs applications in Docker containers. Applications are deployed over SSH, and the server is managed through the `dokku` command line, including domains and SSH keys. The README describes it as a Docker-powered mini-Heroku and does not mention any AI features.
strengths: Installs on a single VM with one bootstrap script
Supports Ubuntu 22.04/24.04/26.04 and Debian 11+ on amd64 and arm64
MIT license, with an active release history and Ubuntu and Arch packages
Written in Go, with documentation and a Slack support channel
weaknesses: Not an AI project; the README has no AI or model features
Targets one server; the README describes no multi-node setup
Only Ubuntu and Debian are listed as supported operating systems
Deployment and management are CLI and SSH based; the README mentions no web UI

projects.name: OpenClaw
projects.tagline: Personal assistant gateway that answers in Discord, Slack, WhatsApp and Telegram
projects.summary: OpenClaw runs a local Gateway that connects one assistant to Discord, iMessage, Slack, Teams, Telegram, WhatsApp and 20+ other channels, plus native apps for macOS, iOS, Android, Windows and Linux. Model providers and agent harnesses (Claude, Codex, local models) are swappable plugins; state, memory and credentials stay on the host. The same Gateway serves one person or a team, differing only in configuration.
strengths: Channels for Discord, iMessage, Slack, Teams, Telegram, WhatsApp and 20+ more from one Gateway
Native companion apps on macOS, iOS, Android, Windows and Linux add voice, camera and screen
No paid tier or hosted service; stewarded by a 501(c)(3) foundation
Model providers and agent harnesses are plugins; swap Claude, Codex or local models
weaknesses: Tools run on the host for the main session unless sandboxing is configured
Requires Node 24.16+ or 26.1+; the repo is pnpm-only, plain npm install is unsupported
Daily version check phones home by default; disable with update.checkOnStart: false

projects.name: nanobot
projects.tagline: Self-hosted Python personal agent with WebUI, TUI and chat-app channels
projects.summary: nanobot is a Python agent framework you run yourself and use from a browser WebUI, a terminal TUI, or chat apps such as Telegram, Discord, Slack and Email. It keeps session history and long-term memory (Dream), runs shell, web, MCP and cron tools, and supports long-running goals. It also exposes a Python SDK and an OpenAI-compatible API, and needs an external model provider or local server.
strengths: Many channels: Telegram, Discord, Slack, WeChat, Email, Mattermost, Linear, Teams, Feishu
Built-in long-term memory, cron automations and /goal long-running tasks
Works with OpenAI-compatible APIs, Ollama and vLLM, with fallback models
Installs via script, uv or pip; Python SDK and OpenAI-compatible API included
weaknesses: Supplies no model; needs a provider account or local model server
Background gateway does not restart after reboot or crash without an OS service
Interrupted subagent tasks and missed scheduled runs are not replayed after restart
Source install needs Git and Bun; native TUI wheels cover limited platforms

projects.name: openhuman
projects.tagline: Rust agent harness with desktop app, built-in memory and embeddable library
projects.summary: OpenHuman is a single-process Rust agent harness shipped as a desktop app (macOS, Windows, Linux), a terminal app, a headless server and an embeddable Rust crate. It bundles memory recalled with citations, browser and desktop control, MCP and skills, 14 messaging channels, durable workflows, and local or BYOK models. The README reports its own benchmark on ten SWE-bench tasks and claims 500 agents fit on a $10 VPS; it is labelled early beta.
strengths: Embeds as a typed Rust library, no sidecar or daemon needed
Public benchmark repo; reports 68 MB peak memory and 19.8 s median task time
Local models (Ollama, LM Studio, MLX) or BYOK across 26 providers
Approval gate, OS-jail or Docker sandboxing, secrets stored in OS keyring
weaknesses: Labelled early beta; README warns of rough edges
Benchmark is self-run on only ten tasks
GPL-3.0 license constrains embedding in proprietary products
119 OAuth app integrations go through Composio, an external service

projects.name: Hermes Agent
projects.tagline: Terminal and chat-app agent that writes its own skills and remembers you
projects.summary: Hermes Agent is a Python agent with a terminal UI and a gateway for Telegram, Discord, Slack, WhatsApp, Signal and email. It creates skills from completed tasks, keeps agent-curated memory, searches past sessions with FTS5, runs cron jobs and spawns subagents; tools execute locally or in Docker, SSH, Modal, Daytona or Vercel Sandbox. Works with Nous Portal, OpenRouter, OpenAI or a custom endpoint.
strengths: Seven execution backends: local, Docker, SSH, Singularity, Modal, Daytona and Vercel Sandbox
Built-in cron scheduler delivers results to any connected messaging platform
Imports settings, memories, skills and API keys from an existing OpenClaw install
MCP server support plus 40+ built-in tools grouped into toolsets
weaknesses: Installer pulls Python 3.14, Node.js, npm, ripgrep and FFmpeg onto the host
No bundled browser UI; interfaces are the TUI and the messaging gateway
Web search, image generation, TTS and cloud browser steer toward the paid Nous Portal
Antivirus on Windows may quarantine the bundled uv.exe; whitelisting is documented

projects.name: career-ops
projects.tagline: Job-search agent that scores postings against your CV and drafts applications
projects.summary: Runs inside an AI coding CLI (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Qwen and others). You paste a job URL or text and it checks the posting is still live, scores fit against your CV, and drafts a tailored ATS PDF, cover letter and form answers. It never submits or sends anything; data stays local apart from calls to the AI provider you choose. It also has a portal scanner, a terminal dashboard and batch evaluation.
strengths: Drafts only: no auto-submit and no mail transport in the code, per the README
No telemetry or backend; CV goes only to your chosen AI provider
Portal scanner preconfigured for 100+ companies across Ashby, Greenhouse, Lever and Wellfound
Works with several AI CLIs and can use local or free-tier models
weaknesses: Requires an AI CLI and a model provider; output quality depends on the model
README says early runs are rough until it learns your profile
CV rewording check cannot catch every fabrication; manual review required
Playwright Chromium needed for PDF generation

projects.name: ZeroClaw
projects.tagline: Single Rust binary agent runtime with 30+ channels and hardware access
projects.summary: ZeroClaw is one Rust binary that routes messages from 30+ channels (Discord, Telegram, Matrix, email, voice, webhooks, CLI) to an agent loop backed by Anthropic, OpenAI, Ollama or any OpenAI-compatible provider, with fallback chains. Tools cover shell, browser, HTTP, MCP servers and GPIO/I2C/SPI/USB on Raspberry Pi, STM32 and ESP32. Supervised autonomy, OS sandboxes and signed tool receipts gate each action.
strengths: Default supervised mode: medium-risk operations need approval, high-risk ones are blocked
Hardware peripherals on Raspberry Pi, STM32, Arduino and ESP32 via a Peripheral trait
HTTP/WebSocket gateway plus web dashboard for chat, memory, config and cron
Dual-licensed MIT or Apache-2.0; installs as systemd, launchctl or Windows service
weaknesses: Hand-written TOML config; a minimal V3 config needs four sections before it runs
README states no RAM figures and no gateway port
Unix installer places the binary under the Cargo bin directory

projects.name: cowagent
projects.tagline: Self-hosted agent assistant with memory, skills and many chat channels
projects.summary: CowAgent is a Python agent that plans tasks, calls built-in tools (file I/O, bash, browser, scheduler, web search) and MCP servers, and replies through Web, Telegram, Slack, Discord, WeChat, Feishu, DingTalk, QQ and other channels. It keeps three-tier long-term memory, a Markdown knowledge base, installable skills and multi-agent teams. Models are configured per capability from a web console on port 9899.
strengths: Many channels at once: Web, Telegram, Slack, Discord, WeChat, Feishu, DingTalk, QQ, WeCom
Chat, vision, image generation, ASR, TTS and embeddings can route to different providers
MCP support over stdio, SSE and Streamable HTTP, plus a skill hub and GitHub skill installs
Three-tier memory with nightly distillation and hybrid keyword and vector retrieval
weaknesses: Agent mode uses substantially more tokens than plain chat, per the README
Local models only via the Custom provider, which lists chat support only
Console is reachable externally once web_host is 0.0.0.0, so a password is needed
Hosted runtime and enterprise features are tied to the vendor's LinkAI service

projects.name: IronClaw
projects.tagline: Rust assistant that sandboxes every untrusted tool in WebAssembly
projects.summary: IronClaw is a Rust take on the OpenClaw idea that runs untrusted tools in WebAssembly sandboxes with capability permissions, endpoint allowlists, host-side credential injection and leak scans. It exposes a REPL, HTTP webhooks, Telegram and Slack channels and a browser gateway with SSE/WebSocket streaming, runs cron and event routines, connects to MCP servers and keeps hybrid-search memory in PostgreSQL.
strengths: WASM sandbox with per-tool rate, memory, CPU and time limits
Secrets encrypted with AES-256-GCM, never exposed to tool code; full audit log
Describe a tool in chat and IronClaw builds it as a WASM module
No telemetry; onboard installs a background service on macOS and Linux
weaknesses: Requires PostgreSQL for persistence; SQLite is not an option
Installer needs a release tag chosen by hand; no latest channel
Slack and Telegram are configured only through the WebUI Extensions page
Windows has no background service; WebUI runs in the foreground via ironclaw serve

projects.name: airi
projects.tagline: Self-hosted AI virtual character with voice, VRM/Live2D avatars and game-playing
projects.summary: AIRI is an attempt to re-create Neuro-sama as a self-owned digital companion. It runs as a web app, an Electron desktop app (Tamagotchi) and a Capacitor mobile app (Pocket), and drives VRM or Live2D avatars with speech input, multi-provider TTS and an LLM backend. It can chat on Discord and Telegram and play Minecraft and Factorio, and the README describes it as early-stage.
strengths: Runs in browser, desktop (Electron) and mobile (PWA/Capacitor) from one TypeScript monorepo
Supports 25+ LLM providers including Ollama, vLLM, SGLang, OpenAI, Anthropic and Gemini
Controls VRM and Live2D avatars with auto blink, look-at and idle eye movement
Connectors for Discord voice and text, Telegram, Minecraft and Factorio
weaknesses: README states development is at an early stage
Long-term memory (Memory Alaya) and in-browser WebGPU inference are unfinished
Factorio and Helldivers 2 support are WIP or proof of concept
No Docker or compose setup; self-hosting means building with pnpm or using release binaries

projects.name: AstrBot
projects.tagline: Chatbot platform bridging LLMs to QQ, Telegram, Discord, Slack and more
projects.summary: AstrBot is a Python 3.12+ chatbot platform that connects LLM providers (OpenAI-compatible, Anthropic, Gemini, DeepSeek, Ollama, LM Studio) to QQ, OneBot, Telegram, WeCom, Feishu, DingTalk, Slack, Discord, LINE, KOOK, Misskey and Mattermost. It adds a WebUI, web chat, MCP, skills, a knowledge base, personas and a code sandbox, and can hand conversations to Dify or Coze. Installs via uv or Docker.
strengths: 14 officially maintained messaging adapters, including QQ, Feishu, DingTalk and WeCom
1000+ plugins installable from the built-in marketplace
Agent sandbox isolates code and shell execution per session
STT and TTS providers built in: Whisper, SenseVoice, Edge TTS, GPT-SoVITS, Azure and more
weaknesses: AGPL-3.0 license
WhatsApp adapter still marked coming soon
Docker setup is documented only in the external docs, not the README
Several model-provider links in the README are referral or affiliate links

projects.name: QwenPaw
projects.tagline: Personal AI agent with memory, skills, and chat-channel connectors
projects.summary: QwenPaw is a personal agent runtime installed with pip, a script, Docker, or a desktop app, with a web Console on port 8088 and a terminal UI. It keeps layered memory as Markdown via ReMe, runs skills, plugins, and MCP tools, and replies through DingTalk, Lark, WeChat, Discord, Telegram, iMessage, and QQ. Models can be local (built-in runtime, Ollama, LM Studio) or any of 14+ cloud providers.
strengths: One instance serves DingTalk, Lark, WeChat, Discord, Telegram, iMessage, and QQ
Works with Ollama, LM Studio, a built-in local runtime, or 14+ cloud providers
Sandbox, Tool Guard, File Guard, and Skill Scanner gate commands before they run
Supports MCP, plus ACP for cross-system agent orchestration
weaknesses: Requires Python 3.11 to below 3.14 for the pip install path
Desktop app is beta and the macOS build is not notarized
RAM and VRAM requirements are unknown; the README does not state them
Major versions shipped monthly since 2.0, so expect fast-changing behavior

projects.name: nanoclaw
projects.tagline: Small personal assistant that runs each agent in its own Linux container
projects.summary: NanoClaw is a self-hosted assistant built on the Claude Agent SDK. A single Node host routes messages from channels such as Slack, Telegram, Discord and WhatsApp to per-agent containers, exchanging them through two SQLite files per session. Channels and alternative providers are installed per fork with /add-<name> skills, and customization is done by changing code with Claude Code rather than editing config files.
strengths: Agents run in Docker containers and only see explicitly mounted directories
Credentials are injected by a gateway, so agents never hold raw API keys
Small codebase: one host process, no microservices, two SQLite files per session
Per-agent-group memory, CLAUDE.md and scheduled tasks; many channels via skills
weaknesses: Default setup depends on Claude Code and an Anthropic credential
No config files or dashboard; customization and debugging go through Claude Code
Channels and non-Claude providers are not in trunk; each needs a skill install
Prebuilt hardened image and managed Slack app require a free account

projects.name: invisible_dots
projects.tagline: Self-hosted agent that works on its own VM desktop with a patched Firefox
projects.summary: invisible_dots runs each agent (a "Dot") on its own hardware-accelerated QEMU VM with a Linux desktop, persistent disk and a patched Firefox that keeps per-identity logins. Dots write their own notes and skills, accept MCP servers, queue tasks and recurring automations, and gate tools with allow/ask/deny permissions. It is reachable via web UI, CLI, HTTP API, Telegram and optional WhatsApp, and uses an OpenRouter key for models. Status is alpha.
strengths: Each Dot gets its own VM with desktop, persistent disk and sleep/wake on demand
Per-tool allow/ask/deny permissions, with pending asks kept in an Inbox across restarts
Accepts user-declared MCP servers and reaches the agent via web, CLI, API, Telegram
Crash-safe: accepted messages and tasks survive kill -9, and cut-short tool calls are not rerun
weaknesses: Marked alpha in the README badge
Requires x86-64 hardware virtualization plus Node 24+, Go 1.25+ and QEMU
No Docker or Compose files; setup is built from source
Model access documented only via an OpenRouter key; local models not mentioned

projects.name: Moltis
projects.tagline: Persistent personal agent server in one Rust binary with sandboxed execution
projects.summary: Moltis is a single Rust binary that serves a web UI (port 13131), Telegram, Signal, Discord, Slack, Teams, Matrix, WhatsApp and Nostr from one gateway, and runs every command in a Docker, Podman or WASM sandbox. It keeps memory in SQLite with full-text and vector search, supports MCP (stdio and HTTP/SSE), ACP, cron, CalDAV and email, 8 TTS and 7 STT providers, and password, passkey and API-key auth.
strengths: Every command runs in a Docker, Podman, Apple Container or WASM sandbox
Passkey (WebAuthn), password and API-key auth; vault encrypted with XChaCha20-Poly1305
Signed releases with Sigstore attestations and GPG; verifiable with gh attestation
Langfuse, OTLP and Prometheus instrumentation built in
weaknesses: Docker deployment mounts the host Docker socket into the container
Serves HTTPS with its own certificate; browsers need TLS trust setup
Source build needs just and Node.js for Tailwind on top of Rust 1.91+
Constrained devices need a custom build with --no-default-features --features lightweight

projects.name: Spacebot
projects.tagline: Multi-user agent harness for Discord, Slack and Telegram communities
projects.summary: Spacebot is a Rust agent server built for many concurrent users: channel processes hold conversations while branches think and workers execute, so replies never block on tool calls. It ships adapters for Discord, Slack, Telegram, Signal, Mattermost and email, a typed memory graph in SQLite and LanceDB, a task system with approvals, cron jobs, and model routing over any OpenAI- or Anthropic-compatible endpoint.
strengths: Per-guild, per-channel and per-DM permissions; identity anchors track users across platforms
Compaction runs in a separate worker, so long sessions never pause the conversation
Tasks created autonomously wait in pending_approval; nothing runs unapproved
Embedded SQLite and LanceDB only; no external database service
weaknesses: Licensed FSL-1.1-ALv2 (source-available), not an OSI license
Coding tasks run only on the built-in worker or OpenCode today
Web search requires a Brave Search API key
Browser automation needs headless Chrome

projects.name: Khoj
projects.tagline: Personal assistant that chats with your documents and the web
projects.summary: Khoj answers questions from the web and your files (PDF, Markdown, org-mode, Word, Notion, images) using local or hosted LLMs such as llama3, qwen, gemma, mistral, GPT, Claude, Gemini and DeepSeek. It is reachable from a browser, Obsidian, Emacs, desktop and phone apps and WhatsApp, supports custom agents with their own knowledge and tools, and runs scheduled automations that deliver newsletters by email.
strengths: Clients for browser, Obsidian, Emacs, desktop, phone and WhatsApp
Reads PDF, Markdown, org-mode, Word, Notion and image files
Hosted instance at app.khoj.dev to try before self-hosting
Custom agents with their own knowledge, persona, model and tools
weaknesses: AGPL-3.0 license
README gives no hardware requirements or ports; setup lives entirely in the docs
Maintainers now promote a newer project, Pipali, at the top of the README
Enterprise and cloud tiers exist; feature parity with self-hosting is not stated

projects.name: PicoClaw
projects.tagline: Go assistant agent that runs in under 20 MB on $10 boards
projects.summary: PicoClaw is a single Go binary for x86_64, ARM64, MIPS, RISC-V and LoongArch that runs a personal agent in roughly 10 to 20 MB of RAM and boots in under a second on a 0.6 GHz core. It talks to 30+ LLM providers via a model_list config, supports MCP, image input and rule-based model routing, and reaches Telegram, Discord, Matrix, IRC and WeChat. A WebUI launcher on port 18800 handles setup.
strengths: Single static binary for RISC-V, ARM, MIPS and x86; runs on $10 Linux boards
10 to 20 MB resident memory; boots in under 1 s on 0.6 GHz
30+ providers including OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Ollama, vLLM, Bedrock and Copilot
Android APK turns old phones into an assistant host
weaknesses: README warns of unresolved security issues; not for production before v1.0
Gateway binds 127.0.0.1 by default; Docker needs PICOCLAW_GATEWAY_HOST=0.0.0.0
AWS Bedrock support requires a custom build with -tags bedrock
No root Dockerfile; compose file lives under docker/ and needs a first-run bootstrap

projects.name: LobeHub
projects.tagline: Agent workspace with builder, groups, scheduling and 10,000+ MCP skills
projects.summary: LobeHub is a self-hostable agent workspace that runs on Vercel, Zeabur, Sealos, Alibaba Cloud or Docker Compose. It centres on an Agent Builder, Agent Groups that work a task in parallel, Pages for co-writing, scheduled runs, projects and shared workspaces, plus structured editable memory and an IM gateway, with 10,000+ tools and MCP-compatible plugins. An OpenAI API key is required to start.
strengths: One-click deploy buttons for Vercel, Zeabur, Sealos, RepoCloud and Alibaba Cloud
10,000+ tools and MCP-compatible plugins for agents
Agent Groups, scheduled runs, projects and team workspaces
Memory is structured and editable rather than a hidden store
weaknesses: OPENAI_API_KEY is a required environment variable
Docker setup runs a curl-piped script from lobe.li before docker compose up
README recommends a third-party API reseller through an affiliate link
README states no ports, databases or hardware requirements

projects.name: Open WebUI
projects.tagline: Self-hosted chat UI for Ollama and OpenAI-compatible APIs with RBAC and RAG
projects.summary: Open WebUI is a Python-served web interface (pip or Docker, port 8080) for Ollama and any OpenAI-compatible API such as LM Studio, vLLM, OpenRouter or Groq. It bundles RAG over 9 vector databases with hybrid BM25 search, web search through 20+ providers, image generation via ComfyUI, AUTOMATIC1111, DALL-E or Gemini, MCP and OpenAPI tool servers, and per-user roles with LDAP, OAuth and SCIM provisioning.
strengths: Images tagged :ollama and :cuda bundle Ollama or CUDA acceleration in one container
RBAC, user groups, LDAP/AD, OAuth SSO and SCIM 2.0 provisioning built in
9 vector databases incl. ChromaDB, PGVector, Qdrant, Milvus and Elasticsearch
Redis-backed sessions and WebSockets for multi-worker, multi-node deployments
weaknesses: Custom Open WebUI License requires keeping the Open WebUI branding visible
Enterprise plan pitched at the top of the README; Terminals isolation is enterprise-only
pip install is pinned to Python 3.11
Data is lost unless the /app/backend/data volume is mounted

projects.name: AnythingLLM
projects.tagline: Document chat and agent app with built-in RAG, MCP and multi-user support
projects.summary: AnythingLLM is a Node.js app that ingests PDF, TXT, DOCX and other files into a workspace and chats over them with any of 40+ LLM providers, from llama.cpp, Ollama and LM Studio to OpenAI, Anthropic, Bedrock and Gemini. It ships a native embedder, LanceDB by default plus 8 other vector stores, a no-code agent builder, MCP support, scheduled tasks, model routing and a developer API.
strengths: LanceDB embedded by default; PGVector, Qdrant, Milvus, Chroma, Weaviate, Pinecone optional
Native embedder and audio transcription run locally with no extra service
Multi-user instance with per-user permissions in the Docker build
Embeddable website chat widget and a full developer API
weaknesses: Anonymous telemetry to PostHog is on by default; opt out with DISABLE_TELEMETRY=true
Multi-user support and the embed widget are Docker-only, not in the desktop app
Speech-to-text is limited to the browser built-in engine
No root Dockerfile; container build lives under docker/

projects.name: Onyx
projects.tagline: Team knowledge chat that indexes 50+ apps for RAG and agents
projects.summary: Onyx indexes content and permissions from 50+ apps into a hybrid vector and keyword index, then answers through agentic RAG, deep research and custom agents with web search, MCP actions and a code sandbox. It works with Ollama, LiteLLM, vLLM, Anthropic, OpenAI or Gemini, deploys via Docker, Kubernetes or Helm, and is reachable from the web app, Slack and Discord bots, an MCP server or a Chrome extension.
strengths: Lite mode runs the chat UI and agents in under 1 GB of memory
Air-gappable: index, database and processing all run inside your environment
MCP server gives Claude Code, Codex or any MCP client company context with user permissions
Community Edition is MIT; install script sets up Docker in one command
weaknesses: SSO (OIDC, SAML), SCIM, RBAC, analytics and whitelabeling are Enterprise Edition only
Standard mode adds index, worker, inference, Redis and MinIO containers
Lite mode cannot index documents
README gives no port or hardware figures for the Standard deployment

projects.name: big-AGI
projects.tagline: Multi-model chat workspace with Beam side-by-side model comparison
projects.summary: Big-AGI Open is the self-hostable web app behind big-agi.com, deployable via Docker or Vercel. It connects 20+ LLM services and 500+ models with your own API keys, and its Beam feature runs one prompt across several models and merges the answers. Personas, request inspection, web search with citations, image generation and multi-vendor speech are included; data stays local-first in the browser.
strengths: Beam and Merge: fan one prompt out to several models and reconcile the results
20+ LLM services incl. Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, Ollama, LM Studio, LocalAI, Bedrock, Groq
AI Inspector shows the exact requests sent to each provider
MIT license; no usage charges, bring your own keys
weaknesses: Cross-device sync and 1 GB storage only on the hosted Pro tier at $10.99/month
No SSO or shared team features in the open build; managed deployments by request
README omits stack, ports and resource requirements; install guide lives in docs/
README is mostly badges, taglines and release notes rather than specs

projects.name: odysseus
projects.tagline: Self-hosted workspace for chat, agents, email, documents, notes and calendar
projects.summary: Odysseus is a self-hosted web workspace that combines chat with local or API models, tool-using agents, deep research, a document editor, an IMAP/SMTP email client, and notes with CalDAV calendar sync. Agents can use MCP, files, shell, skills and memory. A model cookbook recommends, downloads and serves models based on the host hardware.
strengths: Covers chat, email, documents, notes and CalDAV calendar in one app
Agents support MCP, shell, files, skills and memory
Built-in blind side-by-side model comparison and multi-step deep research
Compose file pulls a prebuilt multi-arch image from ghcr.io
weaknesses: Ships local shell and file tools; auth must stay enabled when exposed
Default branch is dev; the more curated branch is main
AGPL-3.0 license restricts closed-source network use
RAM and VRAM requirements are not stated in the README

projects.name: Hermes WebUI
projects.tagline: Browser front-end for Hermes Agent with sessions, workspace files and profiles
projects.summary: Hermes WebUI is a three-panel web interface for Nous Research's Hermes Agent, written in Python with vanilla JS and no build step. It runs the agent in-process using your existing Hermes config, and adds streaming chat, tool call cards, session projects and tags, a workspace file browser and profile switching. Optional password, passkey and OIDC login are available; native Windows is not supported by the bootstrap.
strengths: No build step or bundler: Python backend with vanilla JS frontend
Reuses existing Hermes Agent config, models and memory without extra setup
Optional password, passkey/WebAuthn and OIDC auth; off by default for localhost
Includes ctl.sh daemon control, Docker, compose and a Nix flake/module
weaknesses: Requires Hermes Agent; bootstrap installs it via a curl-piped script if missing
Native Windows not supported by bootstrap; community guide only
OIDC state is in process memory, so multi-instance needs sticky sessions
Full agent-loop delegation to an external gateway is not yet shipped

projects.name: NextChat
projects.tagline: Lightweight Next.js chat client for OpenAI, Claude, Gemini and DeepSeek APIs
projects.summary: NextChat is a Node.js web client (Docker image yidadaa/chatgpt-next-web on port 3000, or a one-click Vercel deploy) that talks to OpenAI, Azure, Anthropic, Google Gemini, DeepSeek, Baidu, ByteDance, Alibaba, iFlytek, ChatGLM, SiliconFlow and 302.AI through environment variables. Chat history stays in the browser, access is gated by a shared CODE password list, and MCP tools switch on with ENABLE_MCP=true.
strengths: First screen about 100 KB with streaming responses; desktop client about 5 MB
Providers configured purely by environment variables; CUSTOM_MODELS edits the model list
UI in 14 languages; PWA, dark mode, Markdown with LaTeX and mermaid
Hosted demo at app.nextchat.club
weaknesses: No user accounts; access control is a comma-separated password list in CODE
Conversations live in browser storage; cross-device sync needs an UpStash setup
OPENAI_API_KEY is marked required even when another provider is used
Local knowledge base still unchecked on the roadmap

projects.name: LibreChat
projects.tagline: Multi-provider ChatGPT-style app with agents, MCP, code interpreter and auth
projects.summary: LibreChat is a self-hosted chat platform that fronts Anthropic, OpenAI, Azure, AWS Bedrock, Google, Vertex AI and any OpenAI-compatible endpoint such as Ollama or OpenRouter. It adds agents with MCP servers, skills and subagents, a sandboxed code interpreter for Python, Node, Go, Rust and more, web search, artifacts, resumable streams, and multi-user login via OAuth2, LDAP or email with an admin panel.
strengths: Admin panel for users, groups, roles and config overrides ships in the Compose stack
Resumable streams reconnect dropped responses and sync across tabs and devices
UI translated into 30+ languages
OpenTelemetry and Langfuse export for traces and logs
weaknesses: Code interpreter is a separate API service, not part of this repo
File search (RAG) depends on the separate rag-api service
Horizontal scaling and resumable streams need Redis
Attached code workspaces are marked highly experimental

projects.name: HuggingChat UI
projects.tagline: SvelteKit chat front end behind HuggingChat for OpenAI-compatible endpoints
projects.summary: Chat UI is the SvelteKit app that powers HuggingChat. It talks only to OpenAI-compatible APIs set through OPENAI_BASE_URL, discovering models from the /models endpoint, so llama.cpp server, Ollama, OpenRouter, Poe or the HF router all work. Chat history, users and settings live in MongoDB 6/7, MCP servers can supply tools, and a heuristic Omni router picks per-message routes with fallbacks.
strengths: chat-ui-db Docker image bundles MongoDB; one container on port 3000
MCP tool calls surfaced as OpenAI function calling with per-model overrides
Same codebase as the public HuggingChat deployment
Apache-2.0 license
weaknesses: OpenAI-compatible endpoints only; legacy provider integrations and GGUF discovery removed
Embeddings and web-search helpers were removed from this branch
Router needs a hand-written routes JSON; no sample file ships
README does not describe authentication or multi-user setup

projects.name: SillyTavern
projects.tagline: Local chat front end for role-play across many LLM backends
projects.summary: SillyTavern is a locally installed Node.js 20+ interface for text-generation LLMs, image generators and TTS, aimed at character and role-play chat. One UI covers KoboldAI/KoboldCpp, Horde, NovelAI, oobabooga, TabbyAPI, OpenAI, OpenRouter, Claude and Mistral, with Visual Novel Mode, AUTOMATIC1111 and ComfyUI image generation, WorldInfo lorebooks and third-party extensions. No hosted service, no tracking.
strengths: Runs on anything that can run Node.js 20; no GPU needed for the UI itself
Backends: KoboldCpp, Horde, NovelAI, oobabooga, TabbyAPI, OpenAI, OpenRouter, Claude, Mistral
WorldInfo lorebooks and deep prompt controls for long-form character chat
No hosted service and no telemetry; 300+ contributors over 3 years
weaknesses: AGPL-3.0 license
Single-user local tool; no accounts or team features
Maintainers describe the learning curve as steep
Installation and Docker instructions live only on the docs site

projects.name: ClaraVerse
projects.tagline: Private AI workspace with chat, agent crews, workflows and Telegram
projects.summary: ClaraVerse is a Go and React workspace (Docker Compose, port 3000) that auto-detects Ollama and LM Studio and also uses OpenAI, Claude, Gemini or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint. It combines chat with Crew multi-agent teams with human review, a visual workflow builder with 200+ integrations, layered AES-256-GCM encrypted memory, knowledge bases, a Telegram channel and the claracli terminal agent.
strengths: Auto-detects Ollama and LM Studio every 2 minutes and imports their models
Per-user AES-256-GCM encrypted memory with pinned and decaying recall tiers
150+ built-in integrations shared across chat, workflows, crew and routines
AGPL-3.0 with no branding clause or user cap
weaknesses: Full stack runs MySQL, MongoDB, Redis, SearXNG, Qdrant and an embeddings sidecar
Single-container mode cannot use knowledge bases or search_knowledge
4 GB RAM minimum, 8 GB recommended
Conversations live in browser IndexedDB by default; sync is optional

projects.name: LoLLMs WebUI
projects.tagline: Single-user web UI for local and remote LLMs with many personalities
projects.summary: LoLLMs WebUI is a Python 3.11 web app (port 9600) fronting local models via HF transformers, GGUF/GGML, ExLlama v2, Ollama and vLLM bindings plus OpenAI, Anthropic and OpenRouter APIs. It adds 500+ personalities, cost/speed-based routing, and hooks into Stable Diffusion, ComfyUI, DALL-E, video and musicgen services. The authors say it is in minimal support, to be replaced by the newer lollms project.
strengths: Bindings for local GGUF, ExLlama v2 and transformers plus Ollama, vLLM and hosted APIs
Image, video and music generation integrations in one UI
Smart routing picks cheaper or faster models by prompt complexity
Apache-2.0 license
weaknesses: Maintainers state it is in minimal support, to be replaced by ParisNeo/lollms
No built-in authentication; designed for local use only
Docker image must be built locally; no published image in the README
Manual install needs submodules plus a per-binding install script

projects.name: gpt_academic
projects.tagline: Gradio web UI with plugins for translating and polishing papers and code
projects.summary: GPT Academic is a Python Gradio app that sends text to OpenAI, Azure, Qwen, GLM, ERNIE, Spark and local models such as ChatGLM and MOSS. It adds one-click buttons and hot-reloadable Python plugins for polishing, translating arXiv, LaTeX and PDF papers, summarizing, code analysis and mermaid diagrams. Configuration is read from config.py, config_private.py or environment variables.
strengths: Plugins for arXiv, LaTeX and PDF paper translation, proofreading and summarization
Many backends: OpenAI, Azure, Qwen, GLM4, ERNIE, Spark, local ChatGLM and MOSS
Plugins are plain Python files with hot reload; buttons are defined in core_functional.py
Several API keys can be listed together in one setting
weaknesses: Documentation is mostly Chinese; the English README is a separate translated file
Gradio compatibility issues; requirements.txt versions must be used exactly
Full-capability Docker image bundles CUDA and LaTeX and is large
No user accounts mentioned; last tagged release is December 2024

projects.name: ChatGPT UI
projects.tagline: Multi-user ChatGPT-style web client with pluggable databases
projects.summary: ChatGPT UI is a web client for ChatGPT-style chat that supports multiple users, multiple languages and several database backends for persistent storage. The front end lives in this repo and the API server in the separate chatgpt-ui-server repository; setup is documented on a GitHub Pages site in English and Chinese.
strengths: Multi-user accounts with persistent history
Several database backends for storage
Documentation in English and Chinese
weaknesses: README is a few lines; no install steps, ports or provider list
Front end and server are split across two repositories
Last commit 2026-05-11; README carries a sponsor banner for a paid AI platform

projects.name: cherry-studio
projects.tagline: Cross-platform desktop chat client for many cloud and local LLM providers
projects.summary: Cherry Studio is a desktop app for Windows, macOS and Linux that talks to cloud providers such as OpenAI, Gemini and Anthropic, and to local models through Ollama and LM Studio. It includes 300+ preset assistants, simultaneous multi-model chats, document handling (text, images, Office, PDF), WebDAV backup and an MCP server integration. An Enterprise Edition with admin backend and shared knowledge bases is sold separately.
strengths: Supports cloud providers plus local Ollama and LM Studio in one client
Runs the same prompt against multiple models in a single conversation
Installs as a desktop app with no environment setup, on Windows, Mac and Linux
300+ preconfigured assistants plus custom assistant creation
weaknesses: AGPL-3.0; commercial use outside AGPL terms needs a separate license
Admin backend, team knowledge base and access control are Enterprise-only
Plugin system, OCR, TTS and ASR are listed as roadmap items, not shipped
No Docker or web deployment; desktop only, so no multi-user server in Community Edition

projects.name: deep-live-cam
projects.tagline: Real-time webcam face swap from a single source image
projects.summary: Deep-Live-Cam is a Python desktop GUI that swaps a face from one source image onto a webcam feed, video or image, using ONNX models (inswapper_128_fp16, gfpgan-1024). It supports mouth masking, mapping different faces to multiple subjects, and CPU, CUDA, CoreML, DirectML and OpenVINO execution providers. A paid pre-built edition with extra features is sold on the project website.
strengths: Live webcam mode plus image and video file processing from one GUI
Execution providers for CPU, CUDA, CoreML, DirectML and OpenVINO
Mouth mask and face mapping for multiple subjects in one frame
Needs only a single source image, no per-face training
weaknesses: Manual install needs Python, ffmpeg, CUDA/cuDNN pinning; README says not for beginners
CPU-only mode is slower; live preview takes 10-30 seconds to appear
Command-line arguments are marked unmaintained in the README
insightface models are limited to non-commercial research use

projects.name: prompt-optimizer
projects.tagline: Prompt rewriting and testing tool for web, desktop, Chrome and MCP
projects.summary: Prompt Optimizer rewrites system and user prompts with an LLM you configure, then lets you test, compare and save the results as versioned favorites. It runs as a browser app, desktop app, Chrome extension or Docker container, and exposes an MCP server at /mcp with optimize-user-prompt, optimize-system-prompt and iterate-prompt tools. Model calls go straight from the client to the provider, including text-to-image and image-to-image modes.
strengths: Ships as web app, desktop app, Chrome extension and Docker image
Built-in MCP server at /mcp for Claude Desktop and other MCP clients
Analysis and compare evaluation, variables, multi-turn and function-calling tests
Client-side processing; requests go directly to the configured provider
weaknesses: Web version may hit browser CORS limits with local endpoints such as Ollama
VITE_* API keys are exposed in browser assets on public deployments
Chrome Web Store version can lag behind the latest release
Workspace/project management is still unchecked on the roadmap

projects.name: jan
projects.tagline: Desktop app that runs local models or cloud APIs, with a local server
projects.summary: Jan is a Tauri desktop app for Windows, macOS and Linux that downloads LLMs from Hugging Face and runs them through a bundled llama.cpp engine. It can also connect to cloud providers such as OpenAI, Anthropic, Mistral and Groq. It exposes an OpenAI-compatible API at localhost:1337 and supports MCP for agent tools.
strengths: Runs local models and cloud providers from one app
OpenAI-compatible local server at localhost:1337 for other applications
MCP integration for agentic tool use
Engine variants for CPU, Vulkan, Metal, CUDA and ROCm builds
weaknesses: Desktop only; no Docker image or multi-user web deployment
README says Apache 2.0, but license detection reports NOASSERTION
Source build needs Node, Yarn, Rust; Windows also needs LLVM, Ninja, CMake
Linux Arm64 is a linked how-to, not a packaged download

projects.name: chatbox
projects.tagline: Desktop and mobile chat client for OpenAI, Claude, Gemini and Ollama models
projects.summary: Chatbox is an Electron app (TypeScript, React) that connects to hosted LLM APIs and local models through Ollama. Chat data is stored on the device. It ships installers for Windows, macOS and Linux, plus iOS and Android apps and a web version.
strengths: Installers for Windows, macOS, Linux (AppImage), plus iOS, Android and a web version
Supports OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Claude, Gemini, Ollama and ChatGLM-6B from one client
Chat data stays on the device; no server deployment needed
Prompt library, Markdown, LaTeX and code highlighting, DALL-E-3 image generation
weaknesses: README lists no document chat, RAG or agent features
Community Edition is synced with a separate pro repo; feature parity is unclear
Provider list in README is dated (llama2, ChatGLM-6B); current coverage is unclear
GPL-3.0 license may restrict embedding in proprietary products

projects.name: dsh-desktop
projects.tagline: Native Windows and macOS desktop client for DeepSeek Harness
projects.summary: DSH Desktop wraps the pinned, unmodified upstream DeepSeek Harness web UI, host service and plugin system in a native desktop app with window, tray, terminal and auto-update. The desktop shell is itself a DSH plugin, and the app includes a plugin market and phone remote control (iOS/Android, from 2.0.9). Installers cover Windows x64 and macOS Universal; no Node.js is needed.
strengths: Installers for Windows x64 and macOS Universal, no separate Node.js install
Runs a pinned, unmodified upstream DeepSeek Harness version
Built-in plugin market and desktop services for third-party plugins
Web service listens on loopback only by default
weaknesses: No Linux build listed
LAN access option has no authentication, per the README
Tied to DeepSeek Harness; independent project, not affiliated with DeepSeek
README and docs are primarily in Chinese

projects.name: aionui
projects.tagline: Desktop and WebUI app that runs a built-in agent plus external CLI agents
projects.summary: AionUi is a TypeScript desktop app for macOS, Windows and Linux. It bundles an agent engine (aionrs) that reads and writes files, searches the web and calls MCP tools using any of 30+ API providers or local Ollama and LM Studio. It also detects installed CLI agents such as Claude Code, Codex and Qwen Code, runs them in parallel sessions, and is reachable through a WebUI or chat bots, with scheduled tasks.
strengths: Auto-detects installed CLI agents (Claude Code, Codex, Qwen Code and others) in one interface
Built-in agent works after pasting an API key, with no separate CLI install
Scheduled tasks support cron with timezone, fixed intervals and one-time triggers
Remote access via browser WebUI or Telegram, Lark, DingTalk and WeChat bots
weaknesses: Local models are reached through a custom API endpoint, not a bundled runtime
Slack, Discord and WeCom channels are listed as coming soon
Unattended YOLO mode and permissions vary by selected agent
README excerpt gives no RAM, port or hardware requirements

projects.name: Langflow
projects.tagline: Visual builder for AI agents and workflows, exposed as API or MCP server
projects.summary: Langflow is a Python platform for assembling agents and workflows on a visual canvas, with Python source access to customize any component. Each flow can be served as an HTTP API, exported as JSON, or deployed as an MCP server so MCP clients can call it as a tool. It installs via uv/pip, Docker, or a Windows and macOS desktop app, and serves its UI on port 7860.
strengths: Every flow can be called as a REST API or exposed as an MCP server
Component source is editable in Python, so custom nodes need no fork
Built-in playground for step-by-step testing of flows
Observability integrations with LangSmith and LangFuse; MIT license
weaknesses: Official releases require setting LANGFLOW_SUPERUSER_PASSWORD; dev branches default to auto-login
Python 3.10–3.14 required for the pip install path
README gives no RAM or hardware requirements
