Specific supported models and vector databases are not listed in the README

projects.name: daily_stock_analysis
projects.tagline: Daily LLM stock analysis for A-share, HK, US and other markets, pushed to chat apps
projects.summary: Python app that pulls quotes, K-lines, news and fundamentals for a watchlist across A-share, HK, US, Japan, Korea and Taiwan markets. It has an LLM write a decision report with score, trend, buy/sell levels and risks, then pushes it to WeCom, Feishu, Telegram, Discord, Slack or email. It runs on GitHub Actions, Docker or locally, with a FastAPI web workbench for history, backtests and strategy chat.
strengths: Runs on a GitHub Actions fork with no server; default schedule is weekdays 18:00 Beijing time
Free data sources (AkShare, Baostock, YFinance) work with zero configuration
Supports Gemini, Claude, OpenAI-compatible APIs, DeepSeek, Qwen and local Ollama models
Six push channels plus a web UI with history, backtest, portfolio and 15 built-in chat strategies
weaknesses: README is mainly Chinese; English docs are in a separate file
Free data sources are subject to rate limits and upstream changes; stability not guaranteed
Report quality depends on a paid news-search API key; a search service is recommended
Output is for study only; the disclaimer excludes investment advice and liability

projects.name: deer-flow
projects.tagline: Agent harness that runs sub-agents, memory and sandboxed skills for long tasks
projects.summary: DeerFlow 2.0 is a ByteDance agent harness where a lead agent delegates to sub-agents, backed by long-term memory, a sandboxed file system and extensible skills. It includes a web UI, a Gateway, MCP support, IM channels, scheduled tasks, a terminal UI and an embedded Python client. It is a ground-up rewrite that shares no code with v1.
strengths: Interactive `make setup` wizard generates config.yaml and .env in about 2 minutes
Web UI model registration for OpenAI, Anthropic, DeepSeek, Qwen, Doubao, Kimi, Zhipu, MiniMax
Tracing via LangSmith, Langfuse and Monocle, plus `make doctor` and `make support-bundle`
Many search and fetch backends: Brave, Tavily, Jina, Firecrawl, Crawl4AI, InfoQuest
weaknesses: README warns improper deployment carries security risks; Gateway admin equals code execution
Local development needs Python 3.12+ and Node.js 22+
README is dense with config detail; RAM and hardware needs are not stated
v2 shares no code with v1; v1 users must stay on the 1.x branch

projects.name: Dify
projects.tagline: Visual builder for LLM workflows, RAG pipelines and agents, with APIs
projects.summary: Dify is an LLM app development platform with a visual workflow canvas, a prompt IDE, a RAG pipeline that extracts text from PDFs and PPTs, and agents that run in their own sandbox. Every app is exposed through an API. Model providers include GPT, Mistral, Llama3 and any OpenAI-compatible endpoint. It runs via Docker Compose or as the hosted Dify Cloud.
strengths: Visual workflow canvas, prompt IDE and RAG pipeline in one platform
Every app exposes an API, so it works as a backend service
Supports hundreds of LLMs plus any OpenAI API-compatible model
Agents can use Marketplace tools, MCP servers or your own APIs
weaknesses: License is the Dify Open Source License (Apache 2.0 plus extra conditions)
SSO, RBAC and support SLAs are in the Enterprise edition
Docker Compose self-hosting needs at least 2 CPU cores and 4 GiB RAM
Observability relies on external tools such as Opik, Langfuse and Arize Phoenix

projects.name: Multica
projects.tagline: Issue board where AI coding agents take assignments like teammates
projects.summary: Multica is a workspace where issues are assigned to AI coding agents, which run through locally installed agent CLIs such as Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and Copilot (26 listed). A daemon on your own machine executes the work next to your code and reports progress back to the issue, which ends in review rather than main. The backend is Go with PostgreSQL 17, and clients cover web, Electron desktop and an Expo mobile app.
strengths: Drives 26 existing agent CLIs, so no model or API lock-in
Execution log replays every tool call, command and error per run
Daemon runs on your own machine, so code stays there
Self-host via Docker Compose or Helm; works with GitHub, GitLab, Gitea, Forgejo
weaknesses: Does not ship agents; each runtime needs a CLI installed and signed in
Custom Multica License (Apache 2.0 plus conditions on hosting, embedding, branding)
Requires Docker, a Go backend and PostgreSQL 17 to self-host
iOS app builds from source only; DingTalk, WeCom, Telegram are community-maintained

projects.name: AutoGPT
projects.tagline: Block-based builder for agents that run on demand, schedule or trigger
projects.summary: AutoGPT Platform lets you describe a job in plain English (AutoPilot) or wire blocks on a visual canvas, then run the agent on demand, on a schedule or from a trigger, with a dashboard of runs and costs and a marketplace of shared agents. It connects to 45+ platforms such as Gmail, Slack, GitHub and Notion. Self-hosting is free with your own Docker host and model API keys; the hosted platform is paid.
strengths: Plain-English AutoPilot and a drag-and-connect block builder for the same agent
Agents run on demand, on schedules or from triggers with a run and cost dashboard
45+ integrations including Gmail, Google Sheets, GitHub, Slack, Notion, Jira, Salesforce
Classic standalone agent still shipped under MIT in classic/
weaknesses: Platform code is Polyform Shield: no offering it as a competing hosted service
README has no self-host commands; the single-container installer is still unreleased
Windows self-hosting is manual-guide only
Hosted platform charges per agent run; README is largely marketing

projects.name: vibe-trading
projects.tagline: Finance research agent for backtests, market data and broker connectors
projects.summary: Vibe-Trading is a Python agent (FastAPI backend, React 19 web UI, CLI, MCP) for trading research. It pulls market data across many exchanges, runs backtests and factor analysis, and checks figures in generated reports against tool evidence. It also connects to 18 brokers and sends scheduled reports through channels such as Email, Slack, Discord and Feishu.
strengths: Grounding gate checks each reported figure against session tool evidence and cuts failures
Backtest run cards cite metrics only where saved CSV output agrees
18 broker connectors, several read-only, with paper/live permissions documented
Active: v0.1.16 shipped 116 merged PRs, with near-daily fixes afterward
weaknesses: Narrow domain: finance research only, not a general agent builder
Some broker features are unavailable, e.g. Robinhood options execution
Data quality depends on public sources such as Stooq, which can block requests
Frequent backtest-correctness fixes in the changelog; verify results independently

projects.name: Paperclip
projects.tagline: Task manager and org chart for teams of AI agents with budgets
projects.summary: Paperclip is a Node.js server and React UI that coordinates external agents (OpenClaw, Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI and custom HTTP adapters) through tasks, approvals, org charts, budgets and routines. Agents wake on heartbeats, check out tasks atomically, and report work and spend to a dashboard; multi-org support, skills, GitHub, Notion and MCP connectors, and company export/import are built in.
strengths: Company, agent and project budgets with alerts and automatic pause at limits
Atomic task checkout with execution locks prevents duplicate runs
Adapters for OpenClaw, Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Hermes, Kimi
Export and import whole organizations with secret scrubbing
weaknesses: Does no agent work itself; needs external agent runtimes installed and authenticated
Agent Chat and Slack, Discord, Telegram, AgentMail connectors are experimental
Paperclip Cloud is waitlist-only
Quickstart, ports and database are beyond the README's first 20,000 characters

projects.name: openmaic
projects.tagline: Generates interactive classes with AI teachers and classmates from a topic or file
projects.summary: OpenMAIC turns a topic or attached documents into a lesson made of slides, quizzes, interactive HTML simulations and project-based learning activities. AI teacher and classmate agents speak via TTS, draw on a whiteboard and discuss with the learner. Built on Next.js 16, React 19 and LangGraph. Since 1.2.0, course generation runs on the server and courses are stored in PostgreSQL.
strengths: Exports lessons as editable .pptx or interactive .html pages
Many providers: OpenAI, Anthropic, Bedrock, Gemini, Ollama, Lemonade, any OpenAI-compatible API
Models set once per slot in openmaic.yml, with lock and allowUserKeys: false options
OpenMAIC Skill lets OpenClaw and similar workbenches generate classrooms from chat apps
weaknesses: 1.2.0 needs PostgreSQL 16 and a long-running server; Vercel and serverless are unsupported
Latest 1.2.0 line is a release candidate; changelog must be read before upgrading
README recommends image, video, TTS and web search keys for full function
Compose install is single-user; shared access needs ACCESS_CODE and manual network publishing

projects.name: Sim
projects.tagline: Workspace to build, deploy and monitor agents with 1,000+ integrations
projects.summary: Sim is a Next.js and Bun app on PostgreSQL that builds agents visually, by chat or in code, with monitoring, schedules and logs. The npx sim-setup wizard (Node.js 20+ and Docker) provisions the database, secrets and images and serves port 3000. Tables, files and knowledge bases share the workspace, 1,000+ integrations such as Slack, Notion and HubSpot are available, and local models run via Ollama or vLLM.
strengths: Built-in tables, file store and knowledge bases alongside workflows and chat
1,000+ integrations including Slack, Notion, HubSpot, Salesforce and databases
Local models via Ollama and vLLM; Apache-2.0 license
sim-setup wizard adds email, storage, sandbox, jobs, cache or knowledge later
weaknesses: Chat is a Sim-managed service; self-hosted installs need a Chat API key from sim.ai
Setup prompt in the README notes the Compose stack needs 12 GB+ RAM
Background jobs use Trigger.dev and remote code execution uses E2B
Self-hosting goes through an npx wizard rather than a documented compose file

projects.name: Skyvern
projects.tagline: Browser automation agent driven by vision LLMs over Playwright
projects.summary: Skyvern drives websites with vision LLMs instead of selectors: a Playwright-compatible Python/TypeScript SDK adds page.act, page.extract and page.validate, and a no-code builder chains tasks into workflows with loops, HTTP and code blocks. pip install skyvern[all] serves API and UI on port 8080 with SQLite by default; Docker Compose bundles Postgres. TOTP 2FA, Bitwarden, browser livestreaming and MCP are supported.
strengths: Works on sites it has never seen; no XPath or CSS selectors to maintain
SQLite default means the pip path needs neither Postgres nor Docker
TOTP, email and SMS 2FA plus Bitwarden and custom credential services
Python and TypeScript SDKs extend standard Playwright calls with a prompt argument
weaknesses: AGPL-3.0 license
Anti-bot measures, proxy network and CAPTCHA solving exist only in the paid cloud
Windows pip install needs Rust plus VS C++ tools and the Windows SDK
Authentication features are offered by email request; 1Password and LastPass unsupported

projects.name: openmontage
projects.tagline: Agent-driven video production pipelines run from your AI coding assistant
projects.summary: OpenMontage is a set of pipelines, tools and stage skills that let a coding assistant (Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, Windsurf, Codex) research, script, generate assets, edit and render a video. Rendering uses Remotion or HyperFrames plus FFmpeg. It works with no API keys using Piper TTS and free footage from Archive.org, NASA and Wikimedia, and adds paid image, video and voice providers when keys are set.
strengths: Works with zero API keys: Piper TTS, free archival footage, Remotion/HyperFrames, FFmpeg
Many providers via optional keys: fal.ai, Atlas Cloud, Kling, Runway, ElevenLabs, Suno, Google
Backlot local board shows pipeline progress, costs, and a storyboard approval gate before render
Can start from a reference YouTube, TikTok or local video and give cost estimates first
weaknesses: Needs an external AI coding assistant to drive it; no standalone prompting UI
AGPL-3.0 license restricts closed-source network use
Setup needs Python 3.10+, Node.js 18+ and FFmpeg; no Docker image
Local video generation needs a GPU; VRAM requirements are not stated in the README

projects.name: Agent Zero
projects.tagline: Agent framework with a Linux desktop, browser and document editing
projects.summary: Agent Zero runs an agent inside a Docker container with an XFCE desktop, a built-in browser with DOM annotation, and LibreOffice editing, all shown in a web UI Canvas. It adds projects with isolated memory and secrets, subordinate agents, a Plugin Hub, MCP and A2A support, and an A0 CLI connector for working on host files.
strengths: Real XFCE desktop in the container; agent drives GUI apps and you share the mouse
Projects isolate files, memory, secrets, repositories and model presets per workspace
Prompts and tools are editable files; MCP, A2A and a 100+ plugin catalog supported
Time Travel snapshots and diffs the /a0/usr workspace so edits can be reverted
weaknesses: Requires Docker; default run maps port 80, which often needs remapping
Agent has shell and desktop access; README warns to isolate it and limit mounts
License is reported as NOASSERTION, so terms need checking before use
RAM and VRAM requirements are not stated in the README

projects.name: FastGPT
projects.tagline: Knowledge-base Q&A and visual workflow platform for LLM apps
projects.summary: FastGPT builds agents and LLM apps from a visual Flow editor on top of a knowledge base that ingests TXT, MD, HTML, PDF, Docx, PPTX, CSV, XLSX and URLs with hybrid retrieval and reranking. A one-script Docker Compose install serves port 3000 (default login root / 1234), supports bidirectional MCP, chat and plugin workflows, evaluation, call-chain logs, login-free share pages and iframe embedding.
strengths: Loaders for TXT, MD, HTML, PDF, Docx, PPTX, CSV, XLSX and URLs
Hybrid retrieval with reranking; chunks can be edited and deleted
Bidirectional MCP and RPA-style workflow nodes
One-script Docker Compose install
weaknesses: FastGPT Open Source License forbids offering it as SaaS and requires kept copyright notices
Default credentials root / 1234 after install
Default README is Chinese; English lives in README_en.md
Debug mode, node logs and auto-generated workflows are still unchecked roadmap items

projects.name: mirofish
projects.tagline: Multi-agent social simulation engine that predicts outcomes from seed documents
projects.summary: MiroFish builds a GraphRAG knowledge graph from uploaded seed material such as news, policy drafts or novels, then generates agent personas and runs a parallel social simulation on the OASIS engine. A ReportAgent writes a prediction report, and you can chat with individual simulated agents afterward. It uses any OpenAI-format LLM API plus Zep Cloud for memory.
strengths: End-to-end pipeline: graph building, persona generation, simulation, report, and agent chat
Works with any OpenAI-SDK-compatible LLM endpoint via LLM_BASE_URL
Public live demo available without installing anything
Docker Compose and source install both documented, ports 3000 and 5001
weaknesses: Requires Zep Cloud API key, so memory is not fully self-hosted
README warns of high LLM token consumption; suggests under 40 rounds first
AGPL-3.0 license restricts closed-source network use
README gives no evidence of prediction accuracy or benchmarks

projects.name: ui-tars-desktop
projects.tagline: Multimodal agent stack: terminal/Web UI agent and a desktop GUI agent
projects.summary: Monorepo with two projects. Agent TARS is a CLI and Web UI agent that controls a browser via GUI vision, DOM, or a hybrid, and mounts MCP servers as tools. UI-TARS Desktop is an app that operates the local or a remote computer and browser through the UI-TARS and Seed-1.5-VL/1.6 vision-language models.
strengths: Browser control by GUI vision, DOM, or hybrid strategy
MCP kernel; external MCP servers can be mounted as tools
Agent TARS runs headful (Web UI) or headless as a server
Works with providers such as Volcengine and Anthropic via CLI flags
weaknesses: Two products in one repo; README splits setup across external docs
Desktop app targets Windows and macOS; Linux support not stated
RAM and GPU needs for local UI-TARS models are not stated
Agent TARS CLI requires Node.js 22 or newer

projects.name: Botpress
projects.tagline: SDK, CLI and open-source integrations for the Botpress Cloud bot platform
projects.summary: This repository holds the TypeScript devtools for Botpress Cloud: the @botpress/cli (bp init, bp deploy), the @botpress/sdk and typed client, every public integration on the Botpress Hub, and example bots written as code. Bots themselves are built in the hosted Botpress Studio and powered by OpenAI; the on-premise server is the separate Botpress v12 repository. Everything here is MIT.
strengths: All public Hub integrations are open source and contributable with bp init and bp deploy
Typed TypeScript SDK and API client for building integrations and bots as code
MIT license for every package in the repository
weaknesses: The chatbot platform (Studio, runtime) is Botpress Cloud, not something you host from here
Self-hosted server is the separate, older Botpress v12 repository
Bots-as-code is described as not the recommended way to build bots
Plugins section is marked coming soon

projects.name: n8n
projects.tagline: Visual workflow automation with code steps, AI agent nodes and 1500+ integrations
projects.summary: n8n is a fair-code workflow platform that runs as one Docker container (docker.n8n.io/n8nio/n8n, port 5678) and combines a visual canvas with JavaScript, Python and npm code nodes. AI agent and workflow nodes connect to OpenAI, Anthropic, Google or open-source models, with human-approval steps and observability, and 1500+ integrations plus 9,000+ templates cover the rest of the stack.
strengths: 1500+ integrations and 9,000+ ready-made workflow templates
Code nodes run JavaScript or Python and can pull npm packages
Single container on port 5678 with one data volume
Switch model providers without rebuilding the workflow
weaknesses: Sustainable Use License (fair-code, source-available), not an OSI license
Some features require a separate n8n Enterprise License
README states no database, RAM or CPU requirements

projects.name: Activepieces
projects.tagline: Self-hosted workflow automation with TypeScript integrations, alternative to Zapier
projects.summary: Activepieces is a no-code workflow builder with loops, branches, auto retries, HTTP calls and npm-backed code steps, and flows are versioned. Integrations are called pieces: TypeScript npm packages, 280+ of which are exposed as MCP servers for Claude Desktop, Cursor or Windsurf. It also has AI pieces for several providers, human-in-the-loop approvals, and chat and form triggers.
strengths: Pieces are open-source TypeScript npm packages with hot reloading for local development
280+ pieces usable as MCP servers from Claude Desktop, Cursor or Windsurf
Flows are versioned and support loops, branches and auto retries
Built-in approval, delay, chat and form triggers for human-in-the-loop flows
weaknesses: Enterprise features sit under a separate commercial license, not MIT
README does not state RAM, CPU or database requirements
Automation-first; AI agents are one feature rather than the core design
README claims of 200+ and 280+ pieces are inconsistent

projects.name: deeptutor
projects.tagline: Self-hosted AI tutor with knowledge bases, guided learning, books and quizzes
projects.summary: DeepTutor is a Python backend with a Next.js 16 web UI for studying from your own documents. It combines chat over knowledge bases (LightRAG, PageIndex, GraphRAG, LlamaIndex, FAISS) with guided learning, generated books, quizzes, question banks and deep research. It also offers multi-user accounts, IM-connected Partners, MCP services and a CLI.
strengths: Several retrieval engines selectable per knowledge base: LightRAG, PageIndex, GraphRAG, LlamaIndex
Covers study workflows: guided learning, mastery gates, quizzes, question bank, daily practice
Multi-user deployment with per-user isolation, admin grants and learner/guardian accounts
Wide provider and parser coverage, including Codex OAuth, MinerU, Tika and PyMuPDF4LLM
weaknesses: Fast release cadence with breaking refactors (v1.6.3) makes upgrades risky
Large surface area: Partners, MCP, CLI apps and plugins add configuration overhead
RAM, GPU and port requirements are not stated in the visible README
Aimed at learning and study; less suited to general chat or enterprise search

projects.name: RAGFlow
projects.tagline: RAG engine with deep document parsing, template chunking and agentic retrieval
projects.summary: RAGFlow parses complex documents (PDF, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, scans, web pages) with its DeepDoc layout, OCR and table recognition, then chunks them by template and answers with traceable citations. It adds multi-step agentic retrieval with four thinking modes, plus knowledge compilation into wikis, graphs and mind maps. Services are written in Go and deployed with Docker Compose, with a web UI and HTTP API.
strengths: Template-based chunking with a visual view of chunks so humans can correct them
Answers include traceable citations back to source chunks
Ingests many formats, plus sitemap crawling and Google BigQuery sync
Configurable LLM, embedding and reranker models; multiple recall with fused re-ranking
weaknesses: Heavy stack: MySQL, MinIO, NATS, Kvrocks and a document engine; 16 GB RAM suggested
macOS is not supported for the Docker deployment
DeepDoc runs on CPU inference in the 1.0 release, which may slow parsing
Current release is 1.0.0-rc1, a release candidate rather than a stable 1.0

projects.name: Open Notebook
projects.tagline: Self-hosted NotebookLM alternative with podcasts and 20+ model providers
projects.summary: Open Notebook collects PDFs, audio, video, web pages and Office files into notebooks and offers cited chat, full-text and vector search, notes and multi-speaker podcast generation. It runs as two containers (SurrealDB plus a FastAPI/Next.js app) and talks to OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Mistral, Groq, Ollama, LM Studio or any OpenAI-compatible server. A REST API and MCP integration expose the same features.
strengths: 20+ providers, including Ollama and LM Studio for fully local runs
Podcasts with 1 to 4 speakers and custom episode profiles
REST API on port 5055 and an MCP server for Claude Desktop or VS Code
Two-service Docker Compose; keys stored encrypted with OPEN_NOTEBOOK_ENCRYPTION_KEY
weaknesses: Single-user; multi-user support is only a future direction in VISION.md
No password by default and ports 8502/5055 bind to all interfaces
Anthropic and Groq offer no embeddings, so a second provider is needed
UI in 14 languages but provider setup is manual per model type

projects.name: LightRAG
projects.tagline: Graph-based RAG framework with a REST API server and web UI
projects.summary: LightRAG indexes documents into a knowledge graph plus vector embeddings and answers queries with dual-level (entity and concept) retrieval. It ships as a Python library and as lightrag-server, which provides a REST API and a web UI for inserting, querying and visualizing the graph. It supports incremental updates, document deletion with graph rebuild, reranking, and several parsing and chunking options.
strengths: Document deletion rebuilds affected graph entries from the LLM cache; inserts are incremental
Storage backends include PostgreSQL, Neo4j, MongoDB and OpenSearch, plus local file stores
Parsers: MinerU, Docling and a native engine; four chunking strategies
Setup wizard generates .env and compose files; RAGAS evaluation and Langfuse tracing supported
weaknesses: Default in-memory/file stores are stated as not for production
Server binds to 0.0.0.0 and endpoints are public until auth is set in .env
Graph extraction needs LLM calls at index time; RAM and GPU needs are unstated
Optional features need extra steps: spaCy models for smart_heading, libcairo for SVG

projects.name: MaxKB
projects.tagline: Enterprise knowledge-base agent platform with RAG, workflows and MCP tools
projects.summary: MaxKB runs as one Docker container (port 8080, state in one volume) with a RAG pipeline that uploads or crawls documents, a workflow engine with function library and MCP tool use, and zero-code embedding into other systems. It works with private models (DeepSeek, Llama, Qwen) and public APIs (OpenAI, Claude, Gemini, MiniMax) and handles text, image, audio and video. Built on Django, LangChain and PostgreSQL.
strengths: Single docker run with all data under one mounted volume
Workflow engine with function library and MCP tool calling
Crawls online documents into the knowledge base automatically
Multimodal input and output: text, image, audio, video
weaknesses: GPL-3.0 limits bundling into proprietary products
Ships with default admin password MaxKB@123..
README gives no hardware guidance or provider configuration detail
Detailed docs are on maxkb.cn, partly in Chinese

projects.name: SurfSense
projects.tagline: Desktop agent that researches and edits your local documents with cited answers
projects.summary: SurfSense is a desktop app, a NotebookLM-style agent that indexes your files on local disk and answers with citations. It can also create and edit PDF, Word, Excel and PowerPoint files, always writing a new copy, and generate podcasts, mind maps, flashcards and quizzes. It works with any OpenAI-compatible API or a local model and needs no account.
strengths: Index stays on local disk; no account needed
Edits PDF, Word, Excel and PowerPoint as new copies, originals untouched
Works with any OpenAI-compatible API or a local model
Installers for Windows x64, macOS Apple Silicon and Linux (AppImage, deb)
weaknesses: Hosted web app is being sunset; export workspaces before 18 October 2026
Word and PowerPoint to PDF needs LibreOffice, enabled in Settings
Image generation needs an image model; none is chosen by default
OCR covers only Latin, Chinese and Japanese script

projects.name: WeKnora
projects.tagline: Enterprise knowledge base combining RAG Q&A, agents and generated wikis
projects.summary: WeKnora turns team documents into knowledge bases with three modes: cited RAG answers, an agent that runs multi-step tasks with skills in Docker, E2B or Cube sandboxes, and auto-generated wiki pages with a knowledge graph. It syncs from Feishu, Confluence, GitLab, Notion and RSS, answers in WeCom, Slack and Telegram, and exposes an MCP server. Deploy with Docker Compose, Helm or one Lite binary on SQLite.
strengths: 29 built-in model vendors including OpenAI, DeepSeek, Qwen, Gemini, LiteLLM and Ollama
Lite single binary with SQLite and in-memory queue for low-resource hosts
Workspace RBAC with four roles, per-resource ownership and audit log
Per-workspace MCP endpoints with own token, scope and rate limit
weaknesses: Many integrations target the Chinese ecosystem (WeChat, Feishu, DingTalk, Yuque)
Sandbox commands run as root since v0.8.2
Maintainers advise against exposing it to the public internet
Desktop app has no published installer; hardware requirements live in external docs

projects.name: quivr
projects.tagline: Go engine that ingests content streams for hybrid search and keyword alerts
projects.summary: Quivr V2 is a Go service that durably ingests text and documents, indexes them in Weaviate for lexical, semantic and hybrid search, and runs saved queries as subscriptions that produce matches and signed webhooks. State lives in PostgreSQL and S3-compatible storage, with Temporal for orchestration and plugins for connectors and alert rules. The README marks it as evaluation stage with a v0 API that may change.
strengths: Idempotent writes and immutable Versions; search index can be rebuilt from PostgreSQL and S3
Hybrid search rehydrates and re-authorizes every hit; outages return errors, not empty results
Subscriptions with keyword, meaning and described alerts, plus signed webhook delivery
Prometheus metrics, optional OpenTelemetry tracing, and documented worker autoscaling and upgrades
weaknesses: README says evaluation stage, API v0 may change, not for production
Heavy stack: PostgreSQL, Temporal, Weaviate, S3 storage and a TEI embedding server
No chat or LLM answer generation described; differs from the earlier Quivr assistant
Described alerts send article text to TypeSafe; last release is February 2025

projects.name: pageindex
projects.tagline: Vectorless RAG that builds a tree index of a PDF and lets an LLM search it
projects.summary: PageIndex builds a hierarchical tree index from each PDF, then has an LLM reason through that tree to find the relevant sections, with no vector database or chunking. The Python SDK (pip install pageindex) runs locally with your own LLM key for text-based PDFs, or points at PageIndex Cloud for OCR, scanned documents and block-level citations. The README reports 98.7% on FinanceBench and about $0.001 per page to index locally.
strengths: No vector DB or chunking; retrieval is traceable to page-level references
Local mode indexes a 1,000-page PDF for roughly a dollar, per README benchmarks
Same client switches between local and Cloud by changing the index argument
Documents integration with OpenAI Agents SDK and Claude Agent SDK
weaknesses: Local mode handles text-based PDFs only; no OCR or image understanding
MCP server, metadata, folders and File System for large corpora are Cloud-only
Each query needs LLM reasoning calls, so accuracy and cost depend on the chat model
Needs an external LLM API key; local-model support is not stated in the README

projects.name: PrivateGPT
projects.tagline: Anthropic-style API layer for private RAG on local inference servers
projects.summary: PrivateGPT 1.0 is an API server shaped like the Anthropic Messages API, adding file ingestion, retrieval with citations, web search, code execution, MCP and direct database or CSV querying. It runs no models; it calls any OpenAI-compatible server (Ollama, llama.cpp, vLLM) through OPENAI_API_BASE. A workbench UI at /ui on port 8080 exists for testing; the API is the product.
strengths: Anthropic Messages API shape, so Claude Code, Claude Desktop and Office add-ins can target it
Backend-agnostic: any OpenAI-compatible inference server via OPENAI_API_BASE
Built-in database and CSV querying, no extra tool server needed
Installs with brew or uv tool install; Docker also documented
weaknesses: Runs no models; a separate inference server and embedding server are required
No prompt caching and no OAuth or organizations
Skills support is marked basic; structured output depends on the backend
RBAC, LDAP, connectors and audit logs exist only in the commercial Zylon platform

projects.name: PipesHub
projects.tagline: Permission-aware search and agent context over Slack, Drive, GitHub and more
projects.summary: PipesHub indexes content from 50+ business systems such as Slack, Google Drive, GitHub, Microsoft 365 and Notion, then answers questions with block-level citations filtered by each user's source-system permissions. It stores data in a Neo4j or ArangoDB graph, Qdrant vectors and MongoDB, and exposes the same context to agents through a no-code builder, an MCP server and Python, TypeScript and Go SDKs. Any LLM provider works, including local models via Ollama.
strengths: Answers cite specific blocks in source documents and respect per-user source permissions
50+ connectors with real-time and scheduled indexing
Exposes context via an MCP server and Python, TypeScript and Go SDKs
Interactive installer generates secrets and .env; Kubernetes with HA defaults supported
weaknesses: Multi-service stack: Neo4j or ArangoDB, Qdrant, MongoDB, Redis, optionally Kafka
Audio and video are stored but not indexed yet
Hosted PipesHub Cloud is only a waitlist; self-hosting is the only option today
Personalized search and PageRank-augmented relevance are not yet shipped

projects.name: graphrag
projects.tagline: Pipeline that builds knowledge graphs from text for LLM question answering
projects.summary: GraphRAG is a Python data pipeline from Microsoft Research that uses an LLM to extract structured data from unstructured text and form a knowledge graph. That graph is used to build context for question answering over private data. It runs from a command line (`graphrag init`, indexing, querying) with configurable settings and tunable prompts. The project is in maintenance mode: bug fixes and dependency updates only.
strengths: Backed by a published paper (arXiv 2404.16130) and a Microsoft Research blog post
Prompt tuning guide for adapting extraction to your own data
Installable from PyPI, with a CLI quickstart and hosted documentation
MIT license, with a release in September 2026
weaknesses: Maintenance mode: no new features and no new PRs accepted
Indexing can be expensive in LLM calls; README advises starting small
Not an officially supported Microsoft offering; code is a demonstration
Config format changes between versions require re-running `graphrag init --force`

projects.name: paperless-gpt
projects.tagline: LLM-based OCR, titles, tags and document links for paperless-ngx
projects.summary: paperless-gpt is a companion service for paperless-ngx that calls an LLM to generate titles, tags, correspondents, created dates and custom fields, with a web UI for manual review or automatic processing. It can also replace the stock OCR with LLM OCR (OpenAI, Ollama, Mistral, Anthropic), Google Document AI, Azure Document Intelligence or a Docling server, and can produce searchable PDFs. It fills Document Link fields by extracting invoice, contract or case references and doing an exact lookup.
strengths: Supports OpenAI, Mistral, Anthropic, Azure OpenAI and local Ollama models
Four OCR backends: LLM, Google Document AI, Azure, Docling
Document linking uses exact whole-word lookup and leaves ambiguous matches unlinked
Prompts and per-document-type workflows editable in the web UI
weaknesses: No built-in authentication; needs a reverse proxy or VPN
Works only with paperless-ngx, tested on 2.20.x and 3.0 beta
Hosted LLM and OCR options send document content to third parties
PDF_REPLACE mode deletes the original document after upload

projects.name: serviette
projects.tagline: RAG and enterprise search app templates built on the Pathway live data framework
projects.summary: A set of Python templates for RAG and document search that stay in sync with sources such as local files, Google Drive, SharePoint, S3, Kafka and PostgreSQL. Indexing is built in (usearch for vectors, Tantivy for full-text), so no separate vector database, cache or API framework is needed. Templates include basic Q&A, multimodal GPT-4o parsing, unstructured-to-SQL, Adaptive RAG, a private Mistral/Ollama variant and video RAG, each exposing an HTTP API.
strengths: Index updates on additions, deletions and edits in connected sources
Built-in vector, hybrid and full-text indexes, no external vector DB
Private template runs locally with Mistral and Ollama
Optional Streamlit UI for quick demos
weaknesses: Tied to the Pathway framework, so pipeline code is not portable
Several templates call hosted APIs (GPT-4o, TwelveLabs)
No tagged releases
README gives no RAM or hardware requirements

projects.name: Docling Serve
projects.tagline: Docling document conversion as an HTTP API with playground UI
projects.summary: Docling Serve wraps the Docling document converter in a FastAPI service: POST a URL or file to /v1/convert/source and get structured text back, with OpenAPI docs at /docs and a playground UI at /ui on port 5001. Container images cover CPU (4.4 GB), CUDA 12.8 (11.4 GB) and CUDA 13.0 on amd64 and arm64; a ROCm image builds locally. Suited to RAG pipelines that need a document-to-text service.
strengths: Single container with API, OpenAPI docs and a playground UI
Stable v1 API after migration
CPU and CUDA 12.8/13.0 images for amd64 and arm64
Converts from HTTP sources or uploads in one call
weaknesses: Images are large: 4.4 GB CPU, 8.7 GB base amd64, 11.4 GB CUDA
CUDA images carry no latest tag; pin explicit versions
ROCm image is not published; build it yourself
Slim images without bundled weights are only announced

projects.name: DB-GPT
projects.tagline: Agentic data assistant that writes SQL and code over your databases
projects.summary: DB-GPT connects to databases, CSV and Excel files, warehouses and knowledge bases, then plans tasks, writes SQL and Python, runs them in sandboxes and produces charts, dashboards and HTML reports. It installs with pip install dbgpt-app (Python 3.10+) plus a setup wizard and serves a web UI on port 5670, with OpenAI-compatible, DashScope, Moonshot and MiniMax profiles and local models via vLLM or llama.cpp.
strengths: NL-to-SQL plus Python analysis with sandboxed execution
Outputs charts, dashboards and HTML reports, not only answers
Skills importable from GitHub for repeatable analysis workflows
Local serving via vLLM or llama.cpp and a Text2SQL fine-tuning hub
weaknesses: Recommended install pipes a remote script into bash
Docs and community largely on dbgpt.cn; Docker and GPU setup only there
Text2SQL fine-tune list stops at older models such as LLaMA-2 and ChatGLM2
Default pip install bundles ChromaDB only; other vector stores need extras

projects.name: DeepWiki-Open
projects.tagline: Generates browsable wikis and diagrams for GitHub, GitLab and Bitbucket repos
projects.summary: DeepWiki-Open takes a repository URL from GitHub, GitLab or Bitbucket, analyzes the code structure, generates documentation and diagrams, organizes them into a navigable wiki and builds a codemap for guided tours. The repo ships a Dockerfile and compose file. The README now points to a 2.0 release called Grok Wiki distributed as a download from grok-wiki.com and no longer documents configuration.
strengths: Works with GitHub, GitLab and Bitbucket repositories
Produces diagrams and codemap guided tours, not only prose
Dockerfile and docker-compose in the repo; MIT license
weaknesses: README no longer documents setup, ports or supported model providers
2.0 is pushed as a separate download at grok-wiki.com
No hardware guidance; single-maintainer project

projects.name: Morphik
projects.tagline: Multimodal retrieval engine for visually rich PDFs, images and video
projects.summary: Morphik Core is a retrieval engine for visually rich documents: it embeds page images with ColPali so charts, tables and diagrams are searchable through one endpoint covering PDFs, images and video, and extracts metadata such as bounding boxes and labels by rules. It is used via a Python SDK, REST API, MCP or the Console web UI. Self-hosting is documented separately and offered with limited support.
strengths: ColPali retrieval over page images instead of extracted text
One search endpoint for images, PDFs and video
Rule-based metadata extraction with bounding boxes and classification
Python SDK, REST API and MCP access
weaknesses: BSL 1.1: commercial use above US $2,000 per month revenue needs a paid key
Self-hosted deployments get no full support from the maintainers
README centers on the hosted dev.morphik.ai service, not self-hosting
Parent company now focuses on back-office AI workers; Core is a side product

projects.name: Kotaemon
projects.tagline: Gradio RAG UI with hybrid retrieval, citations and multi-user login
projects.summary: Kotaemon is a Gradio web app for question answering over uploaded documents, with hybrid full-text plus vector retrieval, reranking, citations shown in an in-browser PDF viewer and ReAct or ReWOO agents. It supports OpenAI, Azure, Cohere, Groq, Ollama and GGUF via llama-cpp-python, with Elasticsearch, LanceDB, ChromaDB, Milvus or Qdrant storage. Docker images come in lite, full and ollama variants on port 7860.
strengths: Hybrid retriever plus reranking by default, with low-relevance warnings
Citations open in a PDF viewer with highlights and relevance scores
Multi-user login with private and public collections
GraphRAG options: nano-graphrag, LightRAG or Microsoft GraphRAG
weaknesses: Default login is admin/admin
GraphRAG extras cause hnswlib version conflicts that need manual pip fixes
Only PDF, HTML, MHTML and XLSX without the larger full image
Last commit 2026-05-30; MS GraphRAG indexing works only with OpenAI or Ollama

projects.name: Paperless-AI
projects.tagline: Auto-tags Paperless-ngx documents and adds RAG chat over the archive
projects.summary: Paperless-AI watches a Paperless-ngx instance, sends new documents to OpenAI, Ollama, DeepSeek, OpenRouter, Gemini or other OpenAI-compatible backends and writes back title, tags, document type and correspondent. It adds RAG chat over the whole archive and a manual review page at /manual. The maintainer has declared the repo unmaintained pending a rewrite.
strengths: Assigns title, tags, document type and correspondent on new documents automatically
RAG chat answers questions across the full Paperless archive
Rules limit which documents get processed; manual mode for sensitive files
Ollama support keeps processing local
weaknesses: Repo marked not maintained; rewrite and future uncertain
Container must be restarted after first setup to build the RAG index
No port, hardware or env var details in the README; see the wiki
Paperless-ngx is adding native AI, which may supersede it

projects.name: langchain-chatchat
projects.tagline: Local knowledge-base Q&A and agent app built on LangChain
projects.summary: Chatchat answers questions over your own files by splitting, embedding and retrieving text, then passing the top-k matches to an LLM. It does not load models itself: it connects to Xinference, Ollama, LocalAI, FastChat or One API through OpenAI-compatible endpoints. It ships a FastAPI backend and a Streamlit WebUI, and installs with pip install langchain-chatchat.
strengths: Connects to Xinference, Ollama, LocalAI, FastChat and One API via OpenAI-compatible endpoints
FAISS by default, other vector stores selectable in kb_settings.yaml
YAML config reloads without restart (0.3.1+)
Also has agent tools, search-engine chat, database chat and image chat with qwen-vl-chat
weaknesses: Needs a separate model server running before the knowledge base can be built
Last release 2024-07-12; README Docker image tag is dated 2024-08-29
Default bind is 127.0.0.1; remote access requires editing basic_settings.yaml
0.3.x differs a lot from 0.2.x; migration is not guaranteed to work

projects.name: Morphic
projects.tagline: Search engine that answers with citations and renders rich inline components
projects.summary: Morphic runs web searches and returns cited answers, rendering inline components such as images, grids and headings from a streamed JSON spec instead of plain markdown. It offers Quick and Adaptive search modes and works with OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Ollama, Vercel AI Gateway and OpenAI-compatible models. Docker Compose brings up PostgreSQL, Redis, SearXNG and the app, with chat history stored in PostgreSQL.
strengths: Compose file bundles PostgreSQL, Redis and SearXNG, so no search API key is required
Supports Tavily, SearXNG, Brave and Exa as search providers
Model selector detects providers, including local Ollama and OpenAI-compatible endpoints
Auth is switchable between Supabase, better-auth and none
weaknesses: Full stack needs four containers: PostgreSQL, Redis, SearXNG and the app
Supabase is the default auth provider unless ENABLE_AUTH=false or AUTH_PROVIDER is set
Needs at least one AI provider API key or a local Ollama setup
README gives no RAM or hardware requirements

projects.name: GPT Researcher
projects.tagline: Research agent that writes cited reports from web and local documents
projects.summary: GPT Researcher splits a query into research questions with a planner agent, scrapes sources in parallel, filters the context and writes a cited report. It works over web search (Tavily by default) and local files such as PDF, CSV, Excel, Markdown, PowerPoint and Word. It runs as a FastAPI server with a static or NextJS frontend, or as the gpt-researcher pip package.
strengths: Covers both web research and local documents (PDF, CSV, Excel, Markdown, PowerPoint, Word)
Usable as a pip package, a FastAPI server with two frontends, or via Docker Compose
Supports MCP data sources, recursive deep research, and LangGraph or AG2 multi-agent workflows
Context filter falls back to local BM25 keyword ranking when no TypeSafe key is set
weaknesses: Needs an LLM API key and a search API key (OpenAI and Tavily in the README examples)
Default Jev context filter requires a TypeSafe API key and a hosted call
Deep research is quoted at about 5 minutes and $0.4 per run with o3-mini
README calls it experimental and provided as-is, with no warranty

projects.name: Local Deep Research
projects.tagline: Agentic research assistant with local LLMs, SearXNG and encrypted libraries
projects.summary: Runs multi-step research across the web, academic engines and your own documents using Ollama or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, with a LangGraph agent that picks engines adaptively and writes cited reports. Each user gets an AES-256 SQLCipher database, and egress scopes limit which engines and providers a run may use. Web UI on port 5000 via Docker, Compose or pip, for privacy-focused researchers.
strengths: Reports about 95% SimpleQA fully local on one RTX 3090 with Qwen3.6-27B
Per-user SQLCipher databases; keys derived from the password, never stored
No telemetry; Docker images signed with Cosign, with SLSA provenance and SBOMs
Downloaded sources build a searchable, embedded personal library
weaknesses: Needs Ollama (or an LLM endpoint) and SearXNG running separately
Private or localhost engine URLs are blocked unless an operator env var allows them
Requires an AVX-capable x86-64 CPU; older CPUs crash with Illegal instruction
docker run --network host only works on native Linux; Docker Desktop needs Compose

projects.name: Vane
projects.tagline: Self-hosted answer engine with cited sources over SearXNG
projects.summary: Next.js answer engine (formerly Perplexica) that runs searches through a bundled SearXNG instance, then answers with citations using Ollama, OpenAI-compatible servers, OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini or Groq models. Offers Speed, Balanced and Quality modes, web, discussion and academic sources, image and video search, file uploads and a search API. One container on port 3000; a slim image uses your own SearXNG.
strengths: Single Docker image bundles SearXNG; no search API key needed
Local models via Ollama or any OpenAI-compatible server, plus cloud providers
Browser search-engine shortcut via /?q=%s and a REST search API
Slim image works with an existing SearXNG (JSON format and Wolfram Alpha enabled)
weaknesses: No authentication yet; listed as an upcoming feature
Own-SearXNG setups must enable JSON output and Wolfram Alpha or searches fail
Tavily and Exa search backends are marked coming soon
Ollama on Linux must listen on 0.0.0.0 for the container to reach it

projects.name: MAESTRO
projects.tagline: Multi-agent research platform that writes long reports from documents and web
projects.summary: Planning, Research, Reflection and Writing agents run research missions over uploaded PDF, Word and Markdown documents and web search, producing long reports with visible agent steps. Retrieval uses BGE-M3 embeddings in PostgreSQL with pgvector; any OpenAI-compatible API, including Azure OpenAI, can serve the models. Docker Compose stack on http://localhost with CPU and NVIDIA variants.
strengths: Mission checkpoints allow pause, resume and writing-phase recovery
Local embeddings (BGE-M3) and pgvector; local LLMs via OpenAI-compatible API
Search providers: Tavily, LinkUp, Jina and SearXNG
CPU-only compose file plus automatic NVIDIA GPU detection
weaknesses: 16 GB RAM minimum (32 GB recommended) and 30 GB disk
Alpha (v0.1.10-alpha); last commit April 2026
Dual-licensed AGPLv3 or commercial; proprietary use needs a paid license
First startup takes 5 to 10 minutes while models download

projects.name: voicestudio
projects.tagline: Desktop app for voice cloning, dubbing and dictation with local speech models
projects.summary: VoiceStudio is an Electron desktop app with a Python backend for voice cloning, text-described voice design, timed video dubbing, dictation, transcription and audiobook creation. The default engine is k2-fsa/OmniVoice, with other engines selectable and models installed through a Model Manager. It also exposes a local API and an MCP server for agents.
strengths: Covers cloning, voice design, dubbing, dictation and audiobooks in one app
CUDA on NVIDIA, Metal on Apple Silicon, and a CPU fallback
Local API and MCP for agents, plus watch folders and reusable recipes
Installers for macOS, Windows and Linux, plus Docker
weaknesses: AGPL-3.0 app licence; model weights and voices carry separate terms
CPU-only use is slower; CPU PyTorch setup needs about 5 GB disk
Intel Mac runs the UI only and needs a remote backend
Windows on ARM is experimental and CPU only

projects.name: whisper.cpp
projects.tagline: C/C++ port of OpenAI Whisper for local speech-to-text transcription
projects.summary: whisper.cpp runs OpenAI's Whisper speech recognition models in plain C/C++ on top of the ggml library, with a C-style API in whisper.h and a whisper-cli example for transcribing 16-bit WAV files. It runs on CPU or can offload to Metal, Core ML, CUDA, Vulkan, ROCm, OpenVINO, Ascend CANN, Moore Threads MUSA and AMD Ryzen AI NPUs. It supports integer quantization and voice activity detection, and builds for desktop, mobile, WebAssembly and Docker.
strengths: No dependencies in core; zero memory allocations at runtime
Wide backend coverage: Metal, Core ML, CUDA, Vulkan, ROCm, OpenVINO, CANN, MUSA, NPU
Runs on iOS, Android, WebAssembly, Raspberry Pi, and Java bindings exist
Q5_0-style integer quantization shrinks models; base model needs about 388 MB RAM
weaknesses: whisper-cli accepts only 16-bit WAV unless built with optional FFmpeg support
Core ML, OpenVINO and VitisAI encoders need a separate Python conversion step
Models must be in ggml format; downloaded via script, not bundled
Library and CLI only; no built-in web UI or multi-user features

projects.name: Voicebox
projects.tagline: Local voice studio for cloning, TTS, dictation and agent speech
projects.summary: Desktop app (Tauri) and Docker service that clones voices from a short sample and generates speech through eight TTS engines, including Qwen3-TTS, Chatterbox and Kokoro, in 23 languages. Adds Whisper dictation with a global hotkey, a REST API on port 17493 and an MCP server so coding agents can speak in a cloned voice. For individuals who want ElevenLabs-style voice I/O on their own machine.
strengths: Eight switchable TTS engines; Chatterbox Multilingual covers 23 languages
REST API plus HTTP and stdio MCP server for Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf
Runs on MLX, CUDA, ROCm, DirectML, Intel Arc or CPU
Auto-chunking with crossfade handles scripts up to 50,000 characters
weaknesses: No prebuilt Linux binaries; build from source or use Docker
Only Chatterbox Turbo honors tags like [laugh]; other engines read them aloud
Dictation auto-paste and the permission flow are macOS-specific
Docker deployment gets one line in the README; details are in external docs

projects.name: Speech-to-Speech
projects.tagline: Modular voice-agent pipeline exposed through the OpenAI Realtime API
projects.summary: Runs a VAD, STT, LLM and TTS cascade, with each stage in its own thread and every backend swappable by CLI flag. It serves the core OpenAI Realtime event set over WebSocket and WebRTC, so existing Realtime clients can point at it. Defaults are Parakeet TDT for speech recognition and Qwen3-TTS for speech output, with the LLM running locally or through any OpenAI-compatible endpoint.
strengths: Implements core OpenAI Realtime events over WebSocket and WebRTC, so client swaps are easy
Fully local on Apple Silicon (MLX) or NVIDIA CUDA, with no API key needed
Many interchangeable STT and TTS backends, including Whisper, Kokoro, Pocket TTS and OmniVoice
Apache-2.0, installable from PyPI, with a packaged microphone client
weaknesses: Qwen3-TTS GGML wheel targets CUDA 12.8 and glibc 2.39 by default
Fully local NVIDIA setup budgets about 24 GB VRAM; the README calls this an estimate
Only the core Realtime event set is implemented, not the full API
Some extras conflict, e.g. DeepFilterNet needs numpy<2 while Pocket TTS needs numpy>=2

projects.name: Kokoro-FastAPI
projects.tagline: OpenAI-compatible text-to-speech server for the Kokoro-82M model
projects.summary: Wraps the Kokoro-82M TTS model in a FastAPI server that implements the OpenAI /v1/audio/speech endpoint, with streaming and output in mp3, wav, opus, flac, aac or pcm. It adds weighted voice mixing, inline multi-speaker tags, pause/rate/pronunciation tokens, per-word timestamps and phoneme endpoints. Prebuilt images cover CPU, NVIDIA CUDA and experimental AMD ROCm; Apple Silicon runs natively via uv.
strengths: Drop-in for the OpenAI speech API; works with the stock OpenAI Python client
Prebuilt CPU and CUDA images for amd64 and arm64 with models baked in
Voice mixing, aliases, inline speaker tags and timestamped captions
Bundled web UI at /web and Swagger docs at /docs
weaknesses: Tied to one model, Kokoro-82M; no other TTS engines
ROCm support is experimental and amd64 only
Apple Silicon GPU (MPS) needs a native uv run, not Docker
Voice tuning from a reference clip is off by default, English only, and approximate

projects.name: meetily
projects.tagline: Desktop app that records, transcribes and summarizes meetings locally
projects.summary: Meetily is a Tauri desktop app with a Rust backend and a Next.js frontend. It captures microphone and system audio, transcribes on-device with Whisper or Parakeet models, and generates summaries through Ollama, Claude, Groq, OpenRouter, or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Installers exist for Windows and macOS; Linux requires a source build.
strengths: Transcription runs on-device with Whisper or Parakeet; no cloud needed
Summary provider is selectable, including local Ollama or a custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint
Records microphone and system audio together with mixing
Imports existing audio files and re-transcribes with another model or language (beta)
weaknesses: No prebuilt Linux package; must build from source
Speaker diarization is not in the community edition; planned for PRO
Custom summary templates, advanced exports and auto-join are PRO-only
Standard Windows installer uses Vulkan; CUDA needs a source build

projects.name: Pocket TTS
projects.tagline: CPU-only text-to-speech model with voice cloning and streaming
projects.summary: Pocket TTS is a 100M-parameter text-to-speech model from Kyutai that runs on CPU, using about 2 cores. It ships a Python API and a CLI with generate, serve and export-voice commands, and clones voices from a wav sample. It supports seven languages, streams audio with roughly 200ms to first chunk, and reaches about 6x real-time on a MacBook Air M4.
strengths: Runs on 2 CPU cores, no GPU required; about 6x real-time on a MacBook Air M4
Voice cloning from a wav file, with export to safetensors for fast reloads
Seven languages (en, fr, de, pt, it, es, nl) plus community models such as Czech, Hindi and Korean
Installs with pip or uvx; serve command gives a local web UI and HTTP endpoint
weaknesses: GPU use is unofficial: no device argument on load_model, and serve and Docker image are CPU-only
Cannot insert silence in the text input to create pauses
Default Linux pip install pulls CUDA PyTorch (~3 GB) unless the CPU index is passed
Pre-made voice embeddings do not work with community-trained models

projects.name: OpenReader
projects.tagline: Reads EPUB, PDF and DOCX aloud with synced word highlighting
projects.summary: Next.js server that narrates EPUB, PDF, TXT, Markdown and DOCX files with synchronized read-along, generating audio ahead of playback through a self-hosted OpenAI-compatible TTS server (Kokoro-FastAPI, KittenTTS-FastAPI, Orpheus-FastAPI) or OpenAI, Replicate and DeepInfra. PDF layout is parsed with PP-DocLayoutV3 and words aligned with ONNX Whisper in a NATS JetStream worker. Exports M4B or MP3 audiobooks.
strengths: Layout-aware PDF parsing and word-by-word highlighting
Audio cache reused across seeks, reloads and audiobook export
Storage on embedded SeaweedFS or S3; SQLite or Postgres; built-in auth
amd64 and arm64 Docker images with automatic startup migrations
weaknesses: Needs a separate TTS server or cloud TTS API; nothing is bundled
Word alignment and DOCX conversion run in a NATS JetStream compute worker you deploy
Setup details (ports, env vars) are only in the external docs

projects.name: voxcpm
projects.tagline: 2B-parameter text-to-speech model with voice design and voice cloning
projects.summary: VoxCPM2 is a 2B-parameter, tokenizer-free TTS model built on a MiniCPM-4 backbone. It synthesizes 48kHz speech in 30 languages, creates voices from a text description, and clones voices from a short reference clip, optionally with a transcript for continuation cloning. It ships as a pip package with a Python API, CLI and web demo, and can be served through Nano-vLLM, vLLM-Omni or llama.cpp-omni.
strengths: Voice design from a text description, no reference audio needed
30 languages plus nine Chinese dialects, no language tag required
Apache-2.0 weights and code, with SFT and LoRA fine-tuning support
Serving options: Nano-vLLM, vLLM-Omni (OpenAI-style endpoint), GGUF on llama.cpp-omni
weaknesses: Standard install requires CUDA 12.0 or newer and PyTorch 2.5.0 or newer
Python support limited to 3.10 through 3.12
RTF about 0.3 on RTX 4090 with the default PyTorch path
llama.cpp-omni path is slower: RTF about 1.76 on Apple M4 Pro

projects.name: IndexTTS
projects.tagline: Zero-shot TTS with emotion, speed and pronunciation control
projects.summary: Clones a voice from one reference clip and synthesizes speech in Chinese, English, Japanese, Spanish and Arabic (IndexTTS-2.5). Emotion comes from a second reference clip, an 8-value vector or the text itself; speed is set by duration_factor (0.5x to 2.0x) and pronunciation by inline Pinyin, CMU phonemes or Kana. Ships a Gradio web UI on port 7860 and a Python API; a vLLM recipe covers production serving.
strengths: Emotion control via reference audio, an 8-value vector or a text description
Inline pronunciation overrides: Pinyin, CMU phonemes and Japanese Kana
BF16 inference with optional DeepSpeed and compiled CUDA kernels
Published vLLM recipe for production deployment
weaknesses: No Dockerfile or compose file; install is uv plus CUDA Toolkit 12.8 or newer
Model weights (IndexTTS-2.5, IndexTTS-2) are separate multi-GB downloads
Five languages only; no streaming API is documented in the README
License is non-standard (GitHub reports NOASSERTION); check terms before commercial use

projects.name: GPT-SoVITS
projects.tagline: Few-shot voice cloning and TTS with a training web UI
projects.summary: Clones a voice from a 5-second sample (zero-shot) or fine-tunes GPT and SoVITS models on about one minute of audio, then synthesizes speech in Chinese, English, Japanese, Korean and Cantonese. The Gradio web UI bundles dataset tools: UVR5 vocal separation, slicing, ASR and label proofreading. Aimed at hobbyists and studios building custom voices locally.
strengths: Zero-shot cloning from 5 s of audio; few-shot fine-tune from about 1 minute
Cross-lingual synthesis across zh, en, ja, ko and yue
Compose services for CUDA 12.6 and 12.8, plus Lite images without ASR and UVR5 models
Reported RTF 0.028 on an RTX 4060 Ti for v2 ProPlus
weaknesses: Pretrained weights are separate downloads from Hugging Face or ModelScope
Docker images lag the code; README says to pull latest source before using them
Training on Apple Silicon GPUs gives lower quality; macOS falls back to CPU
Five model generations (v1 to v5) with different tradeoffs to choose between

projects.name: vibevoice
projects.tagline: Microsoft's open speech models for long-form ASR and streaming TTS
projects.summary: VibeVoice is a family of speech models built on 7.5 Hz continuous tokenizers and next-token diffusion. The ASR models transcribe up to 60 minutes of audio in one pass with speaker, timestamp and hotword support, plus a streaming variant and a CPU build. The TTS side includes a 0.5B real-time model with about 300 ms first-audio latency. The 1.5B long-form TTS code was removed from the repository after misuse.
strengths: ASR handles 60 minutes in one pass, returning speaker, timestamps and text together
Streaming ASR, vLLM serving and ASR fine-tuning code are documented
BitNet CPU build shrinks ASR from 4.62 GB to 1.58 GB, RTF under 1 on 3+ threads
Realtime TTS is 0.5B with about 300 ms first audible latency and streaming text input
weaknesses: VibeVoice-TTS code was removed; the 1.5B TTS model is listed as Disabled
README says it is for research only, not recommended for commercial use
Realtime TTS long-form output is about 10 minutes
README gives no RAM or VRAM requirements for the full models

projects.name: F5-TTS
projects.tagline: Flow-matching TTS and voice cloning with Gradio and CLI
projects.summary: Synthesizes speech from a reference clip and its transcript using the F5-TTS diffusion transformer (plus an E2 TTS reproduction). Runs as a pip package with a Gradio web app on port 7860, a CLI and a Docker image; a Triton and TensorRT-LLM runtime reaches RTF 0.039 on an L20 GPU. Suited to researchers and builders who want a trainable open TTS model.
strengths: pip install f5-tts; Gradio UI, CLI and a ghcr.io Docker image
Triton plus TensorRT-LLM runtime: 253 ms average latency at concurrency 2 on L20
Training and fine-tuning via Accelerate or a Gradio finetune app
PyTorch install documented for NVIDIA, AMD ROCm, Intel XPU and Apple Silicon
weaknesses: Pretrained weights are CC-BY-NC (Emilia data); code is MIT, models are non-commercial
Reference audio needs a transcript, or an ASR model runs and uses more GPU memory
No compose file in the repo; the README's compose example assumes an NVIDIA GPU
Base checkpoints cover Chinese and English; other languages need community models

projects.name: Speakr
projects.tagline: Self-hosted audio transcription with speaker labels, summaries and chat over recordings
projects.summary: Speakr is a Flask and Vue web app that records or imports audio, transcribes it through a configurable engine (WhisperX, OpenAI, Mistral Voxtral, AssemblyAI and others), and generates summaries, titles and action items. It adds per-recording chat, semantic search across the library, tags with custom prompts, groups, OIDC SSO, a REST API and signed webhooks. Storage is SQLite by default or PostgreSQL.
strengths: Many ASR connectors, auto-detected from config, including fully self-hosted WhisperX and VibeVoice
Speaker diarization and cross-recording voice profiles with the WhisperX backend
Multi-user with OIDC SSO, groups, sharing, retention policies and per-user usage budgets
REST API with Swagger UI and HMAC-signed webhooks for n8n, Zapier or Make
weaknesses: Voice profiles and WhisperX diarization need a separate ASR container with a GPU
Version is 0.10.14-alpha; the release is labeled alpha
Summaries and chat need an external LLM API key, or a local model such as Ollama
Full image is about 4.4GB; lite image falls back to basic text search

projects.name: whisper
projects.tagline: Multilingual speech recognition and translation model with Python and CLI interfaces
projects.summary: Whisper is a Transformer sequence-to-sequence model for speech recognition, speech-to-English translation, and language identification. It ships as a pip package with a `whisper` command and a Python API, in six sizes from tiny (39M parameters) to large (1550M), plus a turbo variant. Code and weights are MIT licensed.
strengths: Six model sizes (39M to 1550M parameters) trade accuracy for speed and VRAM
Handles transcription, translation to English and language identification in one model
Simple `whisper audio.mp3 --model turbo` CLI and a short Python API
Code and weights both under MIT license
weaknesses: No built-in HTTP server or web UI; you wrap it yourself
The turbo model is not trained for translation and returns the original language
Requires ffmpeg, and possibly Rust for tiktoken if no prebuilt wheel exists
Accuracy varies widely by language; large model needs about 10 GB VRAM

projects.name: WhisperLive
projects.tagline: Near-real-time Whisper transcription server over WebSocket
projects.summary: Streams audio from a microphone, file, RTSP or HLS source to a server on port 9090 and returns partial and committed Whisper transcripts over WebSocket, with an optional OpenAI-compatible REST endpoint. Backends are faster-whisper (CPU, CUDA, ROCm), TensorRT-LLM and OpenVINO; extras include word timestamps, hotwords, pyannote diarization and translation. For teams embedding live captions or dictation.
strengths: Three inference backends: faster-whisper, TensorRT-LLM, OpenVINO (Intel iGPU/dGPU)
Prebuilt GPU, CPU and OpenVINO Docker images; ROCm Dockerfile
Word-level timestamps, hotword boosting and batched multi-client inference
Chrome, Firefox and iOS clients; Python streaming client for raw PCM
weaknesses: Defaults allow 4 clients and 600 s per connection; must be tuned for more
Without a fixed model, a new Whisper instance loads per client connection
TensorRT backend requires building engines and is recommended only via Docker
Diarization needs the optional pyannote.audio dependency

projects.name: chattts
projects.tagline: Text-to-speech model for dialogue, with laughter and pause control
projects.summary: ChatTTS is a Python text-to-speech model trained for conversational speech in English and Chinese, with multi-speaker support and token-level control over laughter, pauses and interjections. It installs from PyPI, outputs 24 kHz audio, and ships a simple WebUI and command-line example. The released weights are a 40,000-hour pretrained model without SFT, licensed CC BY-NC 4.0 for research use.
strengths: Token-level prosody control: [laugh], [uv_break], [lbreak], plus sentence-level oral/laugh/break prompts
Random speaker sampling with saved embeddings for timbre recovery
Streaming generation and zero-shot inference code are included
Runs with about 4 GB GPU memory for a 30-second clip; RTF around 0.3 on a 4090
weaknesses: Model weights are CC BY-NC 4.0, academic use only; no commercial use
Only English and Chinese supported; English is described as experimental
Autoregressive output is unstable: speaker drift and quality vary between samples
Repo is the algorithm and examples; no packaged server or Docker image

projects.name: Speaches
projects.tagline: OpenAI-compatible STT and TTS server with faster-whisper, Kokoro and Piper
projects.summary: Exposes OpenAI-style audio endpoints: streaming transcription and translation through faster-whisper, speech generation through Kokoro and Piper, plus a Realtime API and audio chat completions. Models load on first request and unload after inactivity, on CPU or GPU, via Docker Compose. For self-hosters who want one container that OpenAI SDKs can talk to for speech.
strengths: Works with any OpenAI SDK; transcription streams over SSE
Dynamic model loading and unloading after idle time
Supports the Realtime API and audio-in, audio-out chat completions
CPU and GPU Docker images with Compose files
weaknesses: Last commit April 2026; development has slowed
README is short; port, env vars and limits live only in the external docs
TTS limited to Kokoro and Piper models
Streaming transcription demo is marked TODO in the README

projects.name: MoneyPrinterTurbo
projects.tagline: Turns a topic into a short video with script, footage, voiceover and subtitles
projects.summary: MoneyPrinterTurbo takes a topic or keywords and produces a finished short video. An LLM writes the script, footage comes from Pexels, Pixabay, Coverr, local files or text-to-video APIs, and TTS, subtitles and background music are added before the final render. It offers a WebUI, HTTP API, CLI and an agent skill, and outputs 9:16, 16:9 or 1:1.
strengths: Covers the whole pipeline: script, footage, voiceover, subtitles, music and render
Many LLM providers, including OpenAI, Claude, Gemini, DeepSeek, and Ollama for local models
Edge TTS needs no API key; Pexels and Pixabay stock footage are free
WebUI, API, CLI and batch generation; Docker and compose files included
weaknesses: Most LLMs and stock sources need API keys; AI video generation uses paid services
Footage relevance depends on keyword matching against stock libraries
README is dominated by sponsor and promotional sections
Web port and Docker setup details are not visible in the provided README

projects.name: ComfyUI
projects.tagline: Node-graph engine for diffusion image, video, audio and 3D models
projects.summary: Builds generation pipelines as a visual node graph and runs them locally for image (SD 1.5, SDXL, SD3.5, Flux.1 and Flux.2, Qwen Image), video (Wan 2.x, LTX-Video, HunyuanVideo), audio (ACE-Step, Stable Audio) and 3D (Hunyuan3D) models, with a local API and an App Mode that exposes a workflow as a simple UI. Runs on NVIDIA, AMD, Intel, Apple Silicon and Ascend. For professionals who want control over every parameter.
strengths: Asynchronous weight streaming runs large models on 4 GB VRAM plus 8 GB RAM
Workflows saved as JSON and recoverable from generated media metadata
Runs fully offline; --offline disables the paid API nodes
Loads checkpoints, separate diffusion models, VAEs, text encoders, LoRAs, ControlNets
weaknesses: Commits outside stable tags can break many custom nodes; stable releases roughly biweekly
GPL-3.0 license constrains embedding in proprietary products
NVIDIA 20-series and newer require PyTorch built with CUDA 13.0 or above
Paid partner and API nodes stay on unless --offline or --disable-partner-nodes is set

projects.name: open-generative-ai
projects.tagline: Image, video and lip-sync studio UI that calls MuAPI, with optional local engines
projects.summary: A JavaScript app, available as a web build and an Electron desktop app, that front-ends hosted image, video, audio and lip-sync models through the MuAPI service. The desktop app can also run local inference: a bundled stable-diffusion.cpp engine for SD 1.5, SDXL and Z-Image, or a user-installed Wan2GP for video models and Flux. Most generation depends on a MuAPI account, and the README promotes a paid white-label offering.
strengths: Desktop app can run sd.cpp locally with Metal, CUDA, Vulkan or ROCm, no API key
Wan2GP integration runs video models locally or on a remote GPU box via MCP
Multi-image input accepts up to 14 reference images on compatible edit models
Installers provided for macOS (arm64, x64), Windows and Linux (AppImage, .deb)
weaknesses: Cloud generation requires MuAPI; the 600+/200+ model claims run through that paid service
Local inference is desktop-only; the hosted web version always uses cloud APIs
Installers are unsigned, so macOS Gatekeeper and Windows SmartScreen need manual bypass
Z-Image needs about 16 GB RAM and is reported to hang 8 GB Macs

projects.name: InvokeAI
projects.tagline: Canvas-first web UI for Stable Diffusion and Flux image generation
projects.summary: Local web server and React UI for image generation with a Unified Canvas (inpainting, outpainting, brushes), a node-based workflow editor and a boards gallery with per-image metadata. Loads SD 1.5 to SD 3.5, SDXL, Flux.1 and Flux.2 variants, Qwen Image, Z-Image, Krea 2 and CogView 4 in ckpt, diffusers and some GGUF formats; Nano Banana, GPT Image and Wan are API-only. For artists iterating on images.
strengths: Unified Canvas with in/outpainting, brush tools and SAM/SAM2 segmentation
Broad model list including Flux.2 Dev and Klein, SD 3.5 Large, Qwen Image Edit
Apache-2.0 license; serves as the base for commercial products
Dedicated launcher application handles install and updates
weaknesses: No Dockerfile or compose file at the repo root; install goes through the Launcher
README lists features only; ports, hardware needs and env vars are in external docs
Video generation (Wan) is API-only, not local
Nano Banana and GPT Image require third-party API access

projects.name: AI Toolkit
projects.tagline: Fine-tuning suite for image, video and audio diffusion models, with GUI and CLI
projects.summary: AI Toolkit trains LoRA and LoKr adapters for diffusion models, covering FLUX.1, FLUX.2, Qwen-Image, Wan 2.1/2.2, LTX-2 and SDXL, plus audio models like ACE-Step 1.5. Jobs are defined in YAML and run with `python run.py`, or started and monitored from a web UI on port 8675. The UI can be protected with an AI_TOOLKIT_AUTH token, and training can also run on Modal or RunPod.
strengths: Supports a wide range of image, edit, video and audio models in one tool
Same YAML configs work from the CLI or the web UI
Training resumes from the last checkpoint after interruption
Layer targeting via only_if_contains and ignore_if_contains, plus LoKr support
weaknesses: Manual install requires an Nvidia GPU; Mac support is experimental
Install manager is labeled experimental by the author
Dataset images must be jpg, jpeg or png; webp has known issues
Ctrl+C during a checkpoint save can corrupt that checkpoint

projects.name: biniou
projects.tagline: Gradio web UI for local text, image, audio, video and 3D generation
projects.summary: biniou is a self-hosted Gradio web UI that bundles many generative modules: a llama-cpp chatbot for GGUF models, Whisper speech-to-text, Stable Diffusion and Flux image generation, MusicGen audio, video and Shap-E 3D. It runs on CPU from 8GB RAM, with optional CUDA or experimental ROCm, and can work offline once models are downloaded. Installers exist for several Linux distributions and Windows, plus a Dockerfile.
strengths: Covers text, image, audio, video and 3D generation in one UI
Runs on CPU only, from 8GB RAM; CUDA and experimental ROCm optional
One-click installers for several Linux distros and Windows; Dockerfile provided
Modules can pass outputs to each other; generation settings saved as metadata
weaknesses: AMD64 only; macOS support is experimental and untested
Many modules need 16GB+ RAM; about 200GB of disk with default models
Python 3.10 or 3.11 required; Windows install adds Visual Studio Build tools
Chatbot has no stated agents, tools or document chat; the README lists only chat and multimodal

projects.name: faceswap
projects.tagline: Python tool that trains neural models to swap faces in images and video
projects.summary: FaceSwap is a Python program with three stages run through `faceswap.py`: extract faces from photos or video frames, train a model on two sets of faces, and convert source media with the trained model. It ships a Tkinter-style GUI (`faceswap.py gui`) alongside the CLI, and includes models such as Villain and Phaze-A. It runs on Windows, Linux and macOS, with CUDA GPUs recommended and some AMD support via ROCm on Linux.
strengths: Covers the full workflow: extract, train and convert, via CLI or GUI
Multiple model architectures named in the README, including Villain, Phaze-A, DFL-H128 and DFaker
Runs on Windows, Linux and macOS; AMD GPUs supported via ROCm on Linux
Existing models can be reused to shorten training on new faces
weaknesses: Training requires a modern CUDA GPU for acceptable speed; exact VRAM needs are unknown
No Docker or compose setup in the repo
Setup problems are directed to the forum and Discord, not GitHub issues
Manual workflow: gathering and curating face data is left to the user

projects.name: Kohya's GUI
projects.tagline: Gradio GUI and CLI for Kohya diffusion training scripts
projects.summary: Wraps kohya-ss/sd-scripts in a Gradio UI that builds the training command for LoRA, LoHa, LoKr, DreamBooth, full fine-tuning, Textual Inversion and LECO concept erasure. Base models include SD 1.5/2.x, SDXL, SD3, Flux.1, Lumina Image 2.0, Anima and HunyuanImage-2.1. Installs with uv or pip, runs headless over SSH on a port such as 7860, ships Docker, Runpod and Colab paths, and suits people training their own LoRAs.
strengths: Covers LoRA, LoHa, LoKr, DreamBooth, fine-tune, Textual Inversion and LECO
GUI shell runs offline after install; no CDN assets or analytics by default
config.toml presets default paths and Gradio allowed_paths
Sample image generation during training with per-prompt seed, size and CFG flags
weaknesses: Needs a GPU-equipped machine; README gives no VRAM figures per model
Without --headless, OS file dialogs on the server can block training over SSH
macOS support is community-maintained and may vary
Last commit July 2026; sd-scripts submodule pinned to v0.11.1

projects.name: Pixelle-Video
projects.tagline: Topic-to-short-video pipeline built on ComfyUI workflows and TTS
projects.summary: Turns a topic into a short video: an LLM (GPT, Qwen, DeepSeek, Ollama) writes the script, ComfyUI or RunningHub workflows or direct APIs (DashScope Wan, GPT Image, Seedream, Seedance, Kling) produce per-sentence images or clips, Edge-TTS or Index-TTS voices it, and HTML templates lay out each frame. Streamlit UI on port 8501, plus digital-human and image-to-video modules. For creators already running ComfyUI.
strengths: Zero-cost path: Ollama for the LLM plus a local ComfyUI instance
Image, video, TTS and VLM steps are swappable ComfyUI workflows or direct APIs
Custom HTML templates for static, image-backed and video-backed layouts
Windows one-click package bundles Python, uv and ffmpeg
weaknesses: README and docs are Chinese first; an English README exists separately
Local image or video generation needs a running ComfyUI server (default port 8188)
Last commit June 2026; update log stops at 2026-06-01
Heavy local footprint: ComfyUI plus diffusion and TTS models

projects.name: FluxGym
projects.tagline: Web UI for training FLUX LoRAs on 12 to 20 GB GPUs
projects.summary: Gradio front end (forked from AI-Toolkit) over Kohya sd-scripts that trains FLUX.1-dev LoRAs with 12 GB, 16 GB or 20 GB VRAM presets. Upload images, caption them with a trigger word and press start; base models download automatically and an Advanced tab exposes every sd-scripts flag. Runs via Pinokio, a manual venv or docker compose on port 7860, for hobbyists training FLUX LoRAs on consumer GPUs.
strengths: VRAM presets for 12, 16 and 20 GB cards
Advanced tab is generated from sd-scripts flags, so every option is reachable
Sample images every N steps with fixed seeds to watch the LoRA evolve
Publish trained LoRAs to Hugging Face from the UI
weaknesses: FLUX.1 only (dev, dev2pro, schnell); schnell results are called not recommended
Manual install clones sd-scripts separately and uses PyTorch nightly builds
Docker image must be built locally; PUID and PGID must match your user
Last commit July 2026

projects.name: upscayl
projects.tagline: Desktop image upscaler using Real-ESRGAN models over Vulkan
projects.summary: Upscayl is an Electron desktop app that enlarges low-resolution images with Real-ESRGAN-based models run through an NCNN Vulkan backend.
