It provides graph pipelines such as SmartScraperGraph, SearchGraph and ScriptCreatorGraph, with multi-page variants that call the LLM in parallel. It works with OpenAI, Groq, Azure, Gemini, MiniMax or local models through Ollama, and uses Playwright to fetch pages.
strengths: Prompt plus URL returns a JSON dict; no per-site selectors to write
Runs against local Ollama models or hosted APIs by changing the llm config
Several pipelines: single page, multi-page, search results, Python script generation
Multi-page graph variants run LLM calls in parallel
weaknesses: Proxies, anti-bot handling and scaling are left to the user in the open-source version
Needs a separate `playwright install` step to fetch page content
Anonymous telemetry is on by default; opt out via SCRAPEGRAPHAI_TELEMETRY_ENABLED=false
README steers users to the paid managed API for crawl and monitor features

projects.name: marker
projects.tagline: Converts PDFs, Office files and images to markdown, JSON, HTML or chunks
projects.summary: Marker is a Python library and CLI that converts PDF, image, PPTX, DOCX, XLSX, HTML and EPUB files to markdown, JSON, HTML or chunks, handling tables, equations, code blocks and image extraction. Layout, OCR and table recognition run through a surya VLM served by a local vLLM (Docker, NVIDIA) or llama.cpp server that starts automatically. An optional --use_llm mode adds Gemini, Claude, OpenAI-compatible, Azure, Vertex, OpenRouter or Ollama for higher accuracy.
strengths: Outputs markdown, JSON block tree with polygons, HTML or chunks, plus extracted images
Fast mode uses text layer and rf-detr layout on CPU; --disable_ocr starts no server
Batch CLI with worker pool, --skip_existing and chunk sharding across multiple machines
Reports 76.0% on olmocr-bench in balanced mode, ahead of MinerU and docling
weaknesses: Model weights use a modified OpenRAIL-M license; commercial use above startup limits needs a paid license
Balanced mode needs Docker with NVIDIA Container Toolkit, or llama.cpp on CPU and Apple Silicon
Non-PDF formats require the marker-pdf[full] extra install
README says the hosted Chandra model is more accurate than Marker

projects.name: pdfmathtranslate
projects.tagline: Translates scientific PDFs while keeping formulas, figures and layout intact
projects.summary: pdf2zh translates scientific PDFs and writes a translated-only and a bilingual (dual) PDF, preserving formulas, charts, table of contents and annotations. It runs as a CLI, a Gradio web UI on port 7860, a Python or HTTP API, or an MCP server, and calls a configurable translation service (Google by default). Layout detection uses a DocLayout-YOLO ONNX model, with optional OCR and an --ultrafast mode.
strengths: Outputs both translated-only and side-by-side bilingual PDFs from one command
Many interfaces: CLI, Gradio GUI, Docker, Python API, HTTP API, MCP stdio/SSE
Selectable translation backends via -s, with Google as the default
Optional OCR for scanned pages and --ultrafast mode for native-text PDFs
weaknesses: Python limited to 3.11 to 3.12
OCR is experimental and targets white-background scans; handwriting may fail
Last release is 2025-07-11; v2 work lives in a separate PDFMathTranslate-next repo
--ultrafast is CLI fast mode only and is weaker on complex tables or formulas

projects.name: paddleocr
projects.tagline: OCR and document parsing toolkit that outputs Markdown and JSON from PDFs and images
projects.summary: PaddleOCR runs text recognition (PP-OCRv6) and document parsing (PaddleOCR-VL 0.9B VLM, PP-StructureV3) on PDFs and images, producing Markdown or JSON for RAG pipelines. It runs on CPU, NVIDIA GPU, Kunlunxin XPU and other accelerators, with ONNX, OpenVINO, TensorRT and Transformers backends. Models are on HuggingFace and ModelScope.
strengths: Three PP-OCRv6 tiers (1.5M, 7.7M, 34.5M params) cover edge to server
One PP-OCRv6 model handles 50 languages; PaddleOCR-VL covers 111
Outputs Markdown, JSON and DOCX; PP-StructureV3 returns table cell and text coordinates
Multiple inference backends: Paddle, Transformers, ONNX Runtime, OpenVINO, TensorRT, plus C++ deployment
weaknesses: Depends on the PaddlePaddle framework; GPU installs need matching CUDA builds
Benchmark claims such as 96.3% on OmniDocBench are the authors' own
Python support listed as 3.8 to 3.12 only
Several pipelines and models, so choosing between PP-OCR, VL and StructureV3 takes reading

projects.name: opendataloader-pdf
projects.tagline: PDF parser that outputs Markdown, JSON with bounding boxes, and Tagged PDF
projects.summary: Java-based PDF parser with Python, Node.js and Java SDKs. The default local mode extracts text, tables, headings and images with bounding boxes and XY-Cut++ reading order. An optional hybrid mode runs a Docling-based backend server for OCR, complex tables, LaTeX formulas and chart descriptions. It can also auto-tag untagged PDFs into Tagged PDF; PDF/UA export is an enterprise add-on.
strengths: Local mode is deterministic and runs without GPU; README lists 0.015 s/page
JSON output includes bounding boxes for every element, useful for source citations
Hybrid mode adds OCR (several engines), borderless tables, LaTeX formulas and picture descriptions
Auto-tags untagged PDFs to Tagged PDF under Apache-2.0
weaknesses: Requires Java 11+ on the host in addition to Python or Node
Each convert() call spawns a JVM, so calls must be batched
PDF/UA-1/2 export and the accessibility studio are enterprise-only
Hybrid mode needs a separate backend server; no Word, Excel or PowerPoint support

projects.name: Jina Reader
projects.tagline: Converts any URL or search query into LLM-friendly markdown
projects.summary: Open-source branch of the service behind r.jina.ai and s.jina.ai: fetches a page with headless Chrome or curl-impersonate, parses PDFs and Office files, and returns markdown, text, HTML, screenshots or JSON controlled by request headers (engine, timeout, token limits). The ghcr.io image bundles Chrome, LibreOffice and CJK fonts, serves HTTP/1.1 on 8081 and h2c on 8080, and runs stateless or with S3-compatible caching.
strengths: Prebuilt image with Chrome, LibreOffice and CJK fonts; stateless by default
Fine-grained headers: x-respond-timing, x-max-tokens, x-token-budget, x-target-selector
Optional VLM captions for images without alt text
Semantic markdown chunking by heading or block level
weaknesses: Hosted proxy pool, rate limiting and MongoDB storage layer are not in the OSS branch
Needs non-redistributable assets (MaxMind GeoLite2, Source Han Sans) fetched at build
Last commit May 2026; the SaaS resync was April 2026
Default h2c port 8080 needs --http2-prior-knowledge from curl; use 8081 otherwise

projects.name: easyocr
projects.tagline: Python OCR library for text detection and recognition in 80+ languages
projects.summary: EasyOCR is a Python package that detects text regions with the CRAFT model and reads them with a CRNN recognizer, built on PyTorch. It returns bounding boxes, text and confidence scores from file paths, URLs, bytes or numpy arrays, and also has a CLI. Model weights download automatically per language, and it runs on GPU or CPU.
strengths: Two-line Python API returns boxes, text and confidence from paths, URLs, bytes or arrays
80+ languages across Latin, Chinese, Arabic, Devanagari and Cyrillic scripts
CPU-only mode via gpu=False; also ships a command-line tool
Documents custom recognition and CRAFT detection model training
weaknesses: Not every language combination works together in one Reader; English works with all
Handwritten text support is listed as upcoming, not available
Last release 1.7.2 was September 2024
Issues older than 6 months are auto-closed; maintainers cite limited resources

projects.name: ai-engineering-from-scratch
projects.tagline: Hands-on curriculum for building AI systems from math to agents
projects.summary: A course of 528 lessons across 20 phases, covering math foundations, ML fundamentals, LLM engineering, agents, tools and protocols, and production infrastructure. Lessons are runnable code in Python, TypeScript, Rust and Julia, with three graded projects: retrieval evaluation, agent trace debugging and a tool-call firewall. It can be followed on the website, from a local clone, or through tutor skills installed into a coding agent.
strengths: Lessons ship runnable code; the first ones need only python3 and no extra dependencies
Three staged projects with local graders (project_test.py --strict) and reference solutions
Tutor skills install via npx skills and save progress to LEARNING.md
Code in Python, TypeScript, Rust and Julia; README translated into 30+ languages
weaknesses: 528 lessons is a large scope; total study time is not stated in the visible README
Project starters fail by design until you implement the stages
Tutor skills need Node.js, npx and a skill-capable coding agent host
GPU and RAM needs for later phases are not stated in the visible README

projects.name: generative-ai-for-beginners
projects.tagline: 21-lesson course on building generative AI apps in Python and TypeScript
projects.summary: A Microsoft Cloud Advocates course of 21 lessons, each a README with a short video and code samples, split into "Learn" concept lessons and "Build" lessons. Topics include prompt engineering, text and chat apps, embeddings search, image generation, function calling, RAG, agents, fine-tuning, and small, Mistral and Meta models. Code targets Azure OpenAI, OpenAI API, Microsoft Foundry Models or Foundry Local.
strengths: Build lessons ship code in both Python and TypeScript where possible
Covers RAG, function calling, agents, fine-tuning and security in one sequence
Lessons are independent, so you can start at any number
MIT license; translations into 50+ languages
weaknesses: Samples assume Azure OpenAI, OpenAI API or Foundry access, which may need paid accounts
Several lessons list video as coming soon
Cloning includes 50+ translations, so sparse checkout is needed for a small download
GitHub Models lessons are tied to a service retiring end of July 2026

projects.name: llms-from-scratch
projects.tagline: Code for the book on building a GPT-style LLM in PyTorch
projects.summary: Official code for the Manning book "Build a Large Language Model (From Scratch)". Notebooks and scripts implement tokenization, attention, a GPT model, pretraining, classification finetuning, instruction finetuning and LoRA in plain PyTorch, without external LLM libraries. Bonus folders add from-scratch Llama 3.2, Qwen3, Gemma 3, Olmo 3, KV cache, MoE and DPO.
strengths: Main chapter code runs on a conventional laptop and uses a GPU automatically if present
Plain PyTorch with no external LLM libraries, so every component is readable
Bonus material covers KV cache, GQA, MoE, DPO and several model architectures
Exercise solutions, a companion video course and CI tests on Linux, Windows and macOS
weaknesses: Tied to a print book; contributions extending main chapter code are not accepted
Produces a small educational model, not a production-grade LLM
License is reported as NOASSERTION; the README states no license terms
Video course and quiz PDF are hosted by the publisher, not in the repo

projects.name: hello-agents
projects.tagline: Chinese-language course on building LLM agents from scratch
projects.summary: A 16-chapter Chinese tutorial from Datawhale covering agent fundamentals, ReAct, Plan-and-Solve and Reflection, low-code platforms (Coze, Dify, n8n) and frameworks (AutoGen, AgentScope, LangGraph). Later chapters build a custom framework on the OpenAI API and cover memory, RAG, context engineering, MCP/A2A/ANP, Agentic-RL (SFT to GRPO) and evaluation. Chapter code is in the repo's code folder.
strengths: 16 chapters from theory to capstone, with runnable code in the code folder
Includes an Agentic-RL chapter going from SFT to GRPO training
Builds a custom agent framework on the OpenAI API, not only framework usage
Free online reading and PDF download, plus extra chapters on interviews and skills
weaknesses: Written in Chinese; an English README is linked separately
License is CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, which bars commercial use
Assumes basic Python and experience calling an LLM API
Hardware and model requirements for the exercises are unknown

projects.name: ml-for-beginners
projects.tagline: 12-week, 26-lesson classic machine learning course using Scikit-learn
projects.summary: A Microsoft Cloud Advocates curriculum covering classic machine learning (regression, classification, clustering, NLP) with Scikit-learn, deliberately excluding deep learning. Each lesson has pre- and post-lecture quizzes, a written lesson, a solution, a challenge and an assignment, built around datasets from different world regions. Lessons are in Python, with R Markdown versions for many.
strengths: Project-based lessons with solutions in /solution folders and quizzes for each lesson
Many lessons also provided in R as .rmd files
Translated into 50+ languages via automated GitHub Action
MIT license; can run in GitHub Codespaces without local Python setup
weaknesses: Covers classic ML only; deep learning is in a separate curriculum
Not about LLMs or generative AI
Clone is large because of 50+ translations unless sparse checkout is used
Per-lesson dependencies must be installed manually

projects.name: ai-agents-for-beginners
projects.tagline: 18-lesson course on building AI agents with Microsoft Agent Framework
projects.summary: A Microsoft course of 18 lessons on building AI agents, each with a written README, a short video for most lessons, and Python code samples in Jupyter notebooks. Topics include tool use, agentic RAG, planning, multi-agent patterns, memory, MCP/A2A/NLWeb protocols, computer-use agents, local agents and securing agents. Samples use Microsoft Agent Framework with Microsoft Foundry Agent Service V2, and some also support OpenAI-compatible providers such as MiniMax.
strengths: Each lesson is standalone, so you can start at any topic
Covers design patterns plus MCP, A2A, NLWeb, memory and deployment
Text, short videos and runnable Python samples per lesson
50+ language translations kept current by GitHub Action
weaknesses: Samples are built around Microsoft Agent Framework and Foundry, which need an Azure account
Some later lessons have no video
Cloning pulls large translation folders unless sparse checkout is used
Alternative provider support is only partial, per the README

projects.name: ai-for-beginners
projects.tagline: 12-week, 24-lesson AI curriculum with PyTorch and TensorFlow notebooks
projects.summary: A Microsoft course that teaches AI from symbolic and expert systems through neural networks, computer vision, NLP, genetic algorithms, reinforcement learning, multi-agent systems and ethics. Lessons pair text with Jupyter notebooks in PyTorch and/or TensorFlow/Keras, and several have labs. Translations into 50+ languages are generated by a GitHub Action.
strengths: Covers symbolic AI, deep learning, vision, NLP, RL and ethics in one ordered path
Most lessons have both PyTorch and TensorFlow/Keras notebooks
Labs for many lessons, plus a Binder badge to run notebooks in the browser
50+ automated translations; MIT license
weaknesses: NLP stops at transformers/BERT and GPT basics; README admits it lags the state of the art
Excludes classic ML, cloud services and deep math; it points to other courses
Not every lesson has a lab; some notebooks are TensorFlow-only or PyTorch-only
Translations inflate clone size; sparse checkout is needed to skip them

projects.name: ai-agent-book
projects.tagline: Open book on AI agent design, with 109 runnable companion experiments
projects.summary: A Chinese-language book, "Understanding AI Agents in Depth", with 10 chapters built on the formula Agent = LLM + context + tools. It covers context engineering, memory and RAG, tools and MCP, coding agents, interaction, evaluation, post-training and multi-agent collaboration. The repo holds the book sources, PDF and EPUB builds in 15 languages, and 109 Python experiments installed per chapter with uv or pip.
strengths: 109 companion experiments mapped to chapters, installable per chapter via uv.lock or pip
PDF and EPUB in 15 languages, plus an online reader
Covers evaluation and post-training (SFT/RL), not only prompting and tool use
External repos are pinned to commit SHAs for reproducible setups
weaknesses: Original text is Chinese; the other 14 translations are community-made and may lag
README says experiment code is agent-generated and not read line by line by the author
Installing or cloning does not mean an experiment was run; status is tracked separately
Most experiments need provider API keys; some need CUDA, browsers or external repos

projects.name: openai-cookbook
projects.tagline: Example notebooks and guides for building with the OpenAI API
projects.summary: Collection of runnable Jupyter notebooks and guides showing common tasks with the OpenAI API. Most examples are in Python, and the README says the concepts apply to other languages. Running them requires an OpenAI account and an API key set as OPENAI_API_KEY. The guides are also browsable at cookbook.openai.com.
strengths: Maintained by OpenAI, so examples track the official API
Runnable notebooks; API key is read from OPENAI_API_KEY or a .env file
Also browsable as a site at cookbook.openai.com
MIT license
weaknesses: Requires an OpenAI account and API key; examples do not target local models
Most examples are Python only
README does not list topics, versions or per-notebook dependencies
No tagged releases

projects.name: claude-cookbooks
projects.tagline: Jupyter notebooks of copy-able Claude API recipes in Python
projects.summary: Anthropic's collection of runnable notebooks and guides for building with the Claude API. Recipes cover classification, RAG, summarization, tool use, vision, sub-agents, JSON mode, prompt caching, evals and cost optimization. Examples are mainly Python, and a Claude API key is required.
strengths: Covers tool use, RAG, vision, prompt caching and evals with runnable notebooks
Maintained by Anthropic, so examples target the Claude API directly
MIT licensed, snippets can be copied into your own projects
Includes third-party recipes such as Pinecone, Voyage AI embeddings and Wikipedia search
weaknesses: Requires a Claude API key; examples do not run on local models
Examples are primarily Python; other languages must be adapted
Recipe links in the README point to the older anthropic-cookbook repo path
Reference snippets, not an installable library or application

projects.name: rag_techniques
projects.tagline: Jupyter notebooks demonstrating 42 RAG techniques, from basic to advanced
projects.summary: A collection of 42 runnable Jupyter notebooks, each implementing one RAG technique such as basic RAG, CSV RAG, reliable RAG, chunk-size selection, proposition chunking and query transformations. Notebooks open on GitHub or Colab, and some have companion videos. The README also promotes the author's course, book and newsletter.
strengths: 42 notebooks, each covering a single technique, grouped from foundational to advanced
Colab badges let notebooks run without local setup
Covers evaluation notebooks (End-to-End RAG Evaluation, Open-RAG-Eval) as well as retrieval methods
Updated recently; last commit 2026-09-21
weaknesses: Teaching notebooks, not a library or deployable RAG system
README is heavy with course, book and newsletter promotion
License is not detected (NOASSERTION), so reuse terms are unclear
Required API keys and package versions are not stated in the visible README

projects.name: self-llm
projects.tagline: Chinese-language tutorials for deploying and fine-tuning open LLMs on Linux
projects.summary: A Datawhale tutorial collection, written mostly in Chinese, that walks through environment setup, local deployment and fine-tuning for 50+ open LLMs such as Qwen, GLM, InternLM, Llama and DeepSeek. Content is Jupyter notebooks and Markdown covering CLI calls, online demos, LangChain integration, LoRA, P-Tuning and distributed full fine-tuning. It also has sections for AMD ROCm, Ascend NPU and Apple M hardware.
strengths: Covers 50+ open models, each with its own deployment and fine-tuning tutorial
Hardware tracks for AMD ROCm, Ascend NPU and Apple M, beyond NVIDIA
Worked examples such as LoRA fine-tuning on Zhen Huan dialogue and an advanced-math model
Active community project with many named contributors and Apache-2.0 license
weaknesses: Main README and tutorials are in Chinese; English README is a separate file
Linux-centered; the MetaX section is marked Coming Soon
Tutorials are tied to specific model versions and may age as models change
No installable package or app; notebooks only, with no stated hardware requirements

projects.name: ai-engineering-hub
projects.tagline: Collection of 93 runnable AI tutorials on RAG, agents, MCP and fine-tuning
projects.summary: A monorepo of about 93 example projects, mostly Jupyter notebooks and small apps, grouped into beginner, intermediate and advanced tiers. Topics include local OCR, RAG with LlamaIndex and Ollama, CrewAI and AutoGen agents, MCP servers, voice agents, model comparisons and fine-tuning with Unsloth. Each project sits in its own folder with its own dependencies.
strengths: Roughly 93 self-contained projects, each in its own folder
Wide coverage: RAG, agents, MCP, voice, OCR, fine-tuning, evaluation
Projects sorted into beginner, intermediate and advanced tiers
MIT license; many examples run locally with Ollama and open models
weaknesses: No single install; each project has its own dependencies and setup
Many examples need third-party API keys such as Firecrawl or AssemblyAI
Example code, not a maintained library; 'production-ready' claim is unsupported
No releases or versioning; project freshness and quality vary

projects.name: happy-llm
projects.tagline: Chinese-language course on LLM theory and building a LLaMA2-style model
projects.summary: Happy-LLM is a Datawhale course in eight chapters, written in Chinese with an English README. It covers NLP basics, the Transformer and pretrained model families, then implements LLaMA2 in PyTorch, trains a tokenizer, and runs pretraining, SFT, LoRA/QLoRA, RAG, agents and GRPO-based agentic RL. Two 215M checkpoints from chapter 5 are published on ModelScope.
strengths: Covers Transformer basics through pretraining, SFT, LoRA/QLoRA, RAG, agents and agentic RL
Publishes 215M base and SFT checkpoints plus a ModelScope studio to try them
Free PDF and companion slides available from the releases page
Dependencies split per chapter, with an environment preparation guide
weaknesses: Main content is in Chinese; only the README has an English version
Content license is CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, which restricts commercial use
Hardware requirements are not stated in the README, only in a separate doc
Extra Chapter blog section is marked as in progress

projects.name: llm-course
projects.tagline: Free LLM course with roadmaps and Colab notebooks for fine-tuning and quantization
projects.summary: A three-part course covering LLM fundamentals (math, Python, neural networks), an LLM Scientist track on building models, and an LLM Engineer track on building and deploying applications. It pairs roadmaps and curated links with Colab notebooks and articles on fine-tuning (Unsloth, ORPO, DPO, QLoRA, Axolotl), quantization (GGUF, GPTQ, EXL2) and model merging with MergeKit.
strengths: Runnable Colab notebooks for fine-tuning, quantization and merging, most with a linked article
Separate tracks for fundamentals, model building and application deployment
Quantization notebooks cover GGUF, GPTQ, EXL2, AWQ and HQQ
Free to use under Apache-2.0
weaknesses: Mostly curated external links rather than self-contained lessons
Several notebooks target older models such as Llama 2 and Mistral-7b
Notebooks run on Google Colab or RunPod, not a documented local setup
Coverage reflects one author's selection of topics and resources

projects.name: made-with-ml
projects.tagline: MLOps course with code for training, tuning, and serving a text classifier
projects.summary: A course repository that walks through building a text classifier end to end: a Jupyter notebook, then refactored Python scripts for training, tuning, evaluation, inference and serving. It uses Ray for distributed workloads, MLflow for experiment tracking, pytest for code, data and model tests, and Anyscale Jobs and Services for production deployment.
strengths: Covers the full path: notebook, scripts, tests, MLflow tracking, Ray Serve, CI/CD
Runs on a laptop without a GPU, with configurable worker counts
Separate pytest suites for code, data and trained models
Plain Python scripts with documented CLI arguments for each workload
weaknesses: Production section depends on Anyscale (account, CLI token, S3 upload paths)
Example task is a small text classifier, not an LLM application
Setup is built around Ray; other stacks need adaptation
README promotes a paid live cohort

projects.name: annotated_deep_learning_paper_implementations
projects.tagline: Annotated PyTorch implementations of deep learning papers with side-by-side notes
projects.summary: A collection of short PyTorch implementations of neural network architectures and algorithms, each rendered on nn.labml.ai as code beside explanatory notes. It covers transformers (including Flash Attention in Triton, RoPE, ALiBi), LoRA, diffusion models, GANs, reinforcement learning, optimizers, normalization layers and more. Installable as the labml-nn pip package.
strengths: Broad coverage: transformers, diffusion, GANs, RL, optimizers, normalization, LoRA, GNNs, CFR
Each implementation has side-by-side code and explanation on a hosted website
Compact PyTorch code that is readable for studying the original papers
MIT license; install with pip install labml-nn
weaknesses: Written for study, not as an optimized production library
No release tags; versioning is only via the pip package
Many entries cover older papers; recent architectures are sparse
README gives no hardware requirements beyond GPU notes for the GPT-NeoX examples

projects.name: hands-on-large-language-models
projects.tagline: Companion notebooks for the O'Reilly book Hands-On Large Language Models
projects.summary: Code for every example in the book by Jay Alammar and Maarten Grootendorst, as one Jupyter notebook per chapter. Chapters cover tokens and embeddings, transformer internals, classification, clustering, prompt engineering, semantic search and RAG, multimodal models, and fine-tuning. Notebooks were built and tested on Google Colab with a free 16GB T4 GPU.
strengths: One notebook per chapter (12), each with an Open in Colab link
Covers embeddings, RAG, multimodal models and fine-tuning of BERT and generation models
Tested mainly on free Colab T4 16GB, so no local GPU is required
Bonus folder links to visual guides on Mamba, quantization and mixture of experts
weaknesses: Explanatory text and figures are in the paid book, not in the repo
Local setup is only a quick-start guide; results may differ by OS and versions
No tagged releases; README states no pinned package versions
Not a library or tool, only teaching code
